A detail most people miss: 
solana:dog1viwbb2vWDpER5FrJ4YFG6gq6XuyFohUe9TXN65u does not live in a contract. Each balance sits inside ordinary Bitcoin UTXOs. A transfer is just a tiny OP_RETURN “runestone” attached to a normal Bitcoin transaction. That is why there is no admin key, no upgrade path, and no mint button. The etching in block 840,000 created the full 100 billion supply in one shot and closed minting forever.

挺有感触的。

过去这些年，单币万倍、DeFi Summer、铭文时代……大起大落，基本也都经历过了。

年轻一点的时候，总觉得人生里最重要的是抓住那几个“大机会”。

后来慢慢发现，不管你某段时间赚了多少钱，经历过多大的起伏，最后还是会回到“你这个人本来的常态”。

所以现在我反而越来越觉得，真正值得长期经营的，是自己的常态。

有事情持续做，有自己一点点搭起来的东西；该工作的时候认真工作，该休息的时候休息。

好好吃饭，好好睡觉，好好活着。

市场好的时候不觉得自己无所不能，市场差的时候也不觉得人生完了。机会来了认真抓，错过了就继续做下一件该做的事。

所谓平常心，可能不是对赚钱没欲望，而是不再需要靠每天的涨跌、别人的暴富、某一次输赢，来证明自己过得好不好。

牛熊都会过去。

最后留下来的，还是你的身体、生活、判断力，以及那些你日复一日经营出来的东西。

我在上个牛市、上上个牛市的时候，从没有人跟我讲过这个道理，但我现在很想把这段话分享给新人们，算是肺腑之言了：

这个世界上努力的人很多，真正能拿到大结果的人永远只是少数，所以如果你到现在还没有赚到很多钱，也没有抓住所谓的人生大机会，真的不用气馁，更不需要焦虑，因为很多时候真正把人拖垮的，并不是暂时没有结果，而是在一个离金钱很近、所有人都在展示结果的环境里，不知不觉开始拿自己和别人比较，别人赚钱，你觉得自己落后，别人暴富，你觉得自己错过，最后每天接收了大量信息，却只留下了内耗。

越是在这种时候，越要安住其心，把注意力从别人身上收回来，从纷乱的信息里只提取真正对自己有用的东西，然后继续照顾好自己的身体、情绪、判断和节奏。

你要记得，这个世界本来就是你一个人的游戏，别人比你快一点、赚得多一点、暂时站得高一点，其实都和你没有那么大的关系，你真正要做的，只是把自己的这一局继续玩好。独善其身，是这个时代最被低估的能力，也是对抗长期内耗最有效的解药。

祝你在这个牛市玩得愉快，也祝你赚到钱之后，心里依获得平静。Love & Peace From 小毛哥 ❤

text:
Jev 这种分类器不是新东西，从机器学习时代开始，分类就是最基础的一个任务。2019 年那会儿，$NVDA 正经历一波大回调，才3点几美金，我还在实验室对 BERT 进行各种微调，比如给金融文本打标签，输出情绪置信度，而这些本质都是分类任务。再往前推一点，手写数字识别，这个跨越几十年的经典分类任务，从机器学习方法一路贯彻到深度学习网络……同样也创造了无数经典模型。

分类这个经典任务的目标其实根本没变过：问一个问题，拿回一个概率。

Jev 真正改的是门槛。过去你要有一个分类器，得先有标注数据、有 GPU、有一个愿意调参几周甚至几个月的人；现在你写一句 prompt，70ms 拿到一个带校准的概率，十亿 token仅需$42。以前一个分类器是一个项目，现在则只是一次接口调用而已。

不过这也不会彻底消灭垂直领域的分类器。自己的数据训出来的模型，永远有场景。但Jev打开的是另一块市场：那些本来就不值得专门训一个模型的场景，例如模型路由、打标、粗筛、给每条内容打分。

数码相机之于胶片、Canva 之于设计、3D 打印之于开模、vibe coding 之于写代码，都很相似，根本目的并不是简单取代过去某一个专业领域，而是让达成目标的办法变得更加简单、价格低廉、速度更快。

BERT 时代我微调一个情绪分类器要两周，现在我的资讯站每天给上千条内容打分分类，就是一段 prompt + 几秒钟的事情。我并不觉得这叫革命，但速度+成本的数量级下降确实是一个非常惊艳的事情。

quoted_text:
被吹的神乎其神的 Jev，似乎并没有什么卵用。

论价格、论场景，能打得过我们 Qwen3.7-flash 吗？分类、打标签，任劳任怨，最关键的是，输入价 $0.03/M，比你的 $0.042/M 还便宜三成。你说输出免费？分类任务的输出本来就只有几个 token，免了个寂寞。

而且 Qwen 还能顺手把标题、摘要、翻译写了。Jev 一个字都写不出来，同一篇文章得再喂一遍别的模型。

准确率呢？官方自己的数据：Jev 67.8%，对照模型 74.1%。便宜是跟 Fable、GPT-5.6 这一档比出来的，可谁会拿旗舰模型做判断题。

唯一能说说的就是延迟和大批量数据分类了：百毫秒级响应，答案自带置信度。

讲到这里，通用模型的创业故事似乎到头了，专用模型开始出现，还拿到了 4000 万美元种子轮。有了巨额融资就可以投巨多钱做内容分发了，屎也能说成是香的。

author: liujackc
quoted_text:
Thanks for the thoughtful post, and also for paying attention to our indexing work for such a long time.

I do agree with one of the core points here: decentralized indexing with a sustainable incentive model can become an important piece of infrastructure on Bitcoin mainnet.

This is also one of the reasons we’ve spent quite a lot of time on FIP-101 over the past few quarters.

The progress on Fractal has been encouraging. During the first three quarters of this year, we were able to bring the standard indexing service online, make the incentive mechanism operational, and gradually get the system running in a relatively stable way.

That work gives us a much stronger foundation for thinking about how a similar model could work on Bitcoin mainnet. A lot of the difficult questions are no longer purely theoretical for us — we now have real operational experience around indexing nodes, incentives, synchronization, performance, and how different participants interact with the system.

In our current plan, FIP-103 will also bring FB to Bitcoin mainnet as a native asset. This creates a natural possibility for FB to become part of the incentive layer for decentralized indexing on Bitcoin mainnet.

At the same time, I think your point about ORDI is worth discussing.

If there is an appropriate mechanism and a clearly defined role for it, ORDI could potentially become an alternative or complementary incentive under certain conditions. Given its history, liquidity and relationship with the BRC-20 ecosystem, it is understandable why people would naturally think about ORDI in this context.

For me, though, the more fundamental question is not simply which token should be used, but how the incentive model can remain sustainable over a long period of time.

An indexing network needs incentives that can support operators continuously, rather than only creating a short-term bootstrap effect. How that incentive should be structured, where the value comes from, and how different assets might participate are all topics that I think are worth exploring openly.

I’d also be very interested to see more discussion and proposals from the community around this.

There are also some practical differences between Fractal and Bitcoin mainnet that we need to take into account.

Bitcoin mainnet indexing itself generally has a lower workload than Fractal, and the hardware requirements can therefore be somewhat lighter. But our goal is not simply to make the software “able to run.” We want the experience of operating an indexer to be stable, efficient and as smooth as possible.

So before bringing this model further onto Bitcoin mainnet, there is still some engineering work we want to do — around performance, synchronization, deployment, reliability and overall operational experience.

More broadly, multi-protocol indexing on Bitcoin mainnet has always been one of UniSat’s core areas of work.

Over time, we’ve also become increasingly convinced that the indexer itself can be a meaningful product.

It is not only infrastructure underneath products such as UniHexa. A high-quality Bitcoin indexing service can also serve developers, applications, infrastructure providers, institutions and many other participants across the ecosystem.

To make that possible, we still need to keep improving the capability, performance and service quality of the system. The standard we want to reach is not simply “an open-source indexer that works,” but infrastructure that people can confidently build production systems on top of.

And of course, as the community has always expected from us, the indexing service will remain 100% open source.

The standard indexing service currently running on Fractal is already fully open source, and we intend to keep the same principle as we continue this work toward Bitcoin mainnet.

Hopefully, in the not-too-distant future, we can deliver an indexing product on Bitcoin mainnet that meets a genuinely high standard — something that not only UniSat can use, but that the broader Bitcoin ecosystem can build on together.

text:
WSJ: Polymarket CEO Reportedly Told Staff to Keep Growing and Pay a Fine if Regulators Found Out Amid $10M Stolen-Card Fraud Attempt

The Wall Street Journal reported that fraudsters linked stolen debit cards to Polymarket US accounts in February, attempting to move at least $10 million through wagers and withdrawals. text:
We’ve never publicly disclosed this before, and I’d prefer not to disclose the exact amount yet.

The reason we held ORDI in the first place was primarily product-related rather than as an active investment position.

Back in 2023, we were trying to build a fully BRC-20-native swap directly on Bitcoin mainnet, with ORDI serving as the base asset for trading pairs and sats used for fees.

Conceptually, we thought the design was extremely elegant, and technically we believed it was achievable. We put an enormous amount of effort into it and, after a lot of sleepless work, managed to validate the idea with an MVP.

The product itself attracted significant attention. Development was largely completed around September 2023, testing began in October, and we started a limited rollout in November.

The difficult part was that the new operations required broader synchronization and recognition across the BRC-20 ecosystem.

To make that transition possible, we came up with what we called the “black-and-white module” approach, allowing the ecosystem to move toward the new rules gradually rather than forcing an immediate protocol-wide change.

Unfortunately, for a number of reasons, it didn’t work out.

The most fundamental problem was that we greatly underestimated how difficult it would be to introduce a meaningful protocol-level change on Bitcoin mainnet to brc-20 by that time.

In particular, it was extremely difficult to convince others that what we were proposing was not simply something designed for UniSat’s own benefit (these were exactly the kinds of problems that the more you explained the more people don't believe).

I personally put essentially everything I could into trying to move it forward, but we were never able to turn the innovation into sufficiently broad ecosystem consensus.

Looking back, I consider this one of the most serious and costly mistakes we’ve made. 

The damage was not only to the project itself, but also financial, emotional, and reputational.

We had promised the community a product on Bitcoin mainnet and then struggled for a very long time to deliver it. That significantly damaged the trust the community had placed in us.

It was one of those rare “everyone loses” outcomes.

For UniSat, the backlash was enormous. The team and I went through a level of criticism and pressure that was difficult to describe from the outside, and our credibility around BRC-20 was badly damaged.

It also changed our own mindset inevitably and historically.

After that experience, we became much more conservative and cautious around BRC-20 protocol innovation. Something that had once felt natural to experiment with started to feel extremely difficult to touch.

I wrote a more detailed—and deliberately calmer—account of what happened here:

2024.09 PizzaSwap — A Real-World Proof of BRC-20’s Decentralization
https://t.co/dMD1f1wOXI

I wrote it exactly one year later, in September 2024.

By then, the Swap had finally launched on Fractal, where it has continued to operate successfully ever since. It was later renamed InSwap.

At the time, I wanted to leave behind a record of what had actually happened, and deliberately tried to write it in a measured way—not to reopen old arguments, but to give people who genuinely wanted to understand the history a place to start, and also to give some meaning to the fearless experimentation we had attempted a year earlier.

Thank you for taking me back to the memory of the good old days 🌈

It doesn’t matter how good an AI model is if it can’t test its work quickly and reliably. That’s especially hard on mobile.

Traditional approaches rely on screenshots or the accessibility tree, making feedback slow and brittle. Agents can change code in seconds, then spend minutes trying to test it.

text:
One 5-foot, 100-pound man built this with his own hands.

No cranes. No crew.

Edward Leedskalnin spent 28 years (1923–1951) single-handedly quarrying, carving, and moving more than 1,100 tons of limestone in Florida. Some blocks weigh 15–30 tons. He worked mostly at night and called the result Coral Castle.

When people asked how he did it, he always gave the same answer:

“I understand the laws of weight and leverage. I discovered the secrets of the pyramids.”

The actual “secret”?

Simple machines + patience + the right rock.

Oolitic limestone is porous and much lighter than it looks. Leedskalnin used homemade tripods, block-and-tackle systems, winches, levers, and wedges - tools he made from scrap metal and old car parts. Photos exist of him using exactly these methods.

The famous 9-ton gate that a child could push open? It sat on a truck bearing and a metal shaft. When engineers finally removed it in 1986, it took a crane and six men.

Conspiracy theories about anti-gravity, magnetic currents, or extraterrestrials appeared later. His own friend and fellow builder called those ideas an insult to Ed’s hard work.

If one small man with 1920s tools could move 30-ton stones, a civilization with thousands of workers, ramps, and sleds could build the pyramids. No spaceships required.

Coral Castle still stands in Homestead, Florida. Worth seeing if you ever get the chance. 

Have you been there?

我对币安的认可，首先最重要的就是对用户需求的重视，平台是否听取意见，是否改进体验，交易体验等都会影响用户的去留，通过持续观察它的产品更新和服务变化，持续判断这一点

从规模来说，币安位列现货交易所综合榜第一，有最好的流动性深度，26年第二季度，前十大中心化现货交易所中，币安的交易量份额为38.7%

数据说明，币安拥有很大的交易基础，但看长期，需要在意能不能把规模化为用户持续愿意使用的服务

交易、钱包、理财产品和支付服务等，都和这个问题有关，而BNB的用途就建立在这些服务之上

持有BNB，能够获得那些实际权益？
长期持有一个币种，要看持币收益、产品奖励、活动机会、使用产品

在符合条件的情况下，BNB可以参与Earn、Launchpool、HODLer空投和Megadrop，它们分别涉及适用产品的持币奖励、新项目代币分配、历史持仓快照、以及持仓和任务积分

这里有实际案例：如你在2024年1月，购买一枚价格313美金的BNB，持续持有至25年第一季度末,并且参与了这些活动，不算代币涨幅的收益你可以拿到226美金，算上BNB涨幅收益达到553美元，一年的投资回报率高达177%，月化11.8%

除此之外，在交易和链上使用中，BNB也可以用于抵扣手续费、支付网格费、参与质押、在支持的协议中进行借贷和提供交易资金

一个资产，如果既没有未来价格空间，也没有持有期间能够使用的权益，那么就毫无吸引力

我们再看BNB Chain全生态累计地址已经超9亿，仅9月16日一天，BSC就处理了1789万笔交易，同时新增约66万个独立地址

9亿地址当然不等于9亿个人，一个人完全可以拥有很多个钱包地址，但每天接近2000万笔交易，这个数据就值得关注了

交易是用户真的在链上活动

转账、交易、买币、卖币、跑DeFi、借贷、质押、做LP，这些都是一笔笔真实的发生在链上交易

而这些活动又会继续创造BNB的使用场景

最基础的是Gas

币安给BNB提供的是一套中心化的使用场景

交易、理财、Launchpool、HODLer空投、Megadrop，包括各种持币权益，都建立在币安巨大的用户和交易规模之上

BNB Chain则给它提供了另外一套链上场景

Gas、质押、交易、借贷、抵押、流动性，包括整个链上生态每天产生的千万级交易需求

一个资产，如果既没有未来价格空间，也没有持有期间能够使用的权益，那么就毫无吸引力

反过来看，如果一个资产背后一直有人用，拿着它有实际权益，链上还有足够大的用户和交易规模，同时又不断有人需要它去Gas、质押、交易、借贷和抵押

你要做的是拿着，并且关注最新动向，相关活动，保持参与=超越了99%参与投资的人

I think $GSTOCK rapid rise to around a $20M market cap is not simply because it is the “leader of a new Launchpad.”

0xcafdbce93477261db8250e42bdae6e66733f9e20

It is actually hitting 5 layers of Narrative at the same time: Geniusfun as a new Launchpad + the first token + BNCB pairing + Stock Meme / RWA + Genius Foundation actually starting to accumulate BNCB.

And the most important change right now is that Genius’s mechanism has started generating real on-chain asset accumulation.

GSTOCK itself is not the official Genius Terminal token, nor is it a 1:1 Tokenized Stock. What makes it special is that it chose BNCB as its paired asset from the beginning.

This connects GSTOCK to:

Geniusfun → GSTOCK → BNCB → Stock Meme → BNB Treasury

So the market is no longer simply trading the “first Meme to pump on Geniusfun.” It is trading a First Runner that carries the combined Launchpad + Stock Meme + BNB Treasury Narrative.

More importantly, Geniusfun’s mechanism has started showing real asset accumulation:

Meme Trading Volume → Fees → Genius Foundation → BNCB Accumulation

This moves the Geniusfun story from “it may eventually use Meme trading fees to buy Tokenized Stocks” to “it is already using trading-generated fees to accumulate assets.”

This is what I believe is the core reason GSTOCK can command a high valuation premium.

Because GSTOCK’s biggest identity right now is being the First Runner / Face Token of Geniusfun.

If the market gradually forms:Geniusfun → GSTOCK

then GSTOCK is getting more than just a Meme premium. It is getting a Platform Representative Premium.

At the same time, Genius officially highlighted GSTOCK after it broke above a $10M MC, and asked:

“Will GSTOCK get a board seat”

This gives the market a potential next Narrative:

GSTOCK → BNCB → Genius Foundation → Real Equity → Shareholder Rights → Potential Board Representation

Of course, the Board Seat is still only a potential Narrative at this point and should not be treated as something that has already happened.

YZi Labs is similar.

The actual relationship is:YZi Labs → Genius → Geniusfun

Not:CZ → GSTOCK

So I would not define GSTOCK as a “CZ Coin,” but the YZi Labs Halo behind Genius can indeed bring additional Attention to the first wave of Geniusfun projects.

Right now, I think GSTOCK’s core flywheel is:Geniusfun Volume ↑ → Creator / Platform Fees ↑ → Foundation Asset Accumulation ↑ → BNCB ↑ → Stock / RWA Narrative ↑ → Attention ↑ → GSTOCK Volume ↑ → Geniusfun Volume ↑

The key thing to watch is whether this flywheel can continue.

Because GSTOCK’s standalone fundamentals are still limited:

Foundation holding BNCB ≠ GSTOCK Holders holding BNCB

Foundation accumulating Tokenized Stocks ≠ GSTOCK being redeemable for stocks

Potential Board Seat ≠ Already having a Board Seat

So right now, GSTOCK is more accurately:A high-beta vehicle for the Geniusfun Narrative.

Going forward, I’ll focus on three things:

1. Whether Geniusfun’s trading volume can continue

2. Whether the Foundation Treasury can continue accumulating real assets

3. Whether GSTOCK can maintain its position as the Attention Leader of Geniusfun

The third point is especially important.

The biggest problem with a new Launchpad is that there will always be new Tokens competing for Attention.

If GSTOCK loses its First Runner / Face Token position, the Platform Premium it currently enjoys could also decline quickly.

On the other hand, if Geniusfun’s trading volume continues to grow, the Foundation continues accumulating BNCB, and GSTOCK remains the market’s first association with Geniusfun, then the Narrative could further upgrade from:

“The first Meme to pump on Geniusfun” → “The first representative asset connecting Geniusfun’s Meme Economy with Real-World Equity.”

I think this is what really needs to be validated for GSTOCK to continue repricing higher from its current market cap.

Finally, Genius tweeted that it will buy the token with the highest market cap on September 25.

If that remains the case, then it seems like GSTOCK is the obvious candidate.

为什么$82,000难以突破？从筹码结构上或许能看到一些端倪。

首先，短期持有者的筹码（STH）分布在$59k-$81k直接（图1中红色），到$82,000的话，意味着所有STH都盈利了。

一些短期投机资金会选择获利了结，这是第一层卖压冲击。

这部分LTH未必真的是信仰者，也有部分只是买入套牢后，被动成为了长持的筹码。

当价格接近盈亏平衡时，选择离场。这是第二层卖压。

更要命的是，这里还是超级鲸鱼的集中地。

持有量超过100k枚BTC的，除了在$40k附近有2处外，剩下的都在$78k-$82k了。

谁的拳头硬，谁就说了算。

text:
作为一个过来人，我说一下终止全平 close position on stop 这个设计吧。。 

一般来说，这个设置就是在触发risk control （bot risk ratio < 1）和insufficient margin（保证金不足) 会把仓位全部平仓掉

这里的保证金又可以区分为：维持保证金，开仓保证金，单占用保证金，网格策略运行所需保证金等等等

大家可以看到这个设计的初衷就是为了“”控制风险“，相当于是一个止损点

为什么会有这个设计：是因为网格的计算比一般的合约还难（是一层层累加的），很多人是算不过来的（算得过来也不用这个了🤣） 

举个例子啊：按照你设计的网格，122后，将会累积到约5,250+个soxl （差不多是643k）按照20x的要求保证金需要33k左右，要是到118的话，保证金达到了40k左右

这里需要说的是：这个终止全平的设计是一个通用的设计，就我知道 @okx @Bybit_Official 都有类似的设计/选项供君选择 

看你说的情况应该是属于后者：开仓保证金不足，没办法开仓，系统判断为：终止，所以触发“终止全平”，所以系统帮你平仓

为什么开仓保证金不足也被系统认为应该“终止”，这个就涉及到网格策略的核心：连续性 ，网格是吃spread价差的，假设不能连续铺单子（出range）：原本自动循环的策略，开始出现缺单，实际交易行为偏离用户设置，就应该止损/不动

当然出现这种情况并不是一定平仓出局，你可以暂停/等，但是如果你选择了“终止平仓”，那系统就会按照你的设置来

你觉得因为是在上升趋势（从118-122），而系统提前帮你平仓所以你觉得亏了，最终损失1.4w+ ，而且随后价格122-128，你少了更多的预期收益

但你有没有想过，假设价格的路径是118 - 122 -110呢？ 这样看的话，你还能省一点

这个就是网格策略这个【终止全平】机制设置的意义 

而且grid合约的高杠杆网格策略天生就不适合大波动（即使是方向对的）。。。

text:
《AI行业最大的谎言，藏在“安全”两个字里》（The Biggest Lie in AI Is Called “Safety”）！
最近硅谷有个很有意思的变化：过去几年大家拼命讲更大的模型、更多的GPU、更快抵达AGI和ASI，但现在越来越多人开始强调另一件事——AI发展太快了，我们需要考虑安全，甚至需要适当减速。

AI安全当然是个重要的问题，但未必是“减速”背后最主要的原因。因为“AI安全”这四个字实在太好用了，它恰好同时解决了大型AI企业面前的三个现实麻烦：小公司的竞争、中国AI崛起带来的焦虑，以及越来越难向资本市场解释的巨额资本开支。

第一个麻烦是小公司。过去AI行业的游戏规则对巨头非常友好：模型越大越好，GPU越多越好，如果参加决赛需要100亿美元，创业公司甚至连报名表都不用填，资本本身就是护城河。但算法效率、模型蒸馏、小模型和开源等，正在改变这个逻辑，越来越小的团队，也可能用更少的计算资源获得过去只有巨头才能拥有的能力。

这时候“安全监管”就产生了一个微妙的效果：许可证、算力审计、安全测试、模型评估、法律责任、合规团队……对巨头来说叫成本，对20人左右的创业公司来说可能叫遗书。
最后AI行业确实安全了——因为牌桌旁只剩三四家公司。大家互相握手：“我们终于保护了人类。”门外创业者敲门：“那我呢？”“不好意思，你没有合规部门。”

第二个麻烦更有意思：中国。过去美国AI产业最舒服的叙事是：最先进的芯片、最大的算力、最多的资本，最终必然产生最强的模型。更多GPU→更强模型→更多资本开支→更深护城河，这条逻辑支撑了整个AI基础设施繁荣。

但DeepSeek和月之暗面等越来越多中国模型真正让美国一些大型AI企业焦虑的地方，不只是“中国也能做AI”，而是它们提出了一个更麻烦的问题：如果中国接近最前沿的AI能力，并不永远需要按照硅谷最昂贵的路线实现呢？算法效率、模型蒸馏、开源和更低廉的推理成本如果不断缩小差距，受到挑战的就不仅是美国的技术领先程度，还有过去几年形成的资本叙事。美国巨头刚准备建设几千亿美元的数据中心，突然有人问：“有没有可能，不需要这么贵？”这个问题比模型性能落后更让资本市场难受。

于是“AI安全”很自然地开始与“国家安全”结合。限制芯片可以谈安全，限制模型可以谈安全，限制开源可以讨论安全，限制外国AI产品仍然可以谈安全。最有趣的是，双方都认为自己在保护安全，同时又都认为对方在利用安全限制自己。AI可能还没学会欺骗人类，人类已经熟练地把AI加入了自己几千年的地缘政治游戏。真正让美国焦虑的也许不只是“中国出现了一个更好的模型”，而是：中国公司证明AI能力提升未必永远与资本投入等比例增长。

第三个麻烦最现实：钱。过去几年大型科技公司已经把AI资本开支推到了惊人的水平，GPU、数据中心、电力等一切都需要钱。资本市场愿意接受这些投入，一个重要前提就是相信：AI能力继续提高→需求继续爆发→需要更多算力→今天投入的几千亿美元最终变成未来更大的现金流。

但资本开支不可能永远比现金流增长得快。总有一天股东会问那个非常没有格局的问题：“哥们，什么时候回本？”，更麻烦的是，很多大型AI企业今天的估值，本身就在隐含一个假设：未来很多年AI投资仍值得持续扩大。如果突然承认“可能没必要再以过去的速度堆算力了”，受到影响的不只是几座数据中心，而是整套估值逻辑。

这时候，“AI安全”就显示出了惊人的叙事价值。模型迭代放缓，如果说“继续提高能力越来越难”，资本市场会紧张；如果说“为了更严格的安全评估，我们主动延长发布周期”，突然就有责任感了。大家应该都记得不久前Mark那个出售“剩余算力”而带崩AI股的场景，那是大家都不愿意看到的。

花钱速度需要缓一缓，不是现金流压力，而是“人类需要更多时间适应和提防AI”。华尔街分析师都不好意思继续追问投资回报率了——人家正在拯救全人类，你还在那里算折旧，格局确实小了。

当然我并不认为AI安全是假的。真正有意思的地方恰恰是：一个真实的问题，可以同时成为很多利益最体面的理由。安全可以保护社会，也可以提高行业门槛；可以防止危险模型扩散，也可以限制新的竞争者；可以成为应对中国AI崛起的政策工具，也可以给巨额资本开支从“无限狂奔”转向“理性增长”提供一个漂亮的解释。

这甚至不需要什么阴谋，利益结构本身，就会让不同的人自然找到同一种最适合自己的语言。毕竟最成功的产业政策从来不会叫《如何保护本国几家大型科技公司的护城河》，这种名字太难听了，最好叫——《为了人类安全》。

所以以后再有人说“为了AI安全，我们应该让AI慢一点”，真正值得问的不是AI有没有风险，而是：谁慢？谁不用慢？中国会不会跟着慢？谁因为大家慢下来获得了更大的利益？如果最后获益最大的，恰好是那些已经拥有最多算力、最多资本和最大市场份额的人，那么我们讨论的可能就不只是AI安全，而是在讨论AI时代一个非常古老的问题：谁有资格继续坐在牌桌上。

资本主义发展几百年，叙事能力也完成了一次升级——以前是“为了利润”，现在是“为了人类”！

text:
In 1984, Nike signed a 21-year-old Michael Jordan for $500K a year. Nike was known for running shoes. Converse dominated the NBA. Jordan gave Nike a way into basketball, and in return, he got his own signature line and royalties.

Air Jordan generated $126M in its first year.

Forty-two years later, Kylian Mbappé is making a similar bet, except this time, the athlete is getting equity in the company itself.

Mbappé had worn Nike since he was 8 years old. After nearly two decades with the brand, he let his contract expire and signed with Swiss running company On.

The reported deal includes equity, a long-term partnership, and involvement in product development. On is entering football in 2027, and Mbappé will be the face of it.

The interesting part is that On has already run a version of this playbook.

In 2019, Roger Federer became an investor in On after his Nike footwear partnership ended. He took an estimated 2.5–3% stake and helped develop the company's tennis products.

When On went public in 2021, his stake was estimated to be worth roughly $300M. Federer earned approximately $130M in career prize money over 24 years. His equity stake became worth more than twice what he earned playing tennis.

Mbappé is now combining the Federer ownership model with the Jordan signature-product model.

And On isn't starting from zero. The company generated CHF 1.68B in revenue and CHF 207.8M in free cash flow during the first half of 2026. It's an established running business trying to enter one of the largest sportswear categories in the world.

The company also brought in Thierry Henry as Director of Football, giving it another recognizable name as it develops its football business.

The difference between an endorsement and equity is what happens after the athlete stops playing.

Nike paid Jordan to wear its shoes, but the royalties meant he also participated in the success of what he helped create. Federer went further by owning a piece of the company. Mbappé now has exposure to On's entire business, not just the sales of his own boots.

That distinction matters when the company is still expanding into new categories.

The question for On shareholders is whether football can generate enough incremental EBITDA and free cash flow to justify the cost of entering a market dominated by Nike, Adidas and Puma.

For Mbappé, the bet is different. He's exchanging some of the certainty of a traditional endorsement relationship for exposure to the long-term value of the business he's helping build.

Jordan helped turn Nike into a basketball powerhouse. Federer helped On establish itself in tennis.

Now On is betting that Mbappé can help it do the same in football.

Its first boots arrive in 2027.

A public free entry point built for TypeSafe AI's Jev model.

Users give it a state, plus several typed questions, and it returns structured answers in parallel at once, without generating long text.

Three question types:

Noul: yes/no, returns a probability from 0 to 1

Choice: picks one from user-defined options, returns the option, probability distribution, and confidence

Score: scores according to user-defined levels, also with probability and confidence

Typical latency is around 70 to 500 ms, and output is essentially free. It's suited for scenarios where programs need to branch immediately, such as ticket triage, urgency assessment, content moderation, agent routing, RAG filtering, and compliance checks, rather than writing articles.

Token utility: trading generates fees → the treasury uses ETH to pay TypeSafe's inference bills → free unlimited API is provided to the public.
Buy and sell taxes are roughly 1% each, with creator fees going into the treasury.

text:
Jev might genuinely be an “Internet moment” for AI.

TypeSafe reports up to 193x faster and 444x cheaper performance in tests with Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.

@0xCodila just wrote a great 10-page article explaining what Jev is, how to use it, and where its 100x advantage comes from.

Here are the 10 steps:

1 → LLMs create. Agents act. Jev decides the next move.

2 → Turn agent forks into three primitives: Choice, Score and probability.

3 → Build with OpenAI, Anthropic or xAI first, then swap Jev in without rebuilding the graph.

4 → Start with shared state, parallel decisions, risk thresholds and an execution queue.

5 → Batch decisions instead of making them sequentially. In one test, 13 questions were 10x faster and 12.2x cheaper.

6 → Put Jev at bounded forks: agent, model, tool, browser action or human escalation.

7 → Benchmark the whole loop, not just individual model calls.

8 → Rank wide, read narrow: shortlist first, then spend compute on what matters.

9 → Reuse the same system: State → Questions → Action → Verify.

10 → Keep Jev out of math, writing and irreversible execution. Code computes, LLMs create, Jev decides.

The result:

A slow, expensive agent loop becomes a much faster decision system that can route, score and escalate in milliseconds.

$FEELSGOOD is a Pepe ecosystem Meme on Solana that has been particularly worth watching recently.

HgcxVs6kJhPAaGqnPNGaa7zYgNT49hJrLufiqcNMuYZT 

Its original core narrative is actually very simple: “Feels Good Man” is a classic Meme expression within Pepe culture, so this name is not creating a new IP from scratch, but directly reusing an internet symbol that has existed for years and is already very familiar to Crypto users.

What really brought it a large amount of attention was PEPE launching on Solana.

On September 19, Sunrise announced that PEPE had officially launched on Solana, and Solana’s official account subsequently reposted the news. Shortly after, StonkFun directly replied:“Solana feels good man.”

StonkFun then announced that users could directly use PEPE as a trading pair to launch Memes on StonkFun.

So the whole story suddenly became very complete:PEPE → Solana → “Solana feels good man” → FEELSGOOD → StonkFun PEPE Pair

This was the core source of attention behind FEELSGOOD’s first major move.

More importantly, FEELSGOOD was not simply piggybacking on a phrase. Its trading market itself is directly connected to PEPE. The publicly available FEELSGOOD/PEPE market uses the Solana PEPE contract launched by Sunrise, creating a very intuitive connection:PEPE Meme → FEELSGOOD Meme → PEPE Liquidity

In other words, the name, event, and trading pair are all aligned.

This is actually one of the ideal situations for a Meme.

Users do not need to read a whitepaper or understand complicated Tokenomics. They only need to see:PEPE is coming to Solana → Solana feels good man → FEELSGOOD

And the whole story is complete.

So why did FEELSGOOD rise so quickly? I think the core was not a single catalyst, but several Attention Layers stacking on top of each other within a very short period of time.

First Layer: Pepe itself is an established Meme IP

“Feels Good Man” is not a newly created meme. It has been a long-standing expression within Pepe culture.

So FEELSGOOD was born with an existing cultural symbol instead of having to educate the market from zero.

Second Layer: PEPE launching on Solana created a real event catalyst

This gave FEELSGOOD a very specific time window.

Without PEPE launching on Solana, “Feels Good Man” would simply be an old Meme.

But once PEPE entered Solana:Old Meme → New Event → New Trading Market

An existing cultural symbol suddenly regained Attention.

Third Layer: StonkFun itself participated in the Meme

This is very important.

StonkFun was not simply providing a trading venue. It directly participated in the Narrative:“Solana feels good man.”

At the same time, it announced support for PEPE Pairs.

This gave FEELSGOOD a very special position: it was not simply piggybacking on PEPE on Solana, but appeared during the exact window when PEPE had just entered Solana and StonkFun had just opened PEPE Pairs.

That is why the market can give it a certain First-Mover / Attention Premium.

FEELSGOOD’s Narrative Stack

I would compress it into:Pepe Culture → Feels Good Man → PEPE on Solana → Solana Meme → PEPE Pair → StonkFun → FEELSGOOD

Or even more simply:PEPE × Solana × StonkFun

That is its core story.

There is also another very important new catalyst: Moonshot.

Moonshot officially posted:“Feels Good Man (FEELSGOOD) is now verified on Moonshot.”

And it directly provides a trading entry for FEELSGOOD.

So Moonshot Verified is one of FEELSGOOD’s important new catalysts.

From a market-structure perspective, Verification has real practical significance:Moonshot Verified → Easier for platform users to discover → New Trading Entry → Larger Potential Retail Flow → More Trading Volume → More Attention

Moonshot currently advertises 2M+ users and provides access to Meme, stock, and leveraged trading.

Therefore, the significance of Moonshot for FEELSGOOD is that it exposes a StonkFun-native Meme to a much larger retail trading entry point.

I think the market is now betting on something more specific than simply:“Will FEELSGOOD continue to rise?”

It is betting on:After PEPE launched on Solana, can FEELSGOOD become the most representative Pepe derivative Meme in the Solana / StonkFun ecosystem?

Because it currently occupies several positions at the same time:

Classic Pepe IP

PEPE’s Solana launch event

StonkFun PEPE Pair

StonkFun Official Meme Attention

Moonshot Verified

So its Attention Flow can be understood as:PEPE → Solana → StonkFun → “Feels Good Man” → FEELSGOOD → PEPE Pair → Moonshot → More Traders

Catalysts Worth Watching

1. PEPE Trading Volume on Solana

This is the most important underlying variable.

If PEPE continues to grow on Solana, FEELSGOOD’s cultural source of attention will not disappear immediately.

2. FEELSGOOD / PEPE Trading Volume

If this trading pair continues to generate volume, it shows that FEELSGOOD is not simply riding the narrative, but is starting to form its own market.

3. StonkFun’s PEPE Ecosystem

If more Tokens start using PEPE as a quote asset, StonkFun could gradually form its own PEPE ecosystem.

If FEELSGOOD can remain at the top, it could evolve from an:Event Meme

into a:StonkFun PEPE Ecosystem Representative

4. Moonshot Traffic

After Moonshot Verification, the most important thing to watch is not the word “Verified” itself, but:Moonshot Volume → Holder Growth → New Wallets → Liquidity

If Moonshot actually brings in a large number of new users, that becomes a real catalyst.

5. Further Attention from Solana / StonkFun

If more official interactions, ecosystem integrations, or additional exposure around:PEPE × Solana × FEELSGOOD

appear in the future, the Narrative could expand further.

But the risks are also very clear

The biggest risk is that FEELSGOOD is still highly dependent on PEPE’s Attention.

If:PEPE Attention ↓ → Solana PEPE Attention ↓ → FEELSGOOD Attention ↓

then it could quickly become just another Meme.

The second risk is Meme replicability.

“Feels Good Man” itself is an open cultural symbol. Anyone can copy the name, image, or narrative.

So what FEELSGOOD really needs to build is:

Community + Liquidity + Recognition

rather than relying solely on the name.

Finally, how I would define FEELSGOOD

FEELSGOOD is a Meme that uses the event of PEPE launching on Solana to connect classic Pepe culture, Solana, the StonkFun PEPE Pair, and Moonshot traffic.

Its price/attention path is quite clear:PEPE Launches on Solana → Stonk: “Solana feels good man” → FEELSGOOD Appears → StonkFun Opens PEPE Pair → FEELSGOOD Becomes an Early Representative Meme → PEPE / FEELSGOOD Attention Grows → Moonshot Verified → Larger Potential Retail Trading Entry

So what the market is really betting on now is:Can FEELSGOOD turn the one-time PEPE × Solana event into a long-term StonkFun / Solana Pepe Meme?

If PEPE’s Solana traffic + StonkFun PEPE trading volume + FEELSGOOD community + Moonshot new users can all grow together, its Narrative could evolve from:“The Event Meme of PEPE Launching on Solana”

into:“The Pepe Representative Meme of Solana / StonkFun.”

On the other hand, if PEPE’s Solana attention fades, Moonshot fails to bring in sustained new users, or a stronger PEPE Meme emerges on StonkFun, this Narrative could weaken very quickly.

So the most important thing to watch for FEELSGOOD right now is whether it can turn this wave of Attention into real Holders, Liquidity, and sustained Volume.

A village once hired a watchman to keep them safe from wolves.

He took the role seriously. Each night, while the rest of the villagers slept, he walked the fence line with a lantern. With time he taught himself to spot what others would overlook: the impressions wolves left in soft soil, the hush of movement in brush, and the shallow stretches of river they often used to cross.

As his skill grew, so did his intensity. What began as careful attention turned into constant searching.

One night he noticed a snapped branch near the fence. “A wolf was here,” he said.

The next night he found no tracks at all. “They’ve learned to hide their tracks,” he said.

Another evening the chickens rustled and complained. “They can smell the wolves.”

When the chickens stayed quiet the following night, his fear didn’t ease - it deepened. “The wolves have learned how to approach without frightening them.”

The villagers pointed out that he hadn’t actually seen a wolf in months and suggested the pack might have moved on. He only shook his head.

“That is exactly what they want us to think.”

From then on, everything became proof to him. Evidence meant wolves.

And so did the absence of evidence.

If a chicken disappeared, it meant wolves.

If a chicken returned, it meant the wolves had released it.

A gap beneath the fence meant wolves had come through.

An unbroken fence meant they’d found another way in.

He stopped sleeping. He started drawing maps, connecting broken branches, footprints, missing tools, odd sounds, and the shifting patterns of birds. Strings began to cover his walls, tying one small incident to the next.

To everyone else, the village felt quiet.

To him, it had never been more dangerous.

Then, one night, he saw two glowing eyes beyond the fence.

“At last,” he whispered.

He raised his bow and let an arrow fly.

By morning the villagers learned what he had hit: and old lantern hanging at the far gate. Two pieces of glass had caught his own light and reflected it back to him.

The old blacksmith bent down, lifted one of the shards, and faced the watchman.

“You were once the best watchman we’ve ever had,” he said.

“I still am,” replied the watchman. “That’s why I see what the rest of you cannot.”

The blacksmith placed the shard in his hand.

“No. Once you searched for wolves.

Now you search for reasons to believe there are wolves.”

The watchman looked into the glass. For the first time in years, the only thing staring back was himself.

Then he finally understood:

A man who doubts everything may believe himself impossible to deceive.

But when every shadow becomes evidence, he no longer needs anyone else to deceive him.

He can do it all by himself.

Poland lost hundreds of millions trying to buy Venezuelan oil with crypto to circumvent American sanctions.

The head of a division of Polish Orlen met a 25-year-old founder of a Dubai firm, and five days later the state-owned company transferred a $230 million advance to this person.

The scheme involved settlement in USDT because ordinary bank payments to Venezuela do not go through. Then comes something that is hard to believe: access to the wallets was handed over to intermediaries on flash drives (!!!) during personal meetings in Caracas. 

One of them was given the keys to 110 million USDT and disappeared. Another $50 million vanished during conversion through another Dubai firm; a court case is now underway there.

The intermediaries from PDVSA never received the rights to specific oil cargoes. Three tankers arrived for 6 million barrels, stood idle at the berth for months and left empty. The demurrage of one of them alone cost $72 million.

The result: a small shipment of petroleum products instead of six million barrels and at least $424 million in losses.

My good friend @A_Leutenegger always says that access control is the main reason for DeFi hacks. In @LidoFinance we agree with that. This is why we have developed “Execution Delegation Framework”, a tool that meaningfully improves the way your protocol interacts with off-chain actors holding important permissions.

The key idea is simple:
- Hot key is only for execution.
- Hot key is easily disposable and replaceable by the Owner.
- Owner is super secure but used only for hot wallet management.

So you have a hot wallet that you can rotate any moment, and owner that is immutable and very secure. This combination gives you a unique set of properties: governance less routine hot key management, easy access to the hot wallet, top level security control over the permission holder via the owner.

Read more about the basic version of EDF - https://t.co/aATKIBF3bl

text:
I am in my late 20s

If you're in your early 20s and feel stuck, your mindset is either your greatest asset or your biggest obstacle. 
Here are 9 brutal truths to build a dangerous mindset for success.

- Big promises don't change your life; execution does. Stop saying 'I'll start tomorrow.' Break goals into small, boring, daily steps. Professionals execute, amateurs dream.

- Long-term success isn't about external validation. Don't chase applause. Track your own progress and stay consistent even when no one is watching.

- Focus isn't a passive feeling it's a skill you train. When your mind drifts, pull it back. That repetition builds real willpower.

- Your success isn't defined by external conditions like the economy or AI. It's defined by your ability to adapt and learn. Filter out the noise.

- Use Reverse Thinking. Instead of staring at the goal (A to B) and getting overwhelmed, start at the end and work backward to find your first step.

- Stop self-sabotage. Don't just set goals, use affirmations and visualization to reprogram your subconscious so your habits support your future, not your past.

- Manage priorities, not time. Stop trying to control the clock. Use an 'Ivy Lee' style card system, pick your top 6 tasks and stick to them.

- Learn to let go. Forcing things outside your control leads to frustration. Focus on your actions, not the outcome.

- Success is a process, not an event. Stay disciplined, keep showing up, and build a mindset that wins regardless of the circumstances.

When Should You Take Profit?

He splits the market into three phases and argues the answer is completely different in each one. By his read we're 50k below the previous high, which is the earliest phase.

A useful framework to keep in mind while setting your profit-taking targets.
author: thedefiedge
quoted_text:
Hard agree here.

I always heavily encourage people to take profit (especially if up a meaningful/life-altering amount), but

The phase of the market we're in matters... a lot

There are three buckets:
-Below ATH
-Just underneath or just barely past ATH
-Past ATH

Right now we're at the earliest phase of "Below ATH".

We're 50k below ATH. And I think a lot of people have expectations (and the expectations of a large group matter, in markets) of going 50k above the prev ATH

Which is to say.. we're insanely early.

I liken the Bessent yield curve control tweet (ie "gov is gonna inject a ton of money into markets) as analogous to when the intern leaked the BTC ETF news last cycle:

There was a BIG impulse up, but then things stalled out, and spent a few weeks slowwwly letting some of the air out of the balloon. But that didn't matter - it was the market tipping its hand to what it *was* going to do under the approval.

Sound familiar?

If we were cruising around the previous ATH, maybe between 115k, or just past it at 130k, I might be a lot more cautious and measured. I think there's still conviction there that we're going substantially higher (why else would we be here, right? if BTC doesn't go above its previous ATH, the entire industry is cooked)

And I'd be especially cautious, and actively shaving off/selling anywhere above that (130, 140, 150k, etc)

But selling and sidelining, right here?

- Fifty thousand dollars below prev ATH, after the treasury secretary signaled "let's intervene, let's grow our way out of debt",

- We have unprecedented regulatory tailwinds, with the SEC not only not antagonizing people, but quite literally cheering us on (ie clarity act doesn't really matter, just a dump truck of icing on a really yummy cake if/when it comes)

- We are literally weeks away from a massive cohort of VERY rich "4 year cycle intact" buyers and sellers that, with cultlike zealousness sell or bid the 4 year cycle top/bottom mark (and this is their 'buy' zone)

- Inflation is ~at expectation, even with oil elevated, and with bonds and other things looking dicey, Trump's hand could finally get forced to finally stop doing disastrous bullshit in Iran, stuff that even many of his supporters are tilted by

- Us stopping here, just purely on charts, is just letting long term moving averages catch up a bit

If I was sidelined here (to what end? re-entering potentially 5, 10% lower?), I'd be shaking like a shitting dog.

Under these conditions, we're literally something like *a single tweet or press release away* from impulsing past the 50 week MA, and every single conviction/quality onchain bag could move up 300% within a week, and majors doubling, kicking off the real consensus bull market in earnest. This all happens into the early end of the 4 year cycle buyer's bids, which then can tsunami in and rip us faster than people can appreciate.

Like man, I dunno. I'm pretty conservative and risk averse -- but that same risk aversion makes me think not being exposed here, and not simply being patient for a bit is what's risky. Being sidelined is risky, to me.

Because Doug Funnie Said So,

Show me your Knot,

Diaperliquid.

text:
这几天我把自己实际在用的 TapeOut / BEM 自动收割流程，整理成了一个可以给别人直接研究和部署的开源版本：

https://t.co/OLqJ27ZiVi

这不是为了开源重新写了一个 Demo。

我做的是反过来：从真实运行的生产脚本里，把可复用的执行内核拆出来，再把我自己的钱包、矿机 inventory、本机路径、个人阈值、资金分配策略等全部剥离。

现在这个版本可以完成：

- 自动读取 TapeOut 可领取奖励
- `claimMany` 自动领取
- 默认只 Claim，也可以按配置把本轮新领取的 BEM 通过白名单 V3 路由卖出
- Dry-run 默认开启，真钱执行需要两道显式开关
- 不靠“钱包余额变了多少”猜执行结果，而是按具体交易 receipt 做归因
- 交易结果未知时不会自动重发
- Exact approve + 失败后的 allowance cleanup
- Gas cap、quote freshness、slippage、confirmations、nonce 等安全门
- 本地 encrypted keystore + OS keyring，不需要把私钥交给 AI

我还专门让 Codex 独立做了几轮从零安全审查。

第一轮抓出 8 个 blocker，第二轮 4 个，第三轮 3 个，全部修完之后最终 blocker-focused review 是：

**Blockers: None**

目前完整测试是 65/65 PASS。

不过我还是把它标成了 `0.1.0rc2`，因为这个公开版本还没有重新拿真钱完整跑一遍。

所以如果你要用：

先看 README / SECURITY，先 dry-run，确认自己的合约地址、miner keys、router 和钱包环境，再考虑 live。

MIT License，欢迎直接研究、改、提 Issue / PR。

如果后面真有人在用，我再继续把 fork test、更多 signer 和运行监控补进去。

Right now, I think GSTOCK’s core flywheel is:Geniusfun Volume ↑ → Creator / Platform Fees ↑ → Foundation Asset Accumulation ↑ → BNCB ↑ → Stock / RWA Narrative ↑ → Attention ↑ → GSTOCK Volume ↑ → Geniusfun Volume ↑

The key thing to watch is whether this flywheel can continue.

Because GSTOCK’s standalone fundamentals are still limited:

Foundation holding BNCB ≠ GSTOCK Holders holding BNCB

Foundation accumulating Tokenized Stocks ≠ GSTOCK being redeemable for stocks

Potential Board Seat ≠ Already having a Board Seat

So right now, GSTOCK is more accurately:A high-beta vehicle for the Geniusfun Narrative.

Going forward, I’ll focus on three things:

1. Whether Geniusfun’s trading volume can continue

2. Whether the Foundation Treasury can continue accumulating real assets

3. Whether GSTOCK can maintain its position as the Attention Leader of Geniusfun

The third point is especially important.

The biggest problem with a new Launchpad is that there will always be new Tokens competing for Attention.

If GSTOCK loses its First Runner / Face Token position, the Platform Premium it currently enjoys could also decline quickly.

On the other hand, if Geniusfun’s trading volume continues to grow, the Foundation continues accumulating BNCB, and GSTOCK remains the market’s first association with Geniusfun, then the Narrative could further upgrade from:

“The first Meme to pump on Geniusfun” → “The first representative asset connecting Geniusfun’s Meme Economy with Real-World Equity.”

I think this is what really needs to be validated for GSTOCK to continue repricing higher from its current market cap.

Finally, Genius tweeted that it will buy the token with the highest market cap on September 25.

If that remains the case, then it seems like GSTOCK is the obvious candidate.

text:
Anthropic 悄悄建了一个生物实验室

据路透社独家报道，Anthropic 已在旧金山湾区建成了一间湿实验室（wet lab，即可以进行真实生化实验的物理实验室），正式把 AI 的触角从软件延伸到药物研发。

Anthropic 生命科学负责人 Eric Kauderer-Abrams 在采访中证实了这件事。他的说法是：要做生物学研究，最终的检验标准仍然是真实的实验室工作，光靠计算机模拟不够。一部分实验自己做，一部分和外部合作伙伴做——这和大多数生物技术公司的做法一样。

这不是心血来潮。过去几个月，Anthropic 动作密集：花约 4 亿美元股票收购了一家叫 Coefficient Bio 的初创公司，用于构建药物研发工具；把诺华 CEO Vas Narasimhan 拉进了董事会；发布了名为 Claude Science 的软件；6 月在旧金山公开宣布要启动药物研发项目。LinkedIn 上也在招采购运营负责人、蛋白质和核酸表征方面的专家，招聘帖里写的目标是"把生命科学的进展速度提高一个数量级"。Kauderer-Abrams 说，生命科学已经是 Anthropic 在人力和资源投入上最大的方向之一。

Anthropic 瞄准的是传统药企觉得"不可成药"（undruggable）的领域——那些因为靶点太难、商业回报不高而被忽视的罕见病。他们认为 AI 可以加速发现双特异性甚至三特异性抗体这类复杂分子，这类药物可以同时攻击多个靶点，设计难度极高，但 AI 擅长处理这种复杂度。CEO Dario Amodei 对此有切身之痛——他的父亲因一种疾病去世，而治愈方法在几年后才出现。

不过，Anthropic 目前画了一条明确的线：只做临床前研究，不做临床试验，不跟药企抢生意。这也是为了缓解一个现实的信任问题——那些使用 Claude 的大药企（基因泰克、百时美施贵宝、诺和诺德都在列）会担心 Anthropic 从它们的数据中学到什么。

值得注意的时间节点：这一切发生在 Anthropic 准备以约 2 万亿美元估值 IPO 的前夕，也正值 AI 安全争议白热化——就在最近两周，Anthropic 自己的研究人员警告 AI 可能导致人类灭绝，公司还发现其系统存在被用于生物武器开发的风险。一边踩油门，一边拉手刹，这种张力是 Anthropic 当下最真实的写照。

作为对比，Google 旗下的 Isomorphic Labs 做 AI 药物发现已经好几年了，原计划 2026 年底进入临床，但之前已经推迟过一次。药物研发的现实就是这样：从发现一个分子到药物上市，通常要好多年，而且大多数药物在临床试验中会失败。Anthropic 的野心很大，但路还很长。

这件事背后的分歧还是 2025 年欧美重新启动对伊朗制裁的问题。欧美认为伊朗违反了 2015 年伊核协议，所以通过 snapback 恢复联合国制裁。中国和俄罗斯一直不承认这套程序合法，因此也不认可在这个基础上继续延长制裁监督机制。

美国认为中俄否决以后，会让伊朗制裁执行出现更大的监督空白。中俄则认为西方把安理会和制裁机制政治化，伊朗核问题应该重新通过外交谈判解决。其实这个专家小组过去一年已经因为人选谈不拢而没有正常运作了。

放到现在的美伊冲突背景下看，这也说明安理会内部对于伊朗问题的分裂越来越明显。美国和欧洲希望继续通过制裁施压，中国和俄罗斯则不接受现有制裁恢复的法律基础，后面想再通过联合国形成统一的对伊朗制裁和监督机制，只会越来越难。

我个人的理解是，中国在支持伊朗维护正当权益的同时，也在要求伊朗考虑其他国家的能源和贸易利益。霍尔木兹受阻，已经影响了包括中国在内的石油进口国。如果红海再出问题，沙特通过东西输油管道将原油送往红海、绕开霍尔木兹的出口路线也会受到影响。现在这条管道本身又出现停运，后续如果航运风险继续扩大，进口国寻找替代供应的成本还会增加。

阿拉格齐这次也表示，希望重回外交解决渠道，并称伊朗已经与阿曼形成开放霍尔木兹海峡的方案，但仍要求美国履行承诺。6月的谈判框架涉及美国解除海上封锁、伊朗恢复商船通航，以及后续制裁和核问题的谈判。所以即便伊朗愿意谈，开放海峡的方案也已经有了，美国如何调整封锁、双方如何落实承诺，仍然需要解决。这次会谈还没有公布恢复通航的日期。

text:
XLS-66 and XRP-collateralized DeFi: two different credit primitives for developers.

XLS-66 is designed around borrower credit. 

Liquidity sits in XRPL Single Asset Vaults, loans are fixed-term, underwriting happens offchain, and first-loss capital helps absorb defaults. Building on it means thinking about borrowers, underwriting standards, repayment schedules, loan brokers and default risk.

Collateralized DeFi takes a different approach. 

XRP becomes FXRP, FXRP is deposited into a lending market, and borrowing capacity is determined by the value of the collateral. That requires reliable pricing, liquidity and liquidations rather than borrower underwriting.

These models complement each other.

XLS-66 can support underwritten credit where the identity and creditworthiness of the borrower matter.

FXRP + Smart Accounts can support permissionless XRP-backed credit where the collateral itself secures the debt, while XRPL remains the user control layer.

奥巴马刚刚公开质疑了 Agentic AI。

而且他说的不是「AI 会不会毁灭人类」这种宏大问题，而是一个更现实的问题：

我们真的需要让 AI Agent 在互联网上自由行动吗？

9 月 18 日，奥巴马在 Colgate University 谈 AI 时说，如果目标只是用 AI 治癌症、开发新能源，其实根本不需要让 Agentic AI 在互联网上到处自主行动。

他认为，科技公司之所以继续往这个方向推，一个重要原因是商业需求：

你得做出一个用户愿意付钱买的产品。

这句话其实戳中了现在 Agent 浪潮里一个挺有意思的矛盾。

从社会价值看，AI 能不能把科研、医疗、能源做得更好是一回事；

从公司的商业模型看，AI 能不能自己打开网页、操作电脑、下单、写代码、替人完成完整任务，又是另一回事。

后者显然更容易直接变成产品和收入。

奥巴马随后也明确表示，他不认为可以单纯依赖市场激励和企业自律来解决安全问题，最终仍然需要政府监管框架。

很有意思。

美国的政治讨论开始我们到底应该允许 Agent 替人做多少事？

这几天，我把自己实际在用的 TapeOut / BEM 自动收割流程，整理成了一个开源版本：

TapeOut Harvester v0.1.0rc2

这不是为了开源临时写的 Demo。

我是反过来做的：从真实运行的生产脚本里拆，把自己的钱包、矿机 inventory、本机路径、个人阈值和资金策略全部剥离，只留下别人也能复用的部分。

现在它能做的事情其实很简单：

- 读取当前可领取的 BEM
- 自动 Claim
- 可以只 Claim，也可以按配置卖出

- 每次执行留下 receipt
- 结果不确定就停，不会盲目重复发交易

我觉得真正有意思的，不是“又开源了一个 Bot”。

以前参与链上项目，很多事情都得自己反复盯：

今天产出多少？
该不该 Claim？
要不要卖？
到底成交没有？
出了异常怎么办？

现在我在一点点把这些重复操作，变成可以被 AI 调用、可以验证、可以长期运行的模块。

从“AI 帮我研究”，到“AI 帮我运营”，再到把真正跑过的模块开源给别人。

完整测试 65/65 PASS，我也让 Codex 做了多轮独立安全审查，最后的 blocker-focused review 是 0 blockers。

text:
我们一直在研究怎么让 Agent 更聪明。

这篇论文反过来问了一句：

能不能让 Agent 自己研究，怎么把自己跑得更便宜？

NVIDIA、NTU、MIT 团队的 SoL-Pi，就是让 Research Agent 自动发现 Harness 里的 Token 浪费，再通过大规模实验筛掉无效改法。

他们让 Research Agent 观察真实执行轨迹，提出 Harness 改法，再放进大量环境中反复测试。整个搜索覆盖 152 个方向、535 个可执行环境和 3000+ 次实验。

最后真正留下来的只有 4 个机制。

思路其实还挺朴素的：合并连续工具操作；只在划算的时候压缩上下文；大段工具输出先存起来、需要时再读；冗长日志只保留经过验证的关键证据。

结果在 EdgeBench 上，SoL-Pi 在 GPT-5.6 Sol 和 Opus 5 上保持接近 Pi 的任务表现，同时减少约 45%–49% 的 Token 流量，API 成本降低约三分之一。并且用 GPT-5.6 Sol 搜出来的 Harness，可以直接迁移到 Opus 5，不需要重新优化。

还有一个细节是最终评测集完全隔离，候选方案冻结后才能进去测试；如果失败，就直接淘汰，结果不会再回流给 Agent 继续针对性修改。这样能尽量避免「为了 benchmark 把 Harness 越改越偏」。

所以这篇工作给的insight是 Harness 自进化未必需要一开始就追求复杂的新架构。

大量价值可能藏在那些每天都在发生的浪费里，重复调用、反复传输、无效上下文和过长日志。

当 AI 开始自己发现并修掉这些系统性浪费，Agent 的「自我改进」也就从能力提升，走到了运行效率这一层。

text:
强烈建议大家去看一下 Jev 创始人 Diogo Almeida 的这个演讲，关于 Jev 的一切，他在这个视频中早就预言。

Jev 一开始就是盯着自动化去的，Diogo Almeida 认为现在的 LLM 陷入了一个史诗级大弯路，就是 RLHF。

RLHF 在人机交互也就是取悦人类方面，很出色，但在自动化方面很糟糕。它不能实现完全的自动化，人类必须在环。

不止 ChatGPT ，Claude Code 的原罪也在于 RLHF。所以他认为 ChatGPT 和 Claude Code 本质上属于一个范式，Claude Code 并不是下一个时代，真正的自动化才是下一个时代。

简单来说，RLHF 就是收集人类便好，并根据人类便好优化。它的优化目标也不是自动化。

他也否定了 RLVR 是答案：RLHF 优化人类偏好，RLVR 优化纯正确性，而他们在做的第三条路优化的是校准过的决策能力。

Diogo Almeida 认为，数据比算力重要，做对的任务比数据重要得多。预训练模型本身已经足够聪明，问题只在于我们用偏好优化把它挖歪了。

欢迎来到老登币狂奔的一天， near:native ， $UNI 和 $ZEC 都成了最靓的仔。

10天前我们提到，当时英文区下一个看好的代币是 near:native ，但当时也有人质疑催化剂从哪来，没有看涨的理由。

现在马后炮的看，NEAR 最大的推手是其“机密意图（Confidential Intents）”TVL 突破 7000 万美元后，触发的 NEAR@3.33 里程碑激励计划。

官方给在机密模式（你可以理解为隐私交易）下持仓>100U、且交互过的用户发放了 333,333 枚名为 NEAR@3.33 的特殊代币。

注意，拿到手的是锁定的死筹码，直接卖是卖不掉的。只有当真实的 NEAR 价格（3日加权均价）连续站稳 3.33 美元以上时，这批锁定的筹码才能 1:1 兑换成真正可流通的 NEAR。

这等于一个新的空投玩法，不给你直接打币怕砸盘，更类似一张“行权价为 3.33 美元的看涨期权”。你拿了奖励不仅不能砸，还得盼着、甚至合力把币价往 3.33 抬。

NEAR 最近价格从大约 2.3–2.5 美元附近快速拉升到 2.8–3.3美元区间，成交量也明显放大。

而 UNI 的催化剂更加明显，在上个月 Robinhood 链活跃时就已经启动了。

Uniswap 在 Robinhood Chain 上占 DEX 成交主导地位，承接了大量 meme 和代币化股票交易。这条链一度贡献协议收入/销毁的很大一部分，有时段到四成甚至六成以上）等于传统券商流量直接灌进 Uniswap，再回流到 UNI 销毁。

此外，Uniswap 从 Arc 上线就接入，不只吃 Robinhood，还能接下一波机构链/稳定币链流量。

另外 SEC 对代币化美股、许可制 AMM 的豁免/创新框架， Uniswap v4 的 permissioned pools 也被人看做是直接受益方。

而至于 ZEC ，无需多言，小编已经拍断大腿了。

在链上打新逐渐内卷的当下，多了解一些老登币的催化逻辑，也是一条越来越值得关注的主线。

author: liujackc
quoted_text:
狗狗币大概率已经被马斯克边缘化了，马斯克重回币圈最好的方式就是重新发币。

随着ZEC市值暴涨至约250亿美元、市值前十，DOGE已经被挤到第11名，市值只剩约130亿美元。

2021年巅峰时期，DOGE市值一度达到880亿美元，排名全球第四；马斯克当年福布斯榜单身家约1510亿美元，11月高点约3400亿美元。

那时候，一条推文就能撬动一个体量接近他身家相当比例的资产，既能获得全球关注，也能为特斯拉、支付和个人品牌制造流量。

但现在马斯克身家已经接近9000亿美元，DOGE市值只相当于其身家的1.5%左右。更重要的是，狗狗币并不完全属于马斯克，他无法控制协议、供应和大部分筹码。即使重新把DOGE喊起来，也很难直接承接其中的大部分价值。

所以从利益角度看，相比于花精力在一个旧盘子上，更高效的方式，是重新创造一个能够直接捕获价值的新叙事。

例如：

特斯拉生态币  
SpaceX或者火星概念币

这只是我的推测，目前没有证据显示马斯克准备发币。
但我不会意外，马斯克下一次重新回到加密市场时，带来的不再是狗狗币，而是一个真正属于他自己的新盘子。

text: The network thrives because it incentivizes the demand, supply, and consensus layers to work together seamlessly.
author: BitTorrent
quoted_text:
𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗲 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝗕𝗧𝗧𝗜𝗻𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗚𝗿𝗶𝗱

Building decentralized AI infrastructure is not simply about putting GPUs on a distributed network.

For a decentralized inference marketplace to work, it needs to create value for the people using compute, the people supplying it, and the participants responsible for keeping the network reliable.

That is where the core value proposition of #BTTInferGrid comes in.

It is built around three key participants:

♤ 𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗨𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀 — 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗔𝗜 𝗶𝗻𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲

Users need access to computing power without being locked into a small number of centralized cloud providers.

BTTInferGrid aims to provide lower-cost AI inference, access to globally distributed GPU resources, reduced vendor lock-in, and greater resistance to centralized control.

More distributed compute → More choice → A more open AI infrastructure.

♤ 𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗠𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀 — 𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝗱𝗹𝗲 𝗚𝗣𝗨𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲𝘀

GPUs that sit unused represent computing capacity that could otherwise contribute to the AI economy.

BTTInferGrid gives miners an opportunity to monetize idle GPU resources by contributing them to inference workloads and generating an ongoing income stream.

The model also emphasizes permissionless participation, allowing more resource providers to contribute to the network.

Idle GPU capacity → Network contribution → Potential additional income.

♤ 𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀 — 𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆

A decentralized inference network also needs mechanisms for verifying performance and maintaining reliable operations.

Validators participate in decentralized verification and scoring while helping maintain network integrity.

In return, validators can earn rewards for contributing to this coordination layer.

Verification → Accountability → Greater network reliability.

The bigger picture is that BTTInferGrid connects these three sides into one decentralized AI marketplace.

Users bring demand.

Miners provide compute.

Validators help coordinate and verify the network.

When these roles work together, computing resources can become more accessible, GPU capacity can become productive, and decentralized verification can support the integrity of the marketplace.

The goal is bigger than simply distributing GPUs.

It is about creating an open infrastructure where compute, participation, incentives, and verification can work together.

That is the core value proposition behind BTTInferGrid.

text:
I was a very fortunate kid. My dad's GP surgery sat between the Dell and Hampshire's County Ground, so at weekends I could go to a game and get a lift home afterwards. It left me with a passion for both sports and a belief that sport opens a window onto who we are.

When I was growing up, the Tebbit test was a matter of intense debate. Which side did you cheer for at the cricket? For all the criticism it received, it was a test anyone could pass. If you supported England because you saw it as home, you were part of the team regardless of the colour of your skin. Born in Southampton, 10 year old me passed it without even knowing about it.

Giving the @MCCOfficial's Cowdrey Lecture on Thursday made me think about cricket's place in our national life and the current arguments about identity.

In Britain we've built the world's most successful multi-faith, multi-ethnic democracy. I was a beneficiary of it. Whatever issues people had with me as PM (and there was no shortage) my race and religion weren't among them. I could read a lesson at the King's coronation or light Diwali diyas on Downing Street with my daughters without controversy. Foreign leaders assumed these must be huge symbolic moments. For most Brits, they just weren't that big a deal.

But Britain's democratic achievement is now under strain. Some of the challenges are ones I've written about before, like Islamism, and the failure of governments, including the one I led, to adequately control immigration. But something else is going on - a risk that we start equating skin colour with nationality.

After I left office, a debate kicked off here on @X about whether I was English at all, because I was a "brown Hindu". During the election campaign I'd been shocked when footage was broadcast of someone calling me a "Paki." It was shocking precisely because it was so unusual. That kind of abuse had simply not been a feature of my political life. But the Englishness argument was stranger still. Call it the reverse Tebbit test. If you're not white, it no longer matters who you support at the cricket, because you can never be English. It's a test no non-white person can ever pass.

I have no truck with people who offend our sense of fairness and come here illegally; I spent half my premiership trying to deport them to Rwanda. I think the bar for legal migration should be high. It is entirely possible to want a radical reduction in immigration and a far more robust approach to integration, and still totally reject the attempt to turn Britishness into a DNA test.

If you're born and brought up in England and view it as home, what are you other than English? Denying people their Englishness or their Britishness because of the colour of their skin is a recipe for alienation and a two-tier society. How are children who hear this meant to feel?

Sport can play a small but significant role here. Cricket is played by nearly every major ethnic group in this country. Ask what my largely white rural constituents in the Dales and the British-Asian kids in Bradford have in common, and the answer is cricket. If cricket can produce England teams in which every kid can see themselves, the impact reaches far beyond the boundary.

As I write in @thetimes today, we must all be on the same side, cheering for the same team.

We cannot allow race to be reintroduced into our politics. We cannot allow Briton to be set against Briton.

text:
整理别人的项目时，我也 Vibe Coding 出了 JEVia，一个在本机运行的 Agent harness。代码已经放到 GitHub，采用 MIT 许可。

一个任务进来，JEVia 会把是否联网和是否拆成多步等问题合并交给 Jev。返回的概率与程序设定的阈值比较，决定接下来走哪条路径。需要生成内容时，再调用语言模型；计划编译和工具循环也仍有语言模型参与。

多步骤任务里，Jev 会评估每一步需要的能力，本地策略再从用户配置的模型清单里挑选。任务执行到写文件时，Jev 的判断通过以后，程序还会检查文件路径，不能越过工作区边界。

欢迎体验，也欢迎到 GitHub Issues 捉虫、提建议。

text:
How to use jev, and the exact tasks where 70ms actually beats a chat model.

jev doesn't generate text. you send it unstructured state plus a set of typed questions, it returns a probability-scored answer to every question at once, in parallel, in 70 to 500 milliseconds. a comparable chat model doing the same class of task runs 3 to 329 seconds, because it's generating tokens sequentially, one at a time, even when the actual output you need is just a classification or a decision.

that gap is not universal. it only matters for a specific category of task, and knowing which category is the entire skill here.

where 70ms genuinely beats a chat model:

routing a request before it hits your actual llm call. deciding which of five prompts to use, which tool to invoke, which department a support ticket belongs to. these are typed, bounded decisions, and running them through a full chat completion is paying token generation cost for an answer that was always going to be one of a handful of options.

safety and content tagging at volume. flagging a message as needing review, scoring sentiment, checking a field against a compliance rule, anything you're currently doing with a cheap llm call purely to get a categorical answer back, wrapped in unnecessary natural language you then have to parse out again.

any high frequency decision sitting in a pipeline where latency compounds. a single 3 second chat call feels fine once. the same call run 10,000 times a day, in sequence, in front of the actual response a user is waiting on, becomes the bottleneck in your whole system.

where it doesn't help at all, and where you should still reach for a real chat model:

anything requiring the response itself to be natural language. jev never generates a sentence. it can't write your customer's email back to them, it can only decide what kind of email that customer's message needs.

anything genuinely open ended, where the set of possible answers isn't something you can define as a fixed schema in advance. jev needs typed questions with typed possible answers. a task where you don't yet know the shape of a good answer isn't a jev task.

the honest limit worth knowing. bounded, typed output can't hallucinate text, since there's no text. it can still pick the wrong option within a valid schema. this isn't a replacement for verification, it's a replacement for the specific work of deciding, cheaply and fast, which then feeds into whatever actually needs to happen next.

the actual mental model. jev is the classification and routing layer sitting in front of and around your real llm calls, not a competitor to them. use it for every decision in your pipeline that's typed and repeated. keep the chat model for everything that still needs to talk.

Now look at blockchain: every payment you make, every trade you make, everything you own is public right now. From frontier-model launches and managed agent runtimes to smart-home control and independent oversight, the period since our last edition brought major developments across the AI-agent stack.

Here’s everything worth catching up on in the latest edition of AI Agents Pulse:

1️⃣ OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, its most capable model to be broadly deployed and the first OpenAI model to reach the Critical level of cybersecurity capability under its Preparedness Framework.
https://t.co/5ZVFHmu8Zd

2️⃣ Google introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash for long-horizon coding and autonomous agents at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, alongside Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber for trusted defenders through the Fairwind Program.
https://t.co/anluNve17Q

3️⃣ OpenAI released the Agents API in public beta for all developers. Powered by the open-source Codex harness, it supports long-running sessions, MCP and other tools, and multi-agent orchestration with subagents.
https://t.co/kBhTq0lDNS

4️⃣ Meta introduced Muse, a personal agent running in a dedicated Muse Secure VM. It can browse, fill forms, keep working after the app closes, and seek approval before sending email or making purchases.
https://t.co/Cz2slZvvC0

5️⃣ Anthropic announced a redesigned Claude Code Projects beta whose coordinator scopes work, delegates to parallel cloud threads, reviews outputs, and shares project memory. Initial access is limited to select Pro and Max subscribers using cloud sessions.
https://t.co/vbpcmT0j9G

6️⃣ Google made Home MCP available in early access, letting compatible agents inspect home structures and device state, control devices, and query history. Its safeguards prohibit sensitive actions such as unlocking doors.
https://t.co/rKkyhHm4DV

7️⃣ Salesforce introduced AIforce, a live interface layer that lets agents reason and act across Salesforce data, workflows, business logic, permissions, security, and governance from interfaces including Claude and Slack.
https://t.co/3oQMVfhSdR

8️⃣ Anthropic announced a non-exclusive embedded-evaluation partnership with Accenture, led by Faculty. Each company expects to invest at least $1 billion over five years, while operating details and evaluation standards are still being worked out.
https://t.co/7pEc90KqhK

9️⃣ California Governor Gavin Newsom issued an executive order accelerating independent AI oversight and directing experts to deliver recommendations within two months, including how to advance an independently verified kill switch for frontier models. The order seeks recommendations rather than imposing a completed kill-switch mandate today.
https://t.co/mzCxgLEJEu

quoted_text:
Samsung Electronics to Double HBM4 and HBM4E Production Next Year

Samsung Electronics is expected to at least double its production of the HBM4 family next year compared with this year, including sixth generation high bandwidth memory (HBM4) and seventh generation HBM (HBM4E). This follows its plan to raise demand for "glass carriers," the glass supports that hold wafers while DRAM for HBM is thinned, to 2.5 times this year's level.

According to the semiconductor industry on the 20th, Samsung Electronics will increase its outsourced cleaning volume of glass carriers, which are essential to the HBM production process, from 20,000 units per month this year to 50,000 units per month next year. Only 10,000 glass carriers per month were needed last year, which means the volume doubles this year versus last year and rises 2.5 times next year versus this year.

A glass carrier is a support temporarily attached to the underside of a DRAM wafer for HBM to keep the wafer from warping or cracking while it is ground thin and holes are drilled through it. Because HBM must stack multiple DRAM dies within a limited thickness, wafer thinning technology and warpage control processes become more important as the stack count rises.

HBM4 and HBM4E, for which Samsung Electronics is especially preparing to expand production, center on high stack products of 12-High and above. The industry's analysis is that, even after accounting for the fact that glass carriers are reused after cleaning and that usage varies with how they are deployed at each process step and with yield, a 2.5 times increase in the related volume makes it highly likely that HBM4 and HBM4E production will be at least double this year's level.

In February this year, Samsung Electronics began mass production shipments of HBM4, which applies sixth generation 10nm class (1c) DRAM and a base die built on a 4 nanometer (nm, one billionth of a meter) process. In May, it also provided HBM4E 12-High samples to customers including Nvidia.

The industry expects Samsung Electronics' HBM production scale, measured by monthly average wafer input, to grow nearly 40% from about 180,000 wafers this year to about 250,000 wafers next year. In terms of shipment mix by product, some also forecast that the HBM4 family will rise from around 40% this year to about 80% next year as HBM4E mass production gets into full swing. An industry official explained, "As Samsung ramps up HBM production, it appears to be placing HBM4, a high value added product, at the center."

text:
This is an elitist statement. That there’s no reason to be this fast, and therefore we have to slow down!

It’s truly remarkable the level of intelligence I have available on my phone with a $200/month pro plan. However, it’s way too expensive for this to be widely available to billions of people around the world.

Tao is worried about the nonlinear nature of progress, except that technological breakthroughs, almost by definition are nonlinear. Otherwise, we would have run out of resources in the world long time ago.

People forget how recently we figured out how to produce food at today’s scale. In the 1800s, an important source of fertilizer was an island off the coast of South America. Birds had spent centuries dropping their shit there, building up deposits that people mined for fertilizer.

Then came a remarkable invention by the German scientist Haber, which Bosch helped scale industrially. By combining nitrogen from the air with hydrogen, using energy, we could manufacture ammonia for fertilizer. Fertilizer from thin air.

There’s another lesson in there about the nature of technology. The same technology that helped create an abundance of food also enabled the production of explosives at scale.

Not sure if it is normal or it is only after the Ceuta incident, but more than half the passengers on my flight to Melilla were in police-like uniforms. We were also told that the MLN/GEML authorities would not grant departure permits unless for diplomatic flights.

Because of that, I checked out of the hotel around 11 am and booked the next commercial flight to Málaga on the taxi to the airport. Iberia sells the flights between mainland Spain and Melilla under the Iberia Regional, which outsources the services to Air Nostrum, which further outsources the flights to Malta-based Mel Air.

Passengers board the ATR 72 through the rear door, and the rows were numbered from back to front. I picked seat 2F, the window seat in the last row on the right. After takeoff, a flight attendant served me a complimentary cup of coffee. The flight from Melilla to Málaga took just under an hour.

Upon arrival, I took an Uber to Universal Aviation at the airport’s general aviation terminal, where I boarded a Pilatus PC-24, registration D-CSLS, for Dublin. Several European leaders would be using Dublin Airport, so it took some effort to secure a landing slot between their flights. The flight from Málaga to Dublin took about three hours. This is my 29th arrival to the Republic of Ireland. 🇪🇸✈️🇮🇪

text:
Uniswap's weakness is being fixed.

@Uniswap has long been a successful platform, but ethereum:0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984 holders captured little of that. 

Most fees went to LPs, while ethereum:0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984 was just a governance token. It makes the protocol valuable but the token value capture weak. 

That structure has changed:

Protocol fees are on and spreading across chains and Uniswap versions.

A part of those fees can sit in TokenJar / Firepit, where ethereum:0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984 can be burned against accumulated fee assets. The loop is:

trading volume → protocol fee → revenue pool → UNI burn → tighter supply

→ That is the piece ethereum:0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984 lacked for years. 

→ If volume and share keep rising while the fee switch stays on, more of what the ecosystem earns can flow back to the token (not only to LPs and users).

The moat is also being widened:

- V4 hooks turn Uniswap into a surface other teams can build markets and liquidity designs on.
- UniswapX extends execution.
- @unichain is a chain aimed at DeFi.
- Permissioned pools open a door to RWAs and tokenized assets.

Now, @Uniswap is closer to base-layer liquidity for onchain markets (no longer an AMM).

So the UNI thesis in 2026 is much more diff compared with 2021 version.

Uniswap already had PMF, brand, depth, and a hard-to-replace liquidity network. With this upgrade, ethereum:0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984 is one of the DeFi tokens worth watching this cycle.

→ @SenatorSlotkin | Wanted stronger ethics and anti-money-laundering safeguards, plus enough staff and oversight at the agencies enforcing the rules.

→ @SenWarren | Argued the bill lacked adequate protections against political self-dealing, investor harm, and illicit finance.

→ @SenThomTillis | Switched from yes to no to preserve the option of bringing the vote back. He still supports moving CLARITY forward.

What I find interesting is that these weren’t all the same reasons, and Tillis’s vote shows why the tally alone doesn’t tell the whole story.

author: Mercy_okx
quoted_text:
今天终于和 @sunlc_crypto 面基上了😂 ，之前一起做直播时，他就分享过自己的 AI 投资思路，这次终于有机会坐下来聊得更深入：

从 AI 三大板块之间的轮动，到他为什么从微软换到 Meta、再换到谷歌，背后的判断串起来之后，有不少值得展开的地方

他把 AI 大致分成三块：硬件和半导体、云厂商与大科技、软件和应用

之前，资金集中关注硬件，是因为订单、收入、资本开支都比较直观，增长的确定性更容易被看见

但确定性强，也更容易被充分定价。如果价格已经包含了未来很高的增长预期，后面即使公司继续交出好业绩，作为投资者也需要想一想：现在的价格，比市场预期，还能好多少？

这时，他开始把目光转向花钱买算力的大科技公司

同一笔 AI 资本开支，在硬件公司的报表里是收入，在云厂商那里却是投入。市场可能一边奖励卖硬件的增长，一边担心买硬件的公司花钱太多、回报太慢

老孙关注的，就是这种预期差：这些大科技公司本身有成熟业务，如果 AI 投入逐步转化为收入和效率，市场会不会重新评价它们？

当然，这个判断也有前提。钱花出去了，不代表一定能赚回来，还得持续看变现、利润和现金流。原有业务能赚钱，也不代表新增投入没有风险。

有了这层板块判断，才是后面具体的换仓。

他提到，微软那段持仓上涨约 30% 后，他认为此前的低估已经修复了不少，于是转向当时在他看来更有性价比的 Meta。Meta 后来也涨了一轮，他又把注意力移回相对位置更低的谷歌

所以这里其实有两次比较：

先比较 AI 产业链里，哪一层的增长和价格更匹配；
再比较同一板块内，哪家公司的预期与估值更有吸引力。

但涨得少只是研究的线索。到底是被低估，还是增长确实更弱，需要回到基本面去验证。否则轮动很容易变成不断卖掉强的、换进弱的

聊到这里，梅西也想到 OKX 的「智能组合」能帮上哪一部分

大家研究之后，如果已经选好了资产和目标比例，可以用它按设定的检查周期和偏离条件做再平衡，管理涨跌带来的仓位变化。但它不会自动判断资金下一步流向哪个板块，也不会替你决定微软、Meta、谷歌谁更有吸引力

板块轮动可能需要修改目标配置，再平衡则是执行已有目标。前面的研究，决定了后面的规则有没有道理。

工具越方便，越值得把“为什么这样配”想清楚。尤其几个不同的资产，也可能都在押同一轮 AI 资本开支，看起来分散，实际承担的是相似的风险

quoted_text:
We just ran Jev on our WebMCP benchmark.

The result: basically broke the benchmark.

Jev + Mercury 2.5 (a fast, low-cost LLM) using WebMCP solved 100% of the tasks at roughly 112× lower model cost than GPT-6 Astra using computer use with code execution. Compared to Astra using screenshot-based computer use, the model cost was 245× lower (!). 

We also compared Jev operating the browser with and without WebMCP. 

We used Browser Use’s open-source Ultrafast, with some improvements to the harness to make it more reliable across the benchmark. 

Jev’s browser-control accuracy on its own was not amazing - adding WebMCP nearly doubled the number of solved tasks, from 25/49 to 49/49, while reducing model cost by 18% (more on why below).

The benchmark and methodology are fully open and reproducible.

Full results: https://t.co/KmplyFMZdv

A few words on how the Jev + WebMCP harness works and why this is exciting:

Jev receives text as input and a set of discrete options it can choose from.  With WebMCP, those options are the tools exposed by the website. At each step, Jev sees the task, the available tools and previous results, then picks what to do next.

The limitation is that Jev can’t generate arbitrary text, which you need for tool arguments. For example, it can choose the search_products tool, but it can’t generate the search query itself.

So we split the work: Jev picks the tool and Mercury 2.5 generates the arguments if needed. 

This works well because turns out most of the cognitive load in these tasks is around choosing the right action. The argument generation itself is relatively simple, so we can delegate to a small and very fast model. We used Mercury, which outputs 1,000+ tokens/sec and is very cheap.

The result is a pretty simple combination: Jev for tool selection + Mercury for arguments + WebMCP for the interface. It ends up being very reliable, very fast, and very cheap.

A few words about Ultrafast and why do we think it underperforms:

Without WebMCP, Jev chooses from the page’s controls: which button to click, which field to fill, or which option to select. 

But choosing a valid button is different from choosing the right next step. The agent still has to navigate menus, understand forms, recover from errors  and recognize when the task is actually complete.

Our hypothesis is that WebMCP makes the decision space much simpler. Instead of figuring out a sequence of clicks through a website, Jev chooses explicit actions that directly advance the task. 

@typesafeai itself documents weaker accuracy on questions requiring multiple reasoning steps. WebMCP moves much of that complexity into the website’s tools, leaving Jev with clearer decisions and fewer opportunities to go wrong (in a sense WebMCP "compresses" a sequence of clicks into one tool call).

Our modified Ultrafast setup solved 25/49 tasks - that is a result for our particular implementation and benchmark, not a universal limit on Jev or Browser Use. We are open to more harness optimization to get this result to perform better, feel free to directly contribute to the benchmark here: https://t.co/cK6MHsRV58

Browser-use ultrafast: https://t.co/DU9OdOtXHT

text:
Jev might genuinely be an “Internet moment” for AI.

TypeSafe reports up to 193x faster and 444x cheaper performance in tests with Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.

@0xCodila just wrote a great 10-page article explaining what Jev is, how to use it, and where its 100x advantage comes from.

Here are the 10 steps:

1 → LLMs create. Agents act. Jev decides the next move.

2 → Turn agent forks into three primitives: Choice, Score and probability.

3 → Build with OpenAI, Anthropic or xAI first, then swap Jev in without rebuilding the graph.

4 → Start with shared state, parallel decisions, risk thresholds and an execution queue.

5 → Batch decisions instead of making them sequentially. In one test, 13 questions were 10x faster and 12.2x cheaper.

6 → Put Jev at bounded forks: agent, model, tool, browser action or human escalation.

7 → Benchmark the whole loop, not just individual model calls.

8 → Rank wide, read narrow: shortlist first, then spend compute on what matters.

9 → Reuse the same system: State → Questions → Action → Verify.

10 → Keep Jev out of math, writing and irreversible execution. Code computes, LLMs create, Jev decides.

The result:

A slow, expensive agent loop becomes a much faster decision system that can route, score and escalate in milliseconds.

Full breakdown below ↓

text:
life is about loss.

not in a sad or pessimistic way. in a beautiful way.

as life moves forward, you lose things. you lose friends, loved ones, relationships, your parents, your youth, your hair, your teeth, your health, your possessions, your strength, your memories. and eventually, you lose your life.

but loss is what gives everything meaning.

if you knew you could keep something forever, would you ever appreciate it? would a moment feel as precious if it could never end?

even life itself is precious because it is temporary. the fact that one day it will end is precisely what makes every day worth living.

so remember, everything you have today, you will eventually lose.

not as something to fear, but as a reason to cherish it while you have it.

cherish your friends. your family. your health. your time. your experiences. every form of wealth you’ve been blessed with.

because one day, they will be gone.

and that isn’t a tragedy.

that’s what makes having them now so beautiful.

之前封号后隔了四天又去派出所喝茶了。
大体经过如下：

上午九点五分左右，我接到一个私人号码的电话让我十点去居住地街道派出所一趟。我回复说是否可以用官方座机打过来，对方问我知不知道自己在微信里面发了什么，然后拒绝了用官方座机的要求。
我便又说我稍等有个短会，十点不一定赶得过去、能否延后一小时，对方说可以。我大体上就知道事情不大了。

我首先锁定了自己的推特，取关了一些比较知名的异见者账号，并找到之前准备的旧电脑和备用手机、尽可能清理了其中所有敏感内容，换上卡简单测试了一下。

然后我跟爱人、跟一位朋友描述了情况——我之前做了什么、我即将去喝茶、我的初步判断。并表示如果十二小时后没回来、失联的话，就马上通过（在她设备上长期保留着的）该推特账号联系求助几位大概率有能力、也大概率有意愿会捞我一下的业内朋友和法律工作者。同时格式化常用电脑、销毁常用手机。
爱人提出要陪我一起去，我表示她在外面更能保护我。

走到距离派出所不到10分钟脚程的时候，我临时决定剩下的路从网约车平台打车过去，并通过行程分享功能将出发点目的地、预计到达时间发给了爱人和好友。

到了以后办公室后还有四个人在场：俩人在旁边玩手机，偶尔离开又回来；一个询问我过程、身份背景、心态（为什么要聊及相关内容）等等，一个在旁边偶尔插话询问。

这时我注意到他们也需要我来提供事情发生的时间线，而并没有完整的微信聊天记录。大概率影响太轻微，上级网警仅仅给他们转告了该账号发表了违规内容，需要做个笔录。我以事情发生在四天前、这几天在忙工作为由，以这个群我平时开着免打扰，刷的不是特别多为由，模糊了很多细节。

对方甚至不知道群主是谁、管理员是谁。我提到群主不常发言，具体是谁我不认识。我和部分群成员在线下 city walk 中见过面，但目前微信无法继续登录也无法查看具体是谁了。我是线下扫码加的群，群聊内容以本地生活和旅行为主。
我提到群管理员有制止我发图的行为，但我没来得及撤回，对方就不再问关于群聊中其他人的问题了。

对方特别问及我有没有关注 李老师。我说是通过关键词在谷歌搜索后看到、截图的，没有推特账号更不可能关注李老师。

主要负责讯问我的警察其实相对友善，旁边另一位工作人员偶尔插话并试图诈出其他“罪证”——比如谎称我发的图片上还有更具危害性的文字注解内容，我当即明确否定。可能是用了 红脸白脸 模式。

友善-恶意 程度大概率是基于图片有没有发生大规模影响或二度、三度传播。

对方问到对领导人、当局和国家有没有什么不满。我说没有，我说自己热爱这片土地和人民，强调自己亲自去大凉山给希望小学捐过钱、还即将要自己去支教。对方听到后明显更加友善了。

对方问及职业。我说自己以代写论文为生，平时就需要上 @arxiv @ResearchGate  等等下论文。对方问我是如何获取的VPN，我说是在泰国旅行期间海外朋友给的。警察问了知不知道翻墙违法，我说知道、以后不会了，就完了。

临走之际，那位表现善意的警察叮嘱我一定要像保证书中承诺的一样未来谨言慎行、我连忙答应并表示后怕，对方点点头又补充到：“这次影响不大放你一马，否则的话可是会影响你三代考公。”我差点没憋住笑。

总体上在派出所门卫签到 到 写完保证书、按完手印出来总计 40min 左右。

quoted_text:
Every @Bitget_zh user is VIP 🩵
FCN 是什麼？家印哥 @xiejiayinBitget 跟你解釋一下！

FCN 固定票息票據簡單講就是：你先設定一個你想買某支美股的「低價」，等待期間結束不管有沒有成交，都能領利息

怎麼運作？假設 $NVDA 現在 225 美元，你投 1 萬 U，設定用 9 折（202.5 美元）去接，期限一個月，利率 20%。到期只有兩種結果：

1️⃣ 股價還在 202.5 美元以上（沒跌到你要的價位）→ 拿回本金 1 萬 USDT + 利息約 167 USDT，等於沒買到股票但賺了一筆利息

2️⃣ 股價跌破 202.5 美元 → 系統直接用 202.5 美元幫你買入 NVDA 代幣（rToken），加發利息，等於用你設定的低價買到你本來就看好的股票

聽起來很棒對吧？但重點來了⋯⋯它不保本！

如果股價跌得比你設的價位還深，比如跌到 190 美元，你雖然是「用 202.5 美元便宜買到」，但當下市值其實已經低於你投入的 1 萬本金了，就算加上利息也不一定補得回來

有時候你看好某支股票，但股價還沒到你理想的位置

FCN 就是讓你先卡好想要的價格，等待的過程順便賺利息，不是把錢晾在那邊

所以這東西適合誰？你本來就真心看好某支股票、只是嫌現在太貴，願意等它回調接貨的人

如果你只是想賺高利息、根本不在乎會不會被迫買到那支股票的人，那 FCN 就不適合了，因為萬一真的跌破，你會被迫接一堆浮虧的股票！

text:
估值这东西，很多人只盯着市盈率，其实那只算了半张纸，另外半张是利率。

一笔钱到底值多少，说穿了就是把未来的现金流折回来，而折现率的锚就是无风险利率。

利率动一下，全世界所有资产的分母都得跟着重算，只是大部分人从来不看那个分母。

9 月这轮很热闹，美联储 9 月 16 日加了 25 个基点，三年多来第一次加息，联邦基金利率到 3.75-4，委员会全票通过，还说可能再加一次。三个月美债收益率 4.08，两年期 4.7，十年期一度重回 5。欧洲那边也凑热闹，欧洲央行 9 月 10 日加息，存款利率升到 2.5，而这已经是三个月内第二次加了，因为欧元区通胀冲到 3.3。

这些数字放一起，有意思的地方就出来了。

你把钱放进短期国债，什么都不干，一年拿 4 个点，这相当于约 25 倍市盈率的资产，而且这份利润永远不增长，也永远不亏。

美股整体远期市盈率 19 倍左右，收益率 5.2，跟十年期国债的 5 比，只多 20 个基点。

只比国债高一丁点，还要承担利润不及预期、股价大跌的风险。

所以指望估值继续扩张来赚钱，胜率已经很低了，接下来赚钱只能靠分子，也就是利润真的增长。

跟国债比。差得太少、生意又一般，意义不大。

差得多、而且利润还能涨，才值得认真看！
