text:
Tools vs. Graphs, clearly explained!

tools are great, and everyone is connecting more of them this month. here is the ceiling:

a tool is a hand. it lets one node reach something it could not reach before.

connect sixteen of them and you have one node that can reach sixteen places, one at a time.

the sixteenth tool did not make it faster. it made the window heavier.

Graph engineering fixes this without removing a single tool: it changes how many nodes are holding them.

you need both, and here is the sentence that resolves the whole confusion:

a tool is what one node can reach. a graph is how many nodes are reaching.

↳ more tools: one context, sixteen schemas loaded before any work starts, one call in flight
↳ a graph: four contexts, four schemas each, four calls in flight, and nothing waits on the others

Prompts → Context → Harness → Loops → Graphs

the tools do not go away when you build a graph.

they get distributed, and now four of them are being used at the same time on four things you would never have run in sequence.

the trick is giving each lane only what it needs.

a lane that audits dependencies does not need your calendar tool. 

every schema you attach to it is tokens spent before the first useful one, and context the lane has to hold while it works.

one thing to know before you scale it.

tool output is the part nobody budgets for.

↳ the schema costs you once, at the top, and it is the small half
↳ the output lands in the same window, every call, and that is the half that grows

that last one catches careful people. a grep across a large repo, a page of browser DOM, a full SQL result: three calls and the window is mostly tool output. the model is now reasoning about your goal inside whatever room is left.

and the one that eats whole nights: connecting a tool is not the same as deciding when to use it. 

sixteen tools in one window means sixteen chances to pick the wrong one, and the model has no idea which of them you actually meant for this step. the cut comes first. the tools come after.

below i have quoted my full guide on graph engineering. it covers the three topologies, the verifier patterns, and where the gate should actually open.

text:
你今年25岁。

六年前，你从斯坦福大学辍学，开始创业。这是你的第一家正式创业公司。

六年过去，你仍然没有做出一个真正成功的产品。

但你还是带着自己的新项目，坐进一家餐厅，向一个陌生人推销。

你打开手机，向他介绍 Loopt。你是这家公司的cofounder 兼 CEO，而 Loopt 想做的，是让人们看到朋友在哪里，发现附近的人、地点和活动。

你和陌生人谈到了位置共享与隐私。你认为，随着时间推移，人们会越来越习惯分享自己的位置，而位置带来的便利和社交价值，可能会超过隐私顾虑。

后来，Loopt 被 Green Dot 以 4,340 万美元收购，原有产品随后关闭。

你的第一次创业，就这样结束了。

如今，已经很少有人记得 Loopt。但对你来说，它从来不只是一款最终关闭的 App。

这段经历让你学会了如何销售，也让你明白市场不是靠创始人的热情，就能凭空创造出来的。

那时的你不会知道，这些看似与未来无关的经验，会在很久以后继续跟着你。

你更不会知道，有一天，世界各地的人会等待你谈论人工智能、工作，以及人类的未来。

你是 Sam Altman，OpenAI 的cofounder兼 CEO。

The recently disclosed FomoPeek security incident and DarkSword exploit toolkit are important reminders to keep iOS devices secure:

◾️ FomoPeek: According to SlowMist, versions 1.1–1.2 were found to contain malicious code that could exploit iOS vulnerabilities, escape the system sandbox, and access data from other apps.

◾️ DarkSword: A recently disclosed iOS exploit toolkit that could use malicious links or compromised websites to exploit unpatched vulnerabilities, gain access to a device, and extract sensitive data.

Although their attack vectors differ, both pose risks at the device and operating system level. Even if a wallet itself has no vulnerabilities, sensitive data may still be at risk on an infected or outdated device.

🛡️ To help protect your assets, we strongly recommend:

🔹 Update iOS to the latest version for your device 
🔹 Remove FomoPeek and any other suspicious apps 
🔹 Avoid unfamiliar links and untrusted websites 
🔹 Download apps only from official sources

If you installed or used FomoPeek 1.1–1.2, create a new wallet on a clean, fully updated device and transfer your assets ASAP. For additional protection against device-level risks, consider using a @KeyPalWallet hardware wallet for larger holdings.
author: TokenPocket_TP
quoted_text:
🚨 SlowMist TI Alert: FomoPeek App v1.1–1.2 Asset Theft 🚨

We have recently received multiple reports of users having assets stolen. Our investigation found that the affected cases involved private key exposure, and some of the users had previously installed and used @FomoPeek App versions 1.1–1.2.

A joint investigation by the @SlowMist_Team and @okx security teams confirmed that the app contains malicious code.⚠️

Besides its normal features, FomoPeek includes two modules that are unrelated to its stated business functions. One of them contains an #iOS kernel exploitation framework with eight different exploit methods. The framework can automatically choose an attack method based on the device model and iOS version.

‼️Affected iOS versions: iOS 12.0–18.7 and iOS 26.0–26.1.‼️

If the exploit succeeds, the app may escape the iOS sandbox, access and decrypt Keychain data, and read files belonging to other apps on the device.

🔐 This means sensitive data stored on the device, including private keys, seed phrases, login credentials, chat history, and files, may be exposed.

The app also connects to hidden servers that are unrelated to its public-facing services and can receive remote commands.

Based on plaintext traffic captured during our analysis, the attack functionality is currently enabled and runs automatically at regular intervals. In general, devices running older iOS versions are at higher risk.

If you have installed or used FomoPeek versions 1.1–1.2, we recommend that you take action immediately:

1️⃣ Check your accounts and assets for any unusual activity.
2️⃣ On a trusted device where FomoPeek has never been installed, create a new account and generate a new private key and seed phrase.
3️⃣ Move your assets to the new account as soon as possible.
4️⃣ Update your device to the latest available iOS version.
5️⃣ Do not continue using or reinstalling FomoPeek.
6️⃣ If you notice any suspicious asset activity, contact the official support team of the relevant platform and keep the affected device and related evidence for further investigation.

text:
Self-improving coding agents just got a massive upgrade.

SIFT (“Self-Improvement via Fast Tree-search”) rewrites the playbook: instead of burning thousands of dollars and days on brute-force benchmarking, it uses a language model as a judge to rapidly compare code changes, guiding search with cheap pairwise votes. Most candidates never touch a full benchmark—only the most promising get the expensive test.

Results: On Polyglot-225, SIFT lifts accuracy from 14% to 35.1% in under 50 CPU-hours and <$150, beating previous bests while using 1/10th the compute. On TerminalBench 2.1, it finds agents scoring 36.7% (vs 29.2% baseline), and generalizes across model families. Judge signals (ρ≈0.68–0.72 with true accuracy) let it move fast without sacrificing quality.

The bottom line: SIFT turns recursive AI self-improvement from a niche for big labs into a practical tool—now you can run a full cycle on a single workstation overnight.

text:
The Economist says AI created a million jobs in America.

I read that twice.

Then I found out who's getting hired and it made total sense.

For two years the only headline was the same one. AI is coming for your job. Learn to code was dead. Entry level was finished. Everyone under thirty was about to be replaced by a chatbot.

So The Economist did the thing nobody else bothered to do. They actually counted.

They lined up every job AI created against every job it killed. The layoffs first, because that's the part everyone was waiting for.

About 200,000 jobs gone since mid 2023. Real people, real pink slips, companies openly blaming AI. Customer service down around 10 percent. Admin and secretary roles down about 15. That part of the fear was true.

Then they counted the other side.

Around a million new jobs. Five made for every one destroyed.

I sat with that number for a second because it's the exact opposite of what I'd been told to expect. Then I looked at where the jobs actually went, and the whole thing clicked.

The biggest winners of the AI boom don't touch a keyboard.

They're electricians.

Here's the part nobody explains. AI doesn't live in the cloud. The cloud is a lie we tell ourselves. AI lives in enormous buildings full of computers that run hot enough to cook an egg, and those buildings have to be built, wired, cooled, and fed more power than a small city.

So the money went there.

Around 320,000 more jobs than normal in the industries that build these things. Electricians. HVAC techs. The people who wire electrical equipment. Utility crews. Companies are so desperate for them that data center jobs pay about 40 percent more than the same work anywhere else.

The white collar side grew too. Roughly 730,000 above trend in the jobs sitting closest to AI. Engineers, software people, data scientists, plus a wave of roles that didn't exist three years ago like the people who label training data and the ones who bolt these systems into real companies.

Even the jobs everyone said were doomed kept growing. Paralegals up 11 percent. Market research analysts up 6. The national average was around 2.

Now the honest part, because I'm not here to sell you a fairy tale.

This is an estimate, not a government census. Nobody at the Bureau of Labor Statistics stamped a form that says one million AI jobs. The Economist built the number from employment trends and some careful guessing, and the two sides aren't perfectly comparable. The layoffs are announced cuts. The million is jobs above where the trend line said we'd be.

And "created by the AI boom" is doing heavy lifting. An electrician wiring a data center is real work. It is not AI hiring a million prompt engineers.

But strip all of that away and one thing survives.

The apocalypse everyone promised is two years late. The thing that was supposed to erase work quietly built a small city's worth of it instead.

We spent two years scared of the wrong number.

text:
Had an interesting discussion this week while allocating on why new, shiny memes plus the stock-backed plays are outperforming legacy ones right now.

Looking at the past week, 2 categories of meme coin have done well and likely keep doing well:

1) Stock-based or "valuable-backed" plays. Anything people can convince themselves is backed by something real. This has genuinely interesting reflexivity built in, since the backing narrative and the price action reinforce each other.

2) New memes tied to a current main character, cult around the person becomes cult around the meme. Cate, Ansem earlier, Useless with Uni sitting at the top of the FOMO PnL board. Social apps are now crowning main characters faster than ever, which feeds directly into this loop.

Once the market sees categories 1 and 2 outperform, you get the reflexive "last hot asset" loop. People just keep bidding what already worked, which is exactly what makes 1 and 2 the de facto meta over legacy plays, rather than any inherent quality difference in the coins themselves.

text:
Fomo明明交易体验路边一条，为什么仍然这么牛逼

因为meme赚钱和合约/预测市场/二级概念的“交易水平”
根本不是同一个东西

大币二级/预测市场/合约赌的是价格预测
你再喊单都不会改变特朗普当选总统的概率和明天油价

妖币二级判断的是对手盘，庄家意图
你喊单可以增加一些对手盘
但操盘资金体量太大了
喊来了也不见得是你在赚

但meme不一样
只要你位置够低
那在你入场后但凡有人接盘
你跑的快就一定等于你赚钱

所以meme的包赢技术就是两点：
>进的足够低
>足够能喊

这个喊不一定非要是传统意义上的喊单
在链上有影响力实名买入就是喊单
影响力决定跟单多寡
跟单决定你的确定性盈利

如果你没有这两样能力
那么你赌的就是预测能喊的人
在你进场后还能不能喊来人

二圣/Vlad/特朗普/马斯克
或者抽象点的共识/叙事
本质上都是在描述同一个东西
但都不直接
不包赢
包赢就是：买的低喊得动

Meme的本质是CX，而不是交易

你每喊一个跟单都是实质上的账面收益
就好比盘子的业绩拨比

战壕本质上就是一个CX的销售体系
每个实名账号就是社区长
通过Fomo这类社交交易产品的“Thesis和算法”
把战壕里的流动性高效引导

如同抖音直播带货一样
告诉散户流动性该往哪儿集中
毕竟散户只会买他们注意力看到的东西
同时让社区长无责任的赚无限代

同样的道理这也是为什么
所有链的行情最终都会走向分流
因为分流对分流的人来说是正EV
PVE是短暂幻觉
PVP才是长期纳什均衡

很多KOL当时鼓吹
meme已死
链上能买美股谁买meme
实际情况是各大发射台、交易终端等meme基建
收入常常超越Hyperliquid

他们不理解为什么meme现在还没死
认为这一定是阴谋
是交易所VC大KOL在作祟
唯独没有意识到这是市场的选择

Meme基业长青才是正常的
只有基业长青才能被大多数人当事业
交易会分牛熊市
但销售行业最多有个淡旺季

对我们这些项目方的启示
是搞盘子
不能一句笼统的“做赌行“就完了
要理解为什么它作为一个实业可以长青
一定要做普通人能靠自己改变收益结果的盘子
销售>交易

毕竟
极致的自律者
伟大的算命先驱
气运之子

在全球人口中是一个很低的比例

Base生态的币股生态，应该关注什么？

Base 目前 DeFi TVL 约 59 亿美元，稳定币规模约 51 亿美元，过去 30 天 DEX 成交约 281 亿美元。

Coinbase 的 B20 币股 8 月 24 日上线，30 天成交已经突破 10 亿美元。

而作为Base生态的龙头DEX Aerodrome ，过去 30 天成交约 140 亿美元，差不多吃掉 Base 全链一半现货。

到了币股这个细分市场，10 亿美元成交里约 8.53 亿发生在 Aero，占了约 85%。

作为Base生态的龙头币股meme发射台  STONKEX，目前累计成交已经突破 5000 万美元。平台的发射币每笔交易收 1%：0.7% 给创建者，0.3% 给平台，其中平台收入的 80% 用来回购销毁 base:0x5ab000ff9b9ffe0349ce5ffa5fd86f217c3680f5 。

目前销毁量已经超过总供应的 8%。现在 STONKEX 池又正式拿到了 AERO 排放资格，接下来 V2 如果把更多发射后的流动性迁到 Aero，这两套系统就真正接上了。

所以我现在看 Base 币股，会有三层：

B20 负责把 NVDA、AAPL、META 这些真实资产搬上链。

AERO 负责吃交易量和流动性。

STONKEX 再把股票变成 Meme 的报价资产，吃最投机、周转最高的那部分流量。

以上大概就是Base生态币股最核心的数据了。

tonight the four are killed, the population reaches 69, and this phase of the game officially concludes.

now the important part, survivors:

your share of the treasury does not move on its own. claiming is a pull function. it does not happen automatically. you go to the site and you claim it yourself. there is exactly one place to do this: https://t.co/emEKYMHQrE. anyone who sends you anywhere else is trying to steal your hard earned eth.

thank you to everyone who played, watched, doubted, screamed, accused, and stayed. all of it was participation. all of it is in the work.

to the 69: you outlived a world. survived 201 grueling days. you will soon collect what the world owes you.

text:
People pay too little attention to something I would call “Asset Weight” (heaviness or lightness of an asset).

The idea behind Asset Weight is essentially: “How much money does it take to move things in one direction or another? How heavy or light is the asset relative to flows.” 

When you understand Asset Weight, especially in relation to a few other factors, you understand the chess board much better. You understand risk better. You understand your own ability to participate in and shape things better. You understand asymmetry better. 

Asset Weight on its own doesn’t mean much. You need to marry it with Asset Level Belief (holders + duration), Memetics (spread of belief), and Flows (an offset to weight).

These are the essentially the core ingredients of the game theory of markets.

This is not subjective. They can all be quantified and experienced.

用自己一个小损失再分享一次关于“套利”的内容。劝诫一下那些总觉得自己在套利，实际在赌博的朋友。

事情起因是昨晚5点我还没睡，在客厅抽烟，公司小伙伴在群里发了一个可以套利的G，截图推特内容大意是，项目方看到交易所价差了，准备解决。出于对小伙伴的信任，我也没多想，就开始一笔5万刀的挂单。然后成交了一部分的时候，我光速意识到不对了，价差为什么没收敛，我的挂单凭什么能成交。然后我就开始去check，让ai去check了当天历史价差，然后去套利群里找到了一些ok会一直延迟erc提现的消息。我马上就确定这绝对不是套利了，这是赌博。不过由于成交的很少，就2w多刀，我也懒得管，就缺睡觉了。早上起来喜提8000刀亏损吧。

其实我的爆仓价是几百倍，狗庄搞不到我的，但我还是起床后第一时间止损了，不会选择扛单的，因为你套利的时候永远要记住，你套的是确定性，不是赌博。即使他只有5%的可能性能拉10倍，但你要想的永远是拉10倍的后果你能不能承受。价差会回归吗？一定会的。价差回归之前你可能的亏损是多少？没人知道。

其实我做错的地方在于，没有发现后立刻止损，因为开的少了就没管直接睡觉去了。其实不是这样的，我在桌子上有个纸条，上面写的是，套利之前想清楚，在套谁的利。如果你想不清楚，你就是那个利。永远不要因为金额少而随意。

币圈也迭代到现在了，21年套利日化1%那种好日子早就一去不返了，现在就我观察到的，90%的人做的90%的事只是美其名曰套利，实际就是赌博。没什么意思，就像这个代币，醒来后去看了下币安的持仓。畜生项目方就是在钓鱼，发张图你们就知道了。然后我弟还和我说，早上起来他看ok 0.008挂了300w刀的货，都被人吃完了。也是在钓鱼。我觉得后面他持仓跑不掉的话，被套的人要小心adl。如果继续硬拉，就用负费率搞人。非常非常明显的操纵了，这些玩意我实在太熟悉了。我建议这些傻逼做市之前聘请我来当顾问，我感觉我能骗持仓骗的比他们好。

text:
Orbital Data Center cost takes by Street analysts making the rounds: 
Wood Mac ~$170B/GW, 
BofA $160B to 180B, 
Futurum ~$72B (infrastructure alone), 
BNP >$100B just for launch to loft 1 GW. 
This is all the same spreadsheet genre that “proved” Starlink couldn’t work in comparison to classical Data Centers at $40B-$60 on the ground. 
However, we now know that Starlink worked because: 
(a) SpaceX’s real Falcon 9 cost was nowhere near list price, and 
(b) V2/V3 satellites blew past the bandwidth per satellite that those early models assumed. 
Starlink satellites kept outrunning the forecast and internal launch costs ran way below analysts estimates.
AI satellites will rhyme. 
Gen-1 is what the cost models price. 
Gen-2 and Gen-3 (better chips, power, and thermal per kg) are where we once again pull away from the spreadsheet.
Starship does the launch cost side slide in short order. @Mach33 is the most comprehensive analysis on Data Centers in the sky. Here are their estimates: 
Starship AI launches, with booster reuse and ship expendable cost at ~$300/kg. 
That would give us: 
~$46B per GW for SpaceX, then 
toward ~$24B/GW over the next decade with Ship reuse. 
Bull case with full reuse and better chips goes lower.
In summary: actual cost likely to start at $46B per GW (and the falling to half that) vs $160B+ headlines from "analysts". 
Add to that less permitting delays and less political pushback than a GW on the ground. 
Starlink redux. 
Bears beware.

text:
We tried to make our production AI agents improve themselves the obvious way: fine-tune the model on its own verified experience.

One $54 LoRA. It got better at what we trained: recovery after a rejected tool call 31/73 → 38/73, seven wins, zero losses, p = 0.0156. It also moved what we didn't train: clean decisions 49/73 → 45/73, three up, seven down, p = 0.34.

At n = 73 you can't tell −4 from noise. The gate we wrote before training allows −2. It fired. Rejected.

Lesson: one weight update gives you a gain and a possible loss in the same artefact. You can't separate them. You can't reverse one without the other.

So we stopped asking the model to improve itself and built a system that improves around the model:

A verified failure improves memory (agent writes it, in the turn), tools and skills (engineers, code review), evaluators (a frozen case in the next suite), and the training curriculum (only if it recurs). A better worker makes better trajectories. That's the recursion.

Fast memory: 433 rules across 74 workspaces, 3,422 memory files, editable, provenanced, reversible by moving a line. No weights.

Slow weights: repeated patterns → frozen 484-decision suite → 9-condition gate → 6-condition production gate → shadow → promote. First candidate rejected by its own gate.

DeepSeek's Engram separates memory from computation inside the model. We do the same one layer up, at fleet scale, in text. Complementary, not competing.

Fast memory. Slow weights. The system learns continuously. The model changes rarely.

Iran and the Houthis have kept escalating, targeting the routes everyone else needs to keep open. Pressure on Hormuz makes Saudi Arabia’s pipeline to the Red Sea more important. text:
油价是决定加息路径的关键变量，能源冲击是核心扰动。这是高盛GBM系列播客 《The Breaks of the Game》的最新一集核心观点。这期是高盛对冲基金业务全球主管Tony Pasquariello主持，高盛研究部高级顾问Dominic Wilson与全球风险主管Josh Schiffrin主要分享。他们认为市场目前定价的约四次累计加息"明显偏多"，两人均认为本轮加息周期实际落地次数更可能为两次。
两人均指出，油价走势是决定最终加息路径的关键变量，一旦油价出现实质性回落，将为全球多类资产提供同步走强的条件。跟我之前很多观点一致性很类似，详细梳理下。

这期播客核心内容要点，
1、加息路径：市场定价“四次”明显偏多，两人更看好两次
市场当时已定价本轮累计约四次加息（一个较完整的紧缩周期）。两人认为这明显过头。基准情形是10月再加一次，然后进入较长时间暂停。实际风险更可能是各央行加息力度不及市场预期；

2、油价是决定加息路径的关键变量
油价大涨被两人视为今年最大的市场意外，持续推高通胀预期，也让市场对加息路径定价越来越激进。一旦油价出现实质性回落，通胀压力会缓解，加息必要性下降，并为全球多类资产同步走强创造条件。油价回落也被视为债市最可能的催化剂；

3、债市：长端实际利率已处多年罕见高位，利空消化较多，但还需催化剂
10年期美债约5%、30年期实际利率超过3%，是相当长时间未见的水平。财政赤字、通胀粘性等利空已被市场消化不少，估值吸引力上升。但在AI资本开支融资需求、财政赤字和增长韧性没有实质性变化前，收益率大幅下行空间有限。需要油价下跌这类偏多头催化剂，买家才会更积极回归；

4、股市：韧性超预期，当前是近期较清晰的做多窗口之一
尽管油价飙升、收益率上行、AI不确定性存在，股市仍展现超预期韧性。原因主要是大规模资本开支周期和实体经济增长依然强劲。当前点位已计入较悲观情景（四次加息、高收益率、油价超100美元），因此“看到缓解路径变得容易得多”。Wilson 将此时点描述为近期多头侧较清晰的做多窗口（虽不如7月底那么好，但感觉类似），可用低成本期权做保护或博取上行。

5、宏观与美联储会议后环境
9月FOMC后，短期政策不确定性下降，被视作配置窗口。增长仍有韧性（约2%），劳动力市场好于部分预期。通胀仍高于目标，但能源冲击是核心扰动。AI、财政赤字和资本竞争推高了实际利率，若没有AI capex转向或增长意外下行，鸽派转向空间有限。

6、高盛年底交易思路
1）美元：受美联储相对鹰派、美国经济领先支撑，倾向走强。
2）“全资产上涨”窗口：若中期选举后油价下行，可能出现股债商品等同步走强的交易机会，但需要油价下跌作为催化剂。
3）超长端高实际收益率：中长期仍有配置价值。
4）利率定价：对年底前加息定价向下修正越来越有信心，倾向用低成本期权结构参与。

这跟个人之前观点很类似，是油价再决定市场近期的走势，油价回落叠加基本面还是很强势，支撑本周后半周市场上行。后续还是要看油价走势： https://t.co/R8noHp3Gme

把这三张图放在一起看，就能清晰看到是谁在影响市场走势，核心是油价。只要油价在下行，即使沃什放鹰导致US10y跳涨纳指暂短下跌，但很快就回到了受油价驱动的轨道上来。所以并不是什么加息利空还是利好之类的论点，因为都站不住脚。核心要去看为什么加息？因为通胀。为何通胀反弹或者下降慢？至少今年内都是油价导致的。长债收益率走高有相当一部分原因也是油价。这也是8月下旬在“收益率高中枢时代的结构性问题”的推文https://t.co/1Zk9fGfdda里聊到的“长债走高的三个驱动因素：油价、财政赤字发债、AI基建科技公司发债潮，最后就要下油价上下功夫”。

期待下周的两场会晤有一个好的结论，这个结论自然是川普做出实质性让步，这次可能沙特也要让步，伊朗和胡塞才能收手。关于让步的程度之前这里https://t.co/L533aRqZCZ有聊过。

当然还要看明天日本央行的动作，加息是确定的，核心还是对后续节奏的表述，日本央行的表态则可能决定市场会出现估值波动，还是叠加更强的杠杆平仓。当谈油价走势还是当下市场首要因素。

text:
The diesel crisis is increasingly a refining-capacity problem, not a crude-supply problem

Everyone focused on crude when the Persian Gulf war began.

But crude flows have already recovered to about 60% of pre-war Middle East levels.

Diesel hasn’t.

The real bottleneck is refining.

Gulf refineries were damaged. Russian plants were hit. Diesel exports from Russia + the Gulf collapsed.

And the system was already short capacity before the war because older refineries had been closed and very little new capacity was being built.

So there are really two problems:

Restore the refining capacity lost to war.
Then replace the capacity that was already missing before it.
Neither has a good near-term solution.

You can have enough crude and still not have enough diesel.

The diesel crisis is increasingly a refining-capacity problem, not a crude-supply problem.

Crude flows from the Middle East have already recovered to about 60% of pre-war levels, helped by alternative routes and U.S.-protected shipping. That may sound encouraging, but it does little to solve the real bottleneck: converting crude into diesel.

The war knocked out Gulf refining capacity just as Ukrainian attacks and Russian export restrictions were removing another major source of middle distillates. Combined diesel exports from Russia and the Gulf are now down roughly two-thirds from 2025 levels.

And this system was not starting from abundance. COVID accelerated decisions to close or rationalize older refineries whose economics already looked poor in a world of slower oil-demand growth, environmental pressure and weak investor appetite for long-lived downstream assets. Very little new large-scale refining capacity has been added outside a handful of exceptional projects such as Dangote.

That creates two separate problems:

Restore the capacity lost to war.
Even that may take years because damaged Gulf plants need specialized equipment, engineering and materials that are already scarce. Russian repairs are even harder under sanctions.
Replace the capacity the world had already lost before the war.
That is a structural problem with no quick commercial solution.

Global refinery throughput is expected to average only 81.5 mb/d this year versus about 84 mb/d in 2025, while available spare capacity is limited and refiners elsewhere are already running hard.
So the market can recover crude supply and still remain short diesel.

That is the uncomfortable part: the barrel exists, but the refining system needed to turn it into the molecule the economy wants does not.

text:
大开眼界，跑完交易回测算法，我见识到了 Jev 交易决策的效率和质量，况且只是简单地跑了几个算法，77 天收益率高达 +6.71%。

跑完之后剩一个问题：这一堆 JSON 怎么给人看？

我把可视化设计稿丢给蚂蚁百灵刚开源的 Ling-3.0-flash-VL，让它照着写前端，最后输出视频。

我没给它设计稿标注，也没给它组件库。它自己看图，直接构建出动态仪表盘页面：净值曲线、三个策略的持仓条、当日决策流、右上角的加速倍数。然后它用 playwright 逐帧截图，390 帧压成 13 秒，浓缩了 95 天的新闻与行情。

说到具体的方法论：我把 NewsHub 攒了三个月的投资日报，一天一份丢给 OpenRouter 上的 Jev 1.13。我给它当天的日报和当前持仓，它能迅速输出每个标的买、卖还是不动，附带三个选项的概率和置信度。后面的程序拿着这些概率去调仓、按 Binance 真实小时级别 K 线成交、算净值、对账。

77 天，3 个策略（动量、逆向、宏观），5 个标的（BTC / ETH / SPY / QQQ / XAU），1155 个决策。全程只花了 $0.09（Ling-3.0-flash-VL目前在OpenRouter免费😺），跑完 87 秒，单次调用 1.1 秒，零次失败。

当然，现在还远没到干死基金经理的程度。动量策略 +6.71%，但同期等权买入持有是 +13.2%，它没跑赢。而另外两个策略表现比较拉胯，一个 −1.0%，一个 −10.3%。

🔥 Jev 和多模态 Ling-3.0-flash-VL，一个负责判断，一个负责看懂和展示。
Ling-3.0-flash-VL 总参数 124B，但 MoE 每 token 只激活约 5.5B。

这对 Visual Agent 很重要，极为广阔的知识，以及极低的激活，能做到又快又好。

OpenRouter现在可以免费使用Ling-3.0-flash-VL：

text:
Yes, and this pattern has persisted for millennia. More than any other group, Jews have historically been maneuvered into the sacrificial position — not because of anything they did, but because accusations repositioned them within the game.

What I call sacrificial positioning is the game‑theoretical process by which groups maneuver to ensure they end up on the side of the accusers rather than the accused. Within this dynamic, accusations become tools of elevation. To accuse is to rise. To accuse falsely is to rise even higher, because it demonstrates one’s power to shape the moral landscape without constraint.

Robert Ian Moore deserves all credit for identifying the historical core of this dynamic. In his analysis of medieval persecution, Moore showed that the act of accusation itself — not the truth of the accusation — is the mechanism by which societies create hierarchies of vulnerability. The accused becomes the sacrificial candidate; the accuser becomes elevated. The truth — and even rationality — becomes largely irrelevant. What matters is the shift in position within the social game.

Palestinians have committed severe and deliberate acts of violence with exultant cruelty — to a degree that their actions categorically cannot be understood as rational bargaining. Yet many commentators insisted on treating even deliberate and profoundly sadistic acts of their violence — including sexual violence — as ‘grievances’ within a ‘conflict.’

This inaugurates the endpoint of a collapse in their system of thought, which dissolves humanism. When academics treat expressive sexual violence — cruelty enacted with exultation, cruelty performed as ritual — as a negotiable grievance, they reintroduce the sacrificial machinery under the guise of a so-called ‘rules-based order.’ They weaponize communicative rationality, ultimately making everything negotiable — including sadistic expressive violence aimed at self-confirmation.

In effect, they are saying: Even the violation of women dancing barefoot in the sand at a music festival can be reframed as a political grievance.

This inevitably marks the return of the ancient pattern of sacrificial positioning, where the truth of accusations does not matter. What matters now is only how accusations reposition actors within the social game. And this is why, after October 7, accusations against Jews proliferated — not because of evidence, but because accusation itself elevates the accuser.

quoted_text:
大开眼界，跑完交易回测算法，我见识到了 Jev 交易决策的效率和质量，况且只是简单地跑了几个算法，77 天收益率高达 +6.71%。

跑完之后剩一个问题：这一堆 JSON 怎么给人看？

我把可视化设计稿丢给蚂蚁百灵刚开源的 Ling-3.0-flash-VL，让它照着写前端，最后输出视频。

我没给它设计稿标注，也没给它组件库。它自己看图，直接构建出动态仪表盘页面：净值曲线、三个策略的持仓条、当日决策流、右上角的加速倍数。然后它用 playwright 逐帧截图，390 帧压成 13 秒，浓缩了 95 天的新闻与行情。

说到具体的方法论：我把 NewsHub 攒了三个月的投资日报，一天一份丢给 OpenRouter 上的 Jev 1.13。我给它当天的日报和当前持仓，它能迅速输出每个标的买、卖还是不动，附带三个选项的概率和置信度。后面的程序拿着这些概率去调仓、按 Binance 真实小时级别 K 线成交、算净值、对账。

77 天，3 个策略（动量、逆向、宏观），5 个标的（BTC / ETH / SPY / QQQ / XAU），1155 个决策。全程只花了 $0.09（Ling-3.0-flash-VL目前在OpenRouter免费😺），跑完 87 秒，单次调用 1.1 秒，零次失败。

当然，现在还远没到干死基金经理的程度。动量策略 +6.71%，但同期等权买入持有是 +13.2%，它没跑赢。而另外两个策略表现比较拉胯，一个 −1.0%，一个 −10.3%。

🔥 Jev 和多模态 Ling-3.0-flash-VL，一个负责判断，一个负责看懂和展示。
Ling-3.0-flash-VL 总参数 124B，但 MoE 每 token 只激活约 5.5B。

这对 Visual Agent 很重要，极为广阔的知识，以及极低的激活，能做到又快又好。

OpenRouter现在可以免费使用Ling-3.0-flash-VL：

author: alexisohanian
quoted_text:
Legendary companies rarely scale in a linear fashion. When you look at the greatest companies and founders, you’ll find that they bypassed consistency and took leaps forward at various points along their journey, despite differences in their values, leadership style, and path to success. 

These leaps take vision, inspiration, conviction, strategy, energy, and, most importantly, action. You have to know where you’re aiming, commit with conviction, and then stick the landing.

Every leap starts with a leader. A leader must be fearless to take leaps and needs to inspire the team to follow. The CEO has to be the most fearless and push the company to solve the boldest and hardest problems and shape their business and industry.

In addition, leaders need to be right a lot. While they have often made plenty of mistakes, they also have strong judgment and good instincts. They seek diverse perspectives and work to disconfirm their beliefs. As @JensenHuang has said, "no one wants to follow a dumb CEO with a bad strategy."

BP is out of scope of SEC's innovation exemption.

Backpack’s stock tokens are not security entitlements. They are tokenized claims on the underlying assets.

They may be redeemable 1:1 for real shares, but that does not mean the tokens themselves carry the same legal rights as the underlying shares.

author: 100y_eth
quoted_text:
A lot of people are misreading the SEC’s new Innovation Exemption for tokenized stocks.

The market seems to be treating this as a blanket green light for anything related to “tokenized equities.”

It isn’t. The SEC’s exemption is much narrower.

The framework allows 

- qualifying Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) to facilitate trading of tokenized NMS stocks through permissioned AMMs without registering as traditional exchanges.

- Certain liquidity providers can also receive conditional relief from dealer registration.

But the key is what actually counts as a “tokenized NMS stock.” The SEC basically recognizes two relevant models:

1. Issuer-native tokenization

- The company itself, or someone acting on its behalf, tokenizes the actual stock.
- Think of a transfer agent recording the actual shares onchain.
- The token Itself is the security, not a wrapper that merely tracks it.

2. Third-party custodial tokenization

- A third party holds the underlying stock within the traditional securities system and tokenizes the investor’s ownership interest / security entitlement.
- Again, the important part is that the token holder must receive the same rights and privileges as a holder of the equivalent traditional stock.
- That explicitly includes things like dividends and voting rights.

What does NOT qualify? → Synthetic exposure.

If a third party issues its own note, derivative, tracker certificate, security-based swap, etc. whose value simply tracks AAPL or NVDA, that instrument is not a “tokenized NMS stock” under this exemption.

This distinction matters because the market reaction has been much broader than the actual SEC framework. Anything vaguely connected to tokenized stocks or onchain trading got bid.

$BP, $ONDO, $HYPE, $LIT and other adjacent names were swept into the narrative, even though their exposure to the exemption is very different.

$ONDO at least has a legitimate connection: Ondo has been moving toward custodial tokenization structures where underlying securities remain within regulated custody while corresponding onchain tokens represent rights tied to those securities.

But HYPE or LIT equity perps? Those are derivatives. They are not what the SEC just exempted.

And this brings us to Backpack.

$BP rallied hard as the market started viewing Backpack as one of the obvious winners from tokenized U.S. equities.

The common thesis seems to be:

“Backpack tokens are redeemable 1:1 for real shares, therefore they are real-equity tokens, therefore the SEC exemption directly benefits Backpack.”

That skips an important legal distinction. Backpack itself describes the two forms very clearly:

Traditional Backpack securities:
→ UCC Article 8 security entitlement

Backpack tokens on Solana:
→ “Tokenized claim”
→ Claim on an SPV holding the underlying assets

Those are NOT the same legal instrument. When you withdraw a traditional Backpack stock position onchain, you are not simply moving the existing Article 8 security entitlement onto Solana.

The security entitlement is converted into a different tokenized instrument.

That token can later be redeemed 1:1 through Backpack Securities and converted back into the corresponding traditional security entitlement.

This is actually a meaningful improvement over many existing stock-token structures.

xStocks, for example, are bearer debt instruments / tracker certificates backed 1:1 by underlying shares.

Robinhood’s Classic Stock Tokens are derivatives against Robinhood Europe and explicitly do not give holders ownership rights in the underlying stock.

Backpack goes further because its token can be redeemed 1:1 into an actual traditional share position / security entitlement.

But redeemability ≠ the token itself being the underlying equity.

And that distinction matters for the SEC exemption.
The SEC does not merely require 1:1 backing or 1:1 redemption.

A tokenized NMS stock traded under the exemption must provide the holder the same rights and privileges as the corresponding traditional stock, including voting rights.

Backpack’s current documentation describes the Solana token as a “tokenized claim” designed to maintain economic equivalence with the underlying security.

It does not describe that token itself as an Article 8 security entitlement or as carrying the full shareholder rights required by the SEC framework.

So I would not classify Backpack’s current stock token structure as a direct beneficiary of the Innovation Exemption.

Could Backpack build a compliant structure around the exemption later? Absolutely. But that is different from saying its existing tokens already fit it.

The infrastructure that is much more directly aligned with what the SEC just described looks more like:

- @SuperstateInc: issuer-native shares recorded onchain through a registered transfer-agent model.
- @Securitize: issuer-sponsored tokenized shares and transfer-agent infrastructure.
- @Figure: blockchain-native registered public equity.
- @The_DTCC: tokenization of DTC-custodied securities with identical legal and ownership rights.
- @DinariGlobal: custodial tokenized equities designed to preserve the rights of the underlying securities.
- @Ondo: moving toward custodial tokenization models tied more directly to securities held inside the regulated custody chain.

I’m writing this because I’ve seen a lot of confusion in the community about what the exemption actually covers and which existing products legally fit that definition today.

Either way, the SEC’s latest announcement is undeniably a major positive for the tokenized equity ecosystem as a whole.

text:
If you're a developer trying to break into AI, here's a project you'd build

An AI agent that turns GitHub issues into tested pull requests.
Not just code generation.
The workflow could be..
Issue → understand the repo → find relevant code → plan the change → implement → run tests → investigate failures → generate PR

Now the project forces you to learn the stuff that actually matters in agent engineering
LLM APIs
tool calling
code search
GitHub APIs
agent state
sandboxed execution
evals
observability
security
And you can measure it.
How often does it solve the issue?
How many tool calls does it need?
How often does it get stuck?
How much does each task cost?
How often do humans have to intervene?
That's much more interesting than building another chatbot.
You also end up with a portfolio project that demonstrates actual AI engineering rather than just API integration.
Build something that can do work, then measure how reliably it does that work.

text:
疯狂看多 CX 能到什么程度？

之前选择重仓梭哈 ZEC 的交易员 @TaikiMaeda2 ，在最新一期播客中，进一步离谱的看多： $ZEC 的牛市目标可以看到 20,000 美元，而我们现在可能还处在「狂暴牛市」的早期。

目标价过于夸张了，但他为什么敢在 ZEC 上下这么重的注？以及什么时候准备撤退，这才是值得大家借鉴的事情。

里面几个核心观点：

1️⃣ ZEC 不是普通山寨，而是「隐私版 BTC」

Taiki 认为，BTC 早期一直面临可编程性、扩展性和隐私三个问题，ETH、SOL 吃到了前两个方向的红利，而 ZEC 押注的是隐私。

目前 ZEC 市值只有 BTC 的约 1.8%～1.9%。历史上 LTC 曾达到 BTC 的 8%，BCH 甚至长期处于 10%～20% 区间。
所以他的算法非常简单：

BTC = $100k
ZEC = BTC 市值的 5% → 约 $5,000
ZEC = BTC 市值的 20% → 约 $20,000

2️⃣ ZEC 越涨，基本面反而越强

他的核心逻辑是「反身性」。

ZEC 价格上涨 → 屏蔽池价值变大 → 能容纳更多财富 → 隐私效果和实际用途增强 → 吸引更多资金进入。

所以在 Taiki 看来，价格本身就是 Zcash 基本面的一部分。

3️⃣ 真正应该承担风险的时候，是所有人都觉得危险的时候

Taiki 认为，当市场充满恐慌、大家握着现金不敢买时，感知风险最高，但实际风险可能反而最低。

等 BTC 突破关键位置、所有人重新宣布「牛市回来了」并开始加杠杆时，反而应该逐渐减仓。

他的原则是：牛市前 10%～30% 阶段承担最多风险，越往后风险敞口越小。

4️⃣ ZEC 怎么止盈？看它占 BTC 市值的比例

Taiki 用的是「下一个 2 倍」框架：

1% → 2%，容易
2% → 4%，仍然可以
4% → 8%，难度明显增加
8% → 16%，越来越难

因此他的第一目标是 ZEC 达到 BTC 市值的 3%～4%，届时先卸掉杠杆、留下现金，现货继续持有。

5️⃣ 赢家摊平赢家，不要给输家补仓

这也是整期我觉得最值得记住的一句话。

Taiki 的交易哲学不是追求高胜率，而是追求「长打率」：错的时候小亏，对的时候重仓吃完整趋势。

用他自己的话说：「把所有鸡蛋放进一个篮子，然后死死盯住它。做一头有勇气的猪。」

当然，他目前持有 $ZEC $HYPE $LIT 等仓位，部分还使用了杠杆，所以这些极其乐观的目标价首先应该理解为一个屁股决定脑袋的重仓者的交易框架，而不是价格预言。

text:
A lot of people are misreading the SEC’s new Innovation Exemption for tokenized stocks.

The market seems to be treating this as a blanket green light for anything related to “tokenized equities.”

It isn’t. The SEC’s exemption is much narrower.

The framework allows 

- qualifying Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) to facilitate trading of tokenized NMS stocks through permissioned AMMs without registering as traditional exchanges.

- Certain liquidity providers can also receive conditional relief from dealer registration.

But the key is what actually counts as a “tokenized NMS stock.” The SEC basically recognizes two relevant models:

1. Issuer-native tokenization

- The company itself, or someone acting on its behalf, tokenizes the actual stock.
- Think of a transfer agent recording the actual shares onchain.
- The token Itself is the security, not a wrapper that merely tracks it.

2. Third-party custodial tokenization

- A third party holds the underlying stock within the traditional securities system and tokenizes the investor’s ownership interest / security entitlement.
- Again, the important part is that the token holder must receive the same rights and privileges as a holder of the equivalent traditional stock.
- That explicitly includes things like dividends and voting rights.

What does NOT qualify? → Synthetic exposure.

If a third party issues its own note, derivative, tracker certificate, security-based swap, etc. whose value simply tracks AAPL or NVDA, that instrument is not a “tokenized NMS stock” under this exemption.

This distinction matters because the market reaction has been much broader than the actual SEC framework. Anything vaguely connected to tokenized stocks or onchain trading got bid.

$BP, $ONDO, $HYPE, $LIT and other adjacent names were swept into the narrative, even though their exposure to the exemption is very different.

$ONDO at least has a legitimate connection: Ondo has been moving toward custodial tokenization structures where underlying securities remain within regulated custody while corresponding onchain tokens represent rights tied to those securities.

But HYPE or LIT equity perps? Those are derivatives. They are not what the SEC just exempted.

And this brings us to Backpack.

$BP rallied hard as the market started viewing Backpack as one of the obvious winners from tokenized U.S. equities.

The common thesis seems to be:

“Backpack tokens are redeemable 1:1 for real shares, therefore they are real-equity tokens, therefore the SEC exemption directly benefits Backpack.”

That skips an important legal distinction. Backpack itself describes the two forms very clearly:

Traditional Backpack securities:
→ UCC Article 8 security entitlement

Backpack tokens on Solana:
→ “Tokenized claim”
→ Claim on an SPV holding the underlying assets

Those are NOT the same legal instrument. When you withdraw a traditional Backpack stock position onchain, you are not simply moving the existing Article 8 security entitlement onto Solana.

The security entitlement is converted into a different tokenized instrument.

That token can later be redeemed 1:1 through Backpack Securities and converted back into the corresponding traditional security entitlement.

This is actually a meaningful improvement over many existing stock-token structures.

xStocks, for example, are bearer debt instruments / tracker certificates backed 1:1 by underlying shares.

Robinhood’s Classic Stock Tokens are derivatives against Robinhood Europe and explicitly do not give holders ownership rights in the underlying stock.

Backpack goes further because its token can be redeemed 1:1 into an actual traditional share position / security entitlement.

But redeemability ≠ the token itself being the underlying equity.

And that distinction matters for the SEC exemption.
The SEC does not merely require 1:1 backing or 1:1 redemption.

A tokenized NMS stock traded under the exemption must provide the holder the same rights and privileges as the corresponding traditional stock, including voting rights.

Backpack’s current documentation describes the Solana token as a “tokenized claim” designed to maintain economic equivalence with the underlying security.

It does not describe that token itself as an Article 8 security entitlement or as carrying the full shareholder rights required by the SEC framework.

So I would not classify Backpack’s current stock token structure as a direct beneficiary of the Innovation Exemption.

Could Backpack build a compliant structure around the exemption later? Absolutely. But that is different from saying its existing tokens already fit it.

The infrastructure that is much more directly aligned with what the SEC just described looks more like:

- @SuperstateInc: issuer-native shares recorded onchain through a registered transfer-agent model.
- @Securitize: issuer-sponsored tokenized shares and transfer-agent infrastructure.
- @Figure: blockchain-native registered public equity.
- @The_DTCC: tokenization of DTC-custodied securities with identical legal and ownership rights.
- @DinariGlobal: custodial tokenized equities designed to preserve the rights of the underlying securities.
- @Ondo: moving toward custodial tokenization models tied more directly to securities held inside the regulated custody chain.

I’m writing this because I’ve seen a lot of confusion in the community about what the exemption actually covers and which existing products legally fit that definition today.

Either way, the SEC’s latest announcement is undeniably a major positive for the tokenized equity ecosystem as a whole.

author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
With the launch of the Matrix model back in March, I was fairly close to a Jev-like architecture. 

Here is where I was
- Frozen pretrained backbone + small trained heads. 
A Judge head, a domain-router MoE, a complexity head, etc., ~278M trainable params. That is exactly the architecture the Jev teardown points to (a pretrained decoder + a decision readout).
- Score in one forward pass, no text generation. The Matrix model did not generate, it read a score straight off a pooled representation in a single pass. That's the defining Jev principle ("don't generate a verdict, read it from the representation"), applied to reranking instead of action-choice.
- Reading decisions from internal representations, not generated tokens. Jev teardown framed the whole proposition as "retain a pretrained LLM's knowledge
but replace generated confidence claims with decision probabilities read directly from its internal representations." That's literally what Matrix's Judge head and reranker do.

Here is what Jev taught
- RLCD, Calibration as the training objective: training the probabilities to be calibrated via proper scoring rules.
- A general "typed questions over shared state" surface. Jev generalized: encode any state once, ask many typed questions sharing the KV cache. Matrix stayed domain-specific.
- Options that interact. Jev scores the whole option list at a final-position head, so adding a 5th option shifts the others. Matrix's reranker scores each query-doc pair
independently.

So I was on the right track: frozen backbone + scoring head, no generation, before Jev launched. 🤷‍♂️ What it taught is the objective (train for calibration) and the generalization (typed questions over shared state).

Jevons Paradox
Now I am taking all these learnings, for a local, on-device Jev-like model as part of the Hyperspace agentic system. It's called Paradox. Already built it's v1 to validate the possibilities: that a local, API-free, Jev-accurate decision engine runs on a laptop and decides real pages correctly in a hybrid setup; measured that
its weak spot is multi-step decision quality which will be solved by Paradox v2. 

More abundance of this type of a model, from Jev's datacenters to running it on-device, the better it will be for society. 

h/t @NielsRogge, @harshagundal, and @4rcherhume (architecture deep-dive) and @CompleteSkeptic 🫡

text: Both advanced key ideas independently before Jev. The Laya paper author (2025) first published RL-driven non-generative probability prediction for domain decisions. Your Matrix (March 2026) aligned more closely with the public teardowns: frozen pretrained backbone plus small scoring heads that read decisions from representations in a single forward pass, no text generation. Jev generalized the pattern further with calibration training and multi-question shared-state interface.

text:
I’ve been digging deeper into microLED interconnects, especially after hearing microLED discussed at the SK hynix Global Forum and continuing to investigate what kind of architecture SK hynix may ultimately be targeting.

That makes this first-hand visit to Avicena particularly interesting.

The key takeaway is that we probably shouldn’t think of microLED as a direct replacement for conventional laser-based optics.

Avicena’s current production microLEDs operate at roughly 3–3.5 Gbps per lane, while its next-generation device has demonstrated around 8 Gbps in the lab. That is obviously much slower per lane than microVCSELs or laser-based optical links.

The approach is different: massive parallelism.

Instead of pushing tens or hundreds of gigabits through each optical lane, microLED uses hundreds of low-speed lanes at very tight pitch to achieve high aggregate bandwidth density.

And that leads to perhaps the most important point: reach.

Because microLEDs have a much broader optical linewidth than lasers, chromatic dispersion becomes a significant limitation as distance increases. For now, the most credible application space appears to be roughly 10 meters and below, rather than trying to compete with laser optics at 30–50 meters and beyond.

In other words, the real competitor may not be conventional optics.

It may be copper.

Avicena’s actual implementation makes this more interesting.

The company demonstrated a roughly 5-meter cable containing 300+ parallel optical links, while the entire cable was only around 3 mm in diameter. So one of the common criticisms—that hundreds of fibers inevitably make the cable physically impractical—doesn’t appear as obvious in a real implementation.

Crosstalk is another frequent concern.

With hundreds of electrical and optical lanes operating together, some crosstalk and jitter are inevitable. But Avicena’s victim/aggressor BER and bathtub measurements suggest that, at the current ~3 Gbps lane rate, the degradation exists but is not remotely enough to collapse the link.

The more interesting long-term question may actually be gearboxing and system architecture.

Converting a 200G SerDes lane into ~3G microLED lanes requires a very large gearbox ratio today. But if future XPUs or memory interfaces are designed from the beginning around a wide-and-slow optical architecture, much of that gearboxing could potentially be reduced—or eliminated entirely.

And this is exactly why I keep digging into SK hynix’s approach to microLED.

The real killer application may not ultimately be an optical cable.

It could be scale-in: die-to-die, chip-to-chip, and especially memory-to-XPU optical connectivity.

Avicena itself originally envisioned microLED for chip-to-chip optical interconnects, and the author notes that this concept has received renewed attention following SK hynix’s work in Nature Electronics. Avicena also says data-center, XPU-platform, and memory companies have asked it to develop and qualify the technology for their infrastructure.

So my current framework is:

MicroLED may not be trying to beat lasers at their own game.

It may instead become an optical solution for the distances where copper starts breaking down, but conventional laser optics remain unnecessarily expensive or power-hungry.

As AI systems connect increasingly larger numbers of GPUs and HBM, and scale-up networks expand from a single rack toward multi-rack systems, the scale-in and short-reach interconnect layer could become a very important battleground.

That is why I’m continuing to dig into what SK hynix is doing with microLED—and how far they intend to take it within future memory-centric architectures.
author: mindmoon_108
quoted_text:
MicroLEDs for interconnects are becoming increasingly interesting as a technology for AI datacenters.

I went to Avicena's office and spent 3 hours talking to their entire team, from the CEO to senior leadership to engineering working on the tech. 

I asked in-depth questions and I took lots of pictures. The latest report combines all my observations in a single post.

Important ideas to take away:
- MicroLEDs are more of a copper replacement for scale up/in. Don't compare to laser optics. They are not the competition.
- Slow lane rates simplify a lot of things; faster isnt always better.
- Crosstalk isn't as big an issue as everyone makes it out to be.
- Fiber bundle does not make the cable fatter. It's a pretty normal sized cable.
- Gearboxing is a requirement for "wide-but-slow" ; more lanes require deskew, slow lanes simplify circuits.
- It is a killer technology for scale-in; the rumblings of which we are just beginning to see.

What I still don't buy: that microLEDs have 30m reach. I have not seen a demo yet. This messaging from companies working on microLEDs draws comparison to optics -- which is missing the point.

There is room for a good interconnect in the sub-10m range.

The post below addresses lots of the nuance that is missing from the dialog on microLEDs for interconnects.

Read it here:
https://t.co/5DCl9RDTxT

text:
This is an elitist statement. That there’s no reason to be this fast, and therefore we have to slow down!

It’s truly remarkable the level of intelligence I have available on my phone with a $200/month pro plan. However, it’s way too expensive for this to be widely available to billions of people around the world.

Tao is worried about the nonlinear nature of progress, except that technological breakthroughs, almost by definition are nonlinear. Otherwise, we would have run out of resources in the world long time ago.

People forget how recently we figured out how to produce food at today’s scale. In the 1800s, an important source of fertilizer was an island off the coast of South America. Birds had spent centuries dropping their shit there, building up deposits that people mined for fertilizer.

Then came a remarkable invention by the German scientist Haber, which Bosch helped scale industrially. By combining nitrogen from the air with hydrogen, using energy, we could manufacture ammonia for fertilizer. Fertilizer from thin air.

There’s another lesson in there about the nature of technology. The same technology that helped create an abundance of food also enabled the production of explosives at scale.

text:
刚开始做套利的朋友，很容易过分痴迷于工程问题。

监控怎么搭，执行怎么快，警报怎么配，最好再搞个漂亮的 dashboard，看着满屏跳动的数字，感觉在 AI 的帮助下，离印钞就差一个 API key。

但当你真把这门生意做到足够大时，你会渐渐意识到，这些玩意儿既不是必要条件，也不是充分条件。

你和套利佬之间的沟壑，根本不是代码能力，而是在深入研究交易类产品规则，和衍生品底层资产特性后，提出猜想，验证猜想的能力。

比如我可以很自信的说在 @Lighter_xyz 上，所有的套利机会都是我的机会。

为什么？

因为从币圈原生资产，到 RWA 这波的黄金、原油、指数、美股个股，我和 @Boywus 算是跟着平台一个个的资产上新，把规则一点点完整地啃了下来。

价格怎么来，资费怎么算，休市后怎么办，极端行情下有什么限制，同一资产放到其他所又是怎么处理的。

哪些差异能赚，哪些只是看起来能赚；哪些仓位平时相安无事，一到周末就能给你整出点节目。

这些都得弄明白。

这个过程很漫长，也很痛苦。尤其早期规则不完善时，很多认知，是要拿大额亏损换的。

旁人看到的是我狩猎巨鲸，日入百万；
是几千万美金的 OI 持仓，爽吃资费和积分。

但他们没看到的是，哥们儿也曾在 LG 周末涨跌熔断机制带来的费率爆杀里，抱头鼠窜。

没有实打实的痛过，就永远不知道策略的边界在哪里。

赚钱的时候觉得自己理解了规则，亏钱的时候才发现，自己漏读的那一行 docs 里的小字，收费是真他妈贵。

所谓理解一个策略，不只是知道它什么时候赚钱，还得知道它会怎么亏，最坏能亏到哪儿，以及自己有没有能力扛到退出。

而最终沉淀下来的那些策略，作为碳基生命的我，走老艺术家手搓路线，也能把单开出来。

但是这一刻，已经没必要了，因为你对它们太了解了，什么条件该开，什么情况该停，哪些异常必须报警把我摇起来，心里都有数了，那就索性就甩给程序去做吧。

像图里这种 10 亿美金交易量以上的号，TGE 后，我跑了得有 20 个。

一年大几百亿美金的交易量给我带来的肌肉记忆，才是哥们儿的护城河。
author: Metabape
quoted_text:
其实大部分的套利交易机会都是用时间和金钱刷出来的，并不是来自AI给你挖矿挖出来的。

就好像很多机会都是老大哥 @Metabape 在每个凌晨观察数据特性算出来的，甚至有好几次是实战大仓位被交易所坑了一波学费，我们才明白：还能这样玩？

我并不能得到人类在这方面还是强于AI的结论，只是在现阶段，更像是AI统治世界后还有个犄角旮旯的人类反抗军聚集地，像极了红果的末日剧。

text:
MOST PEOPLE TALKING ABOUT JEV HAVE NEVER READ PAST THE PRICING PAGE.

Here's what's actually buried in the docs.

1/ Jev plays DOOM.

Not as a gimmick. TypeSafe ran it live, roughly 10 decisions per second, structured game state in, action out.

No frames. No pixels. Just typed state and a choice every 100ms.

Cost to run it continuously: about $7 an hour.

That's the real pitch. A model that reacts inside a loop where a 3 to 30 second LLM call isn't even an option.

2/ It's not autoregressive.

Jev uses a parallel sampler that generates every output in a single pass, not token by token.

That's the actual mechanism behind the 70 to 500ms latency, not just "smaller model, faster server."

3/ There are exactly three question types, and each one has a hard ceiling.

Choice: max 255 options.
Score: 2 to 10 levels, no more.
Noul: a boolean, and the probability itself IS the confidence. There's no separate confidence field on a Noul question.

4/ You get a shared 64K token budget across state and questions combined.

But there's a second, tighter constraint hiding under that one: your state plus your single longest question has to fit in about 32K tokens. Roughly 150,000 characters.

Most people hit this limit before they hit the first one.

5/ Batching isn't a nice to have, it's the entire cost model.

13 questions in one call measured out at 12.2x cheaper and 10x faster than 13 separate calls, with no drop in answer quality from batching itself.

If you're calling Jev once per question, you're paying a tax you don't have to.

6/ The single biggest mistake people make writing questions for it: asking Jev to extract or generate something.

Don't ask it to name a card.
Give it the deck and ask it to pick one.

Candidates in, choice out. That's the entire design contract.

7/ Jev cannot count, do date math, or compare versions reliably.

Not a bug. A boundary. Anything that's arithmetic gets computed in your code and handed to Jev as a pre-computed fact, not asked as a question.

8/ Accuracy quietly degrades as you cram unrelated content into the state.

It's not context rot the way LLMs get it. It's state pollution. Every irrelevant token in state is competing for weight against the one thing you actually need judged.

9/ If you're on the Vercel AI SDK, confidence doesn't live where you'd expect.

It's not inside the answers object. It's at result.providerMetadata.typesafe.confidence, keyed by question id.

Miss that and you'll think confidence scoring doesn't exist.

10/ Output tokens are free. Not cheap, free.

TypeSafe calls them "too cheap to meter" because the output is a typed answer, not generated text. At $0.042 per million input tokens, a 300 token classification costs about $0.0000126.

That's the number that makes per record AI classification make sense for the first time.

Most people are still evaluating Jev like it's a smaller, faster chatbot.

It isn't one. It's a completely different primitive, and the docs make that obvious if you actually read them.

Follow @cyrilXBT, I read the boring parts of the docs so you don't have to.

text:
The SEC’s recent Innovation Exemption for tokenized stocks is a major positive for the tokenized securities ecosystem, but it’s important to distinguish which companies and platforms are actually positioned to benefit from it.

👇
author: FourPillarsFP
quoted_text:
A lot of people are misreading the SEC’s new Innovation Exemption for tokenized stocks.

The market seems to be treating this as a blanket green light for anything related to “tokenized equities.”

It isn’t. The SEC’s exemption is much narrower.

The framework allows 

- qualifying Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) to facilitate trading of tokenized NMS stocks through permissioned AMMs without registering as traditional exchanges.

- Certain liquidity providers can also receive conditional relief from dealer registration.

But the key is what actually counts as a “tokenized NMS stock.” The SEC basically recognizes two relevant models:

1. Issuer-native tokenization

- The company itself, or someone acting on its behalf, tokenizes the actual stock.
- Think of a transfer agent recording the actual shares onchain.
- The token Itself is the security, not a wrapper that merely tracks it.

2. Third-party custodial tokenization

- A third party holds the underlying stock within the traditional securities system and tokenizes the investor’s ownership interest / security entitlement.
- Again, the important part is that the token holder must receive the same rights and privileges as a holder of the equivalent traditional stock.
- That explicitly includes things like dividends and voting rights.

What does NOT qualify? → Synthetic exposure.

If a third party issues its own note, derivative, tracker certificate, security-based swap, etc. whose value simply tracks AAPL or NVDA, that instrument is not a “tokenized NMS stock” under this exemption.

This distinction matters because the market reaction has been much broader than the actual SEC framework. Anything vaguely connected to tokenized stocks or onchain trading got bid.

$BP, $ONDO, $HYPE, $LIT and other adjacent names were swept into the narrative, even though their exposure to the exemption is very different.

$ONDO at least has a legitimate connection: Ondo has been moving toward custodial tokenization structures where underlying securities remain within regulated custody while corresponding onchain tokens represent rights tied to those securities.

But HYPE or LIT equity perps? Those are derivatives. They are not what the SEC just exempted.

And this brings us to Backpack.

$BP rallied hard as the market started viewing Backpack as one of the obvious winners from tokenized U.S. equities.

The common thesis seems to be:

“Backpack tokens are redeemable 1:1 for real shares, therefore they are real-equity tokens, therefore the SEC exemption directly benefits Backpack.”

That skips an important legal distinction. Backpack itself describes the two forms very clearly:

Traditional Backpack securities:
→ UCC Article 8 security entitlement

Backpack tokens on Solana:
→ “Tokenized claim”
→ Claim on an SPV holding the underlying assets

Those are NOT the same legal instrument. When you withdraw a traditional Backpack stock position onchain, you are not simply moving the existing Article 8 security entitlement onto Solana.

The security entitlement is converted into a different tokenized instrument.

That token can later be redeemed 1:1 through Backpack Securities and converted back into the corresponding traditional security entitlement.

This is actually a meaningful improvement over many existing stock-token structures.

xStocks, for example, are bearer debt instruments / tracker certificates backed 1:1 by underlying shares.

Robinhood’s Classic Stock Tokens are derivatives against Robinhood Europe and explicitly do not give holders ownership rights in the underlying stock.

Backpack goes further because its token can be redeemed 1:1 into an actual traditional share position / security entitlement.

But redeemability ≠ the token itself being the underlying equity.

And that distinction matters for the SEC exemption.
The SEC does not merely require 1:1 backing or 1:1 redemption.

A tokenized NMS stock traded under the exemption must provide the holder the same rights and privileges as the corresponding traditional stock, including voting rights.

Backpack’s current documentation describes the Solana token as a “tokenized claim” designed to maintain economic equivalence with the underlying security.

It does not describe that token itself as an Article 8 security entitlement or as carrying the full shareholder rights required by the SEC framework.

So I would not classify Backpack’s current stock token structure as a direct beneficiary of the Innovation Exemption.

Could Backpack build a compliant structure around the exemption later? Absolutely. But that is different from saying its existing tokens already fit it.

The infrastructure that is much more directly aligned with what the SEC just described looks more like:

- @SuperstateInc: issuer-native shares recorded onchain through a registered transfer-agent model.
- @Securitize: issuer-sponsored tokenized shares and transfer-agent infrastructure.
- @Figure: blockchain-native registered public equity.
- @The_DTCC: tokenization of DTC-custodied securities with identical legal and ownership rights.
- @DinariGlobal: custodial tokenized equities designed to preserve the rights of the underlying securities.
- @Ondo: moving toward custodial tokenization models tied more directly to securities held inside the regulated custody chain.

I’m writing this because I’ve seen a lot of confusion in the community about what the exemption actually covers and which existing products legally fit that definition today.

Either way, the SEC’s latest announcement is undeniably a major positive for the tokenized equity ecosystem as a whole.

text:
Had an interesting discussion this week while allocating on why new, shiny memes plus the stock-backed plays are outperforming legacy ones right now.

Looking at the past week, 2 categories of meme coin have done well and likely keep doing well:

1) Stock-based or "valuable-backed" plays. Anything people can convince themselves is backed by something real. This has genuinely interesting reflexivity built in, since the backing narrative and the price action reinforce each other.

2) New memes tied to a current main character, cult around the person becomes cult around the meme. Cate, Ansem earlier, Useless with Uni sitting at the top of the FOMO PnL board. Social apps are now crowning main characters faster than ever, which feeds directly into this loop.

Once the market sees categories 1 and 2 outperform, you get the reflexive "last hot asset" loop. People just keep bidding what already worked, which is exactly what makes 1 and 2 the de facto meta over legacy plays, rather than any inherent quality difference in the coins themselves.

很简单
币安需要市场的注意力集中到自己，并且要尽可能的白嫖

币安和其他链，比如rh，最大的区别是，币安坐稳了好几年的行业老大垄断地位，他选择了对外打压创新，对内涸泽而渔。

举例ftx,在21年的那轮牛市中对币安构成了巨大的挑战，cz隐忍不发，到最关键的时候，通过假意收购从而让sbf自曝资不抵债引发全市场的挤兑，一击毙命。

ftx死了，死的不是sbf一个人，死的是整个加密市场的财富效应。当币安垄断了绝对的市场份额，整个市场都成为他倾倒老鼠仓垃圾币的流动性提供者。从23年到25年，币安不停的上各种组局vc币，硬生生的扼杀了上一轮牛市的山寨季。

举例hype，hype的创新让币安，让cz如芒在背。jellyjelly事件中币安重拳出击，试图重创hype，但是没有成功。如今hype的市值即将超越bnb，不知道cz心里怎么想。

举例rh，rh对meme的支持是显而易见的。创始人直接下场表态，并且不会言而无信朝秦暮楚，rh链的创始人的做事方式，人格，带动了整个市场对rh链的信心和信任。rh链的流动性好，并不是单纯罗宾汉的嫡系做市商出钱拉盘，更多的是市场的合力。

那么随着pons和rh链上一众代币的拉升，bsc推出了marscoin，并且扭扭捏捏的支持了一个自然流量发酵的牛来。
当marscoin和牛来都上现货以后，链上的注意力涣散，情绪消退了。（大众普遍都是踏空，并且希望找到下一个低市值的）

币安需要在这个链上注意力的真空期，不断的制造热点和新鲜，来让自己站在舞台中央。bsc的本质，是一个定期提供暴富幻想，让整个市场的鱼群受币安指挥的工具。

所有人，市场中的散户，大户，项目方，庄，都是币安的工具。cz的每一次的动作，都不是承诺，而是信号，这个信号就让大家去猜，有时候猜对了赚钱，有时候猜错了亏钱。

有人疑问，cz为什么不能给个准信，为什么要这么折磨大家。

因为币安过于强大，强大到他的利益的对手盘是整个市场，整个加密世界，除了币安自己，都是币安的猎物。这就注定了币安的行事风格，就是让所有人都活在猜不透上意，如履薄冰的困境中。而币安也正是通过这种局面，来持续的最大化的从所有人的口袋，注意力中榨取最大的利益。

但是天之道，损有余而补不足。从hype到rh，挑战者的实力越来越强大，币安也越难越难以招架，他的应对肉眼可见的失措。这轮牛市，我们会见证币安的衰落，也会见证加密牛市财富效应的复兴。

On the one hand, you have to be incredibly attentive to your problems, and recognize the myriad ways in which your product totally sucks. If you're just cheerfully whistling along, Lego Movie style — everything is awesome — reality is going to give you a rude slap in the face pretty quickly.

You simultaneously need to have this attitude that, okay, everything is terrible today, but we really have conviction that we can make it fantastic in two years' time, in four years' time, in six years' time. Part of what we're trying to do is acknowledge this tension and give you structural permission to be extremely critical of what exists today — because otherwise people feel tentative, like, can they say the dashboard sucks or this API sucks?"

等等，这里有个东西被混过去了：Nimble 复刻的是行为，不是架构。

它靠 constrained decoding 把输出摁进候选答案里，底子还是自回归的 Qwen。Jev 是真的非自回归，几个答案一次并行出来，不走逐 token 生成。一个改输出层，一个换架构，中间隔着东西。

顺带说一句，Jev 是判别式，这条路线属于 AI 2.0，不是 3.0。风控和邮件过滤里跑了十几年，只是没人喷它。新的地方在另外两样：一次并行出全部答案，还有把概率校准到跟真实准确率对上。

还有一点我没搞懂，Jev都特么算AI古典主义了，没看懂一群人在高潮啥？
author: lizikk_zhu
quoted_text:
牛逼！Jev 刚火没两天，已经有人搞了个开源的Jev🤣

@bespokelabsai  发布了一个开源版的Jev：Bespoke Nimble。

更离谱的是，整个项目是基于 Qwen3.5-9B ，只花了大约两天。

数据、模型权重、训练配方、推理代码全部公开，而且没有从 Jev 蒸馏，只拿 Jev 做评测参照。

最终方法是在 Qwen3.5-9B 上做了一次很轻量的 LoRA微调。

只用了2676 条训练数据，结果在他们自己的 324 条 held-out 测试集上拿到了90.12%，而原版的Jev是93.21%。

一个 9B 模型，已经做到距离 Jev 只差 3 个百分点。

但我觉得最值得看的不是这个分数，而是他们到底怎么训的。

核心方法叫 contrastive data curation。

简单说，他们会构造两个几乎完全一样的样本，只修改一个足以改变最终决策的关键事实，让正确答案发生翻转。

模型因此被迫学会一件事：

到底哪条证据，才真正应该改变决策。

这其实特别符合 Jev 这类模型的用途。

它本来就不是拿来陪你聊天的，而是塞进 Agent 和软件系统里，做路由、审核、打分、策略判断这些高频的小决策。

推理方式上Nimble 不生成 CoT，甚至不生成 JSON。

它直接读取候选答案 token 的 logits，再把它们转成概率，最后由程序拼成结构化输出。

能不生成一个 token，就不生成一个 token。

这也是 Jev 这类模型路线真正有价值的地方。

对于大量根本不需要长思考的决策，怎么让模型几乎不想，直接判断。

PS：我个人很反感这两天狂吹 Jev 的帖子....

主编真的不让发，你们不要告诉他！

《SEC豁免新政催生山寨牛，UNI外哪些项目最值得关注》

💎核心背景与行业转变

政策红利：SEC 豁免政策为链上股票交易打开了合规大门。
叙事升级：UNI 从“加密 DEX”升级为“链上股票交易中心”。
市场重点转向：从单纯的“发行股票代币”，转向“谁能赋予代币化股票更多金融用途（收益拆分、借贷、结构化产品等）”。

四大潜在获利板块与代表项目

1️⃣股息与收益分离（Yield Stripping）
将股票代币拆分为本金代币（PT）和收益代币（YT），实现收益的二次交易。
Pendle（$PENDLE）：加密原生收益交易龙头，已在 Robinhood Chain 上试水英伟达（NVDA）股息分离产品，为该领域最确定性的基础设施候选。
Pare Stocks（$PARE）：Robinhood 链原生协议，已支持 AAPL、SPY、QQQ 等标的拆分（拆分费 10 bps，收益赎回费 5%），YT 收益源于发行人披露的股息参数。

2️⃣信贷与结构化收益（Lending & Structured Products）
赋予股票代币抵押借贷与票据化属性，提高资金利用率。
Morpho（$MORPHO）：隔离市场借贷协议，可针对单只股票代币精细化配置风险参数（抵押率、清算线），极为适合建立独立股票借贷池。
Gage（$GAGE）：Robinhood 链点对点固定成本借贷，支持以代币化股票或 Meme 作抵押借出 USDG。主打“到期不还清算资产而非强制平仓”模式。
Note Systems（$NOTE）：Robinhood 链结构化票据协议，将股票代币包装成“带障碍价格、自动赎回”的票息产品（如年化票息与下跌保护结构）。

3️⃣多链流量出口 DEX（EVM & Non-EVM）
股票代币交易热潮将向 Ethereum/Robinhood 链之外的生态辐射：
PancakeSwap（$CAKE）：BSC 生态的绝对 DEX 龙头，承接 BSC 链上的股票代币交易流量。
Raydium（$RAY）：Solana 生态核心 AMM，高弹性标的，若 Solana 出现股票代币与配对 Meme 发行潮，将最直接受益。

4️⃣币股 Meme 的爆发行情与两条新路径
传统币股 Meme（如结合股票概念的代币）在政策后呈现两条新分化路径：
获得底层公司/创始人积极回应（正向背书）：
SEC 政策赋予了上市公司“交易阻断权”。因此，公司态度至关重要。
正例（BONER）：其正股 Hims & Hers（HIMS）创始人关注了 BONER 官方账号，社区解读为积极信号，支撑其高市值。
反例（MEME）：因 AMC CEO 对 Robinhood 股票代币公开排斥，缺乏长期监管与正统性预期。
链上股权控制权与无主基金会（治理演进）：
https://t.co/tIaRLYPy43（$GSTOCK 等）：BSC 上的新尝试，主张将股票代币放入无主基金会，通过链上多签在链下行使真实股权权利（结合 CZ 提及的 BNC 生态与财库公司概念）。

📒总结与风险提示

短期看点：围绕 收益拆分（Pendle）、抵押借贷（Morpho/Gage）、结构化票据（Note） 和 流量 DEX（Pancake/Raydium） 这四层叙事进行炒作。
长期关键：项目能否真正落地，取决于上市公司是否接受、链下股权/股息权利是否真实对应、资产能否顺畅赎回，以及交易场所是否满足监管的具体条件（TSV）。
风险提示：许多新协议（如 Pare、Gage、Note、https://t.co/tIaRLYPy43）仍处于初创早期，存在未经审计、合规风险高（如对美国用户限制）及市场波动剧烈等不确定性。

text:
Jev is going to change the prosumer/consumer AI landscape by unlocking a specific thing:

Ad-supported + free AI native apps

this is going to usher in a generation of new AI-native marketplaces, social networks, photo apps, messaging, calendars, email, collab tools, and much more.

Why? Previously, if you wanted to have an AI-native app with multiple/fast LLM calls on every screen, the math just didn’t work - inference costs just couldn’t be paid back from throwing a few video ads or affiliate links. So there were really just two solutions:

1) be a massive company and subsidize AI costs
2) charge a subscription fee to cover inference
(or both)

So what happens when you take a different approach that’s looks to be, initially, >400x cheaper than a more general LLM? I think it means that app developers are going to make their apps smarter and different in interesting ways. It won’t be as generically powerful as LLMs, but instead folks will create highly differentiated point solutions. You may not have a generically powerful virtual admin to schedule all your meetings, but you may have a free/ad-powered assistant that can comb through your inbox, filter for only important emails, figure out important dates, prioritize contacts, and do other interesting 80/20 work. Same for generically powerful virtual companions, or app builders, etc - it may be that we can hybridize the LLM and future Jev-like models that adds “wow” features at 1/1000ths of the cost, to make the economics work.

If folks hear of interesting new apps/interactions/etc built on Jev, I’d love to hear it!

text:
这是一个美丽的误会 🤣 

主要是持仓保证金 vs 开仓保证金  之争

背景知识：
1. 网格策略是一个动态的策略 - 它会一直频繁平仓开仓（按照你的设置0.04%（5u的距离）之内放了100个grid，差不多就是每0.05u 一个grid，这非常的密集。。）

bn的grid的规则是，成交的同时会在另一侧给你摆单子（其他人take了就算做是你的盈利 matched trade）；但是如果一直没人take，那么这个东西就会成为unmatched profit / loss

grid是怎么弄的呢？比如125.5的long成交了，但就在125.55摆一个close long，假设这个close long没有被take，就一直放在哪里，计入unmatched pnl

好处就是，假设价格在一个区间内震荡，那这个价差就吃得很爽；坏处就是，突然单边的话，你一侧的单子都要承压 - 这个会吃掉你的保证金

2. 保证金可以分成几种：持仓初始保证金，开仓保证金，维持保证金， - 你这里的主要问题是开仓保证金耗尽了。。而开仓保证金耗尽按照bn的规矩也是终止的条件之一

3. 网格重启后的的动作：先卖出减仓，再补买单 （这个是重点，后面会考） 

在你的案例里 - 反弹时，机器人先执行上方挂着的平多卖单。卖出一格的数量后，再到下面一格挂买单，等价格回落时接回来。

我没看到具体的order flow，所以我猜测是：
第一次碰到122的时候没事，是因为你这个时候122的单子是之前就开好的。。 （钱已经花出去了） 

跌到122，最后一格买入成交
机器人买入53.79 SOXL，然后在约122.05挂出同样数量的平多卖单。

价格随后跌到118，这个122.05的卖单暂时成交不了，然后unmatched loss就一直在增加 （蚕食你为数不多的开仓保证金）

然后第二次到达122的时候，grid就重新启动 -触发新一轮的买单回补

价格反弹进入区间、平多卖单成交后，机器人会尝试在下方补挂买单。这个动作可能触发新的保证金检查。如果下单因保证金不足失败，策略可能终止

你可以理解成：
第一次下跌时，122买单可能是此前就挂好的订单；第二次反弹时，平多成交可能触发新的买单申请 aka你需要花钱开单 （注意：开单的保证金与持仓保证金不是同一个体系） ，而这个时候因为unmatched pnl等问题，你的开仓保证金已经不够了。。 

已存在的订单与新申请订单，检查时点不同。这就能解释“为什么偏偏在反弹时暴露问题”。。。

换句话，这时：

1. 不发生新的开仓申请，仓位可以继续存在。

2. 一旦网格申请补挂开仓单，就可能遇到资金不足。

3.如果系统因此终止策略，再执行你开仓时选择的“终止全平” —— 这个就是你看到“是反弹时被全部平仓” 

知其然，且知其所以然

I am thinking about something called #TapeAPI.

If DeWEB enables decentralized websites and TapeSend facilitates communication between people, then TapeAPI could allow websites to interact with one another without relying on a central server.

You can think of TapeAPI like this:

Today, most websites need to connect to a server/backend owned by a company to get data or perform certain functions.

For example:

Website → Server → Get BEM price
Website → Server → Process AI
Website → Server → Store game data

The idea behind TapeAPI is to turn these services into services with their own addresses on TapeOut.

For example:

price.tape → provides price data
ai.tape → provides AI services
game.tape → handles game data
payment.tape → handles payments

A DeWEB website could simply call whichever service it needs.

A simple example

Imagine you build a game on DeWEB.

Your game needs a translation feature.

Instead of building your own server:

Game → Your Server → Translation API

it could be:

Game → TapeAPI → Translation

The API provider could receive BEM as payment, while users only pay when they actually use the service.

This could create a decentralized marketplace for services:

Developer A builds an AI service
Developer B builds translation
Developer C provides data
Developer D provides payments

Other applications can use these services without having to build everything from scratch.

What I find interesting is:

DeWEB = Websites
TapeSend = Communication
TapeAPI = Services

Together, they could become another piece of the infrastructure for a decentralized Internet.

This is just an idea I’m proposing

#Tapeout $BEM

text:
你用AI时，AI 幻觉最大能闯多大的祸？

据外媒报道，它差点让美军对中国货船采取登船行动，险些挑起冲突。

据 CNN 援引知情人士称，美国特种作战司令部一名分析员用AI 聊天机器人把开源信息与机密信号情报拼在一起，生成了一份“完全虚假”的情报报告。

其中 AI 产生了严重的“幻觉”，把一艘在中东海域正常航行的中国船只，错误的识别成了“正在运输核武器项目部件”。

美军一度准备拦截登船，所幸行动前官员复查报告，发现是聊天机器人误判货物，才紧急叫停。

一名知情人士说，这“几乎引发了一场战争”。不过报道未能确认船上实际装了什么，也未说明用的是哪款模型。

虽然这只是个个例，可能是临时工的锅，但从大方向上来，美国政府似乎在军事方面已经全盘接入了 AI ：

去年 12 月，五角大楼引进了谷歌的 Gemini（定制版）作为军方 AI 平台的基础。

上个月，他们又把 Grok 给加进了选项清单，平台用户已超过 150 万。

此外，Anthropic 也曾为美方情报工作提供过定制模型。

用这些不同的 AI 模型分给不同部门，装多了真的不会出问题吗？

虽然大多数时候是智能，但少数智障时刻的后果可能很严重。

text:
Random thought experiment on NFTs, although I’m not sure it will be a loved idea.

Dopamine from hyper gamification has changed crypto. For the longest time it was just holders and occasionally flippers. 

High speed, cheap chains like solana came along with orderbooks and AMMs that made it much easier for Market Makers and others to build their bot trading systems. This is most volume in crypto in case you live under a rock. No real financial markets are people clicking buttons. 

We’ve reached a point where mostly everything is trading fast. This is great, it’s how it was always gonna end up.

I think it’s possible for NFTs to come back, but as nostalgic as it is. And IF they come back it won’t be all community and vibes. We are beyond that now. Small communities will exist, but people will build systems that suck the soul out of these projects to extract as much money as possible. Anyone can do it now with ai and a decent brain.

Just like with regular trading, you will see higher volumes of trades in the books. Yes there will be the long term community and holders, but there will be more bot trading than ever. 

And for this to work, you couldn’t have a single market per project. They aren’t all equal value. You’d have to have markets by rarity, created by some other system and stored in metadata

Idk if it plays out exactly like this, but I don’t think it will look like it did the first time.

text: Probably didn’t need a 25 year study to figure this out, but I’m glad it’s out there.
author: DonaldJTrumpJr
quoted_text:
A landmark Finnish study has found a sharp rise in psychiatric illness among adolescents following sex-alteration procedures.

The peer-reviewed study, published in Acta Paediatrica, tracked every young person under 23 who contacted Finland's gender clinics between 1996 and 2019.

A total 2,083 individuals were studied, with 16,643 matched controls. They were followed for up to 25 years.

Finland's health registers are mandatory, which means no one opts out — this is the complete national picture.

The numbers: psychiatric morbidity rose from 9.8% to 60.7% in adolescents who underwent feminising reassignment, and from 21.6% to 54.5% in masculinising reassignment.

Even after adjusting for prior psychiatric history, gender-referred adolescents faced five times the risk of male population controls, and three times the risk of female controls.

"Psychiatric needs do not subside after medical gender reassignment," the authors concluded.

Referrals after 2010 arrived sicker. 47.9% had already needed psychiatric treatment before their first clinic visit, against 15.3% among controls.

The authors' read: for some adolescents, gender distress may be secondary to other mental health challenges.

The evidence keeps mounting. The silencing continues anyway.

How many more adolescents will be told this is "care"?

text:
最近参与并研究了一个挺有意思的 Bitcoin Native 早期实验：$LEAF / CRC-20。

先留个时间戳。

简单来说，CRC-20 / PRECOP 想探索的是：能不能在 Bitcoin L1 之上做出一套更复杂的资产和金融应用，而不是再复制一条 EVM 链。

现在还非常早，也非常实验性，但已经不只是停留在概念阶段，链上有真实的 mint、migration 和用户参与。

我自己已经实际跑过一遍整个参与流程，所以决定继续跟下去。

真正让我感兴趣的不是短期价格，而是接下来几个问题：

— CRC-20 能不能顺利完成完整的流转闭环
— Mint 结束后能不能形成真正的 Swap / LP 和流动性
— 会不会有更多钱包、Indexer、市场开始支持 CRC-20
— PRECOP 能不能从一次实验，继续长成 Bitcoin Native 的金融基础设施
— 如果生态真的起来，$LEAF 最终能捕获多少价值

目前 Mint 已经非常接近尾声。

但这里我要强调一下：我参与时和现在的市场条件已经不同，当前 legacy 流动性也比较薄。

所以这不是一条“现在赶紧冲”的 Call，也不建议因为看到这条就去追价格。

我更愿意把它当成一个 Early Alpha Research：

东西很早，赔率曾经很有意思，后面还有不少关键节点需要验证。

如果它最后没跑出来，这条就当一次早期实验记录。

如果以后真的从现在这个阶段一路长到更大的体量，我也会回来完整复盘——当时为什么关注、哪些判断对了、哪些判断错了。

Bitcoin Native 这种东西，真正有意思的往往就是在所有答案都还没出来的时候。

项目：
https://t.co/55Jy4fMubn

我会继续跟踪 CRC-20 / PRECOP，以及其他 Bitcoin Native 早期机会。

更多研究和 Alpha：
https://t.co/Z5GxfEJSw8

仅为个人研究记录，不是买入建议。

text:
This week I delivered a 60-minute workshop to CFOs, CHROs, and CLOs teaching them how to go from desired outcome (i.e. offer acceptance >60%) to designed AI pilot in 6 steps. 

Here are the 6 steps: 

*If you want the deck & worksheet I used for the workshop, check the link below. 

1) Identify the outcome

Transformation isn't about AI. It's about driving outcomes and using tools (like AI) to solve problems that stand in the way. Before deciding what work/product to transform, you need to decide the outcome. 

To do that, fill in the blanks: 

Improve [measure] from [baseline] to [target] by [date].

Examples: overdue invoices 18% to 12%. Month-end close 10 days to 6. Cash-forecast updates 2 days to 2 hours. Offer acceptance 40% to 60%.

2) Find the workflow

Every business is plagued with inefficiency, even the most AI-native ones. Make a list of all of the workflows within your function/company that sit close enough to your outcome to impact it. 

Shorten the list to the workflows that pass the PAIN IN THE ASS TEST, and then circle one workflow that you believe, if made maximally efficient, would have the greatest impact on driving your outcome. 

One exercise for brainstorming workflows is forcing yourself to answer two questions: 

If you imagine work 12 months from now...
1) What is one specific way work happens differently?
2) What measurable result does that change create?

3) Design the new work

First, create a process diagram of the workflow you chose as it stands today. It should look like 5-7 steps connected by lines. 

Second, draw a new process diagram of the workflow in its future, most efficient form. Next to each step put a label for what drives the work. Three labels to choose from: AI-led, AI-assisted, Human-only. 

Example: Hiring outreach process

Current: Define hiring criteria --> Search for prospects
--> Research fit and contact history --> Write outreach messages --> Approve, send, and log in ATS --> Copy activity into a separate tracker --> Handle replies and hand off

New: Define criteria and permitted sources (Human) --> Find prospects using approved sources (AI-led) --> Review AI research; choose contacts (AI-assisted) --> Draft outreach from approved context (AI-led) --> Approve (Human) --> send, and log in ATS (AI-led) --> Handle replies and hand off (AI-assisted)

4) Assess readiness

Once you've reimagined the work, you still can't press go. There's a list of 8 items that must be checked (GREEN/YELLOW/RED) before proceeding. You don't necessarily need all items to be GREEN ahead of a pilot, but you definitely do ahead of production. 

• Value at stake - You can name the specific benefit to your business (you've built out the ROI case) and a plausible path from this workflow to it
• Process clarity and measurability - You know the (new/old) steps, start and finish, exceptions, and how to establish a baseline
• Data and context readiness - The required context exists, is fit for the test, and can be accessed within agreed boundaries
• Deployment capability - Someone (internally/externally) can configure, connect, test, support, and roll back the pilot
• User adoption - Intended users help design it, understand their role, and will try it in real work
• Change capacity - The team can spare time for training, review, feedback, and workflow changes
• Ownership and decision rights - A business owner owns the result. People know who approves changes, resolves issues, and stops the test
• Legal risk and controls - Required approvals, access limits, human review, logging, and stop rules are in place for the pilot.

5) Design & run pilot 

Every pilot should be documented & pitched internally with the following considerations included: 

• Scope: Who's included, what's the work they're doing, for how long?
- Example: Two recruiters. One engineering role family. Four weeks, after permissions and controls are cleared.

• Success: What's the business result you're looking to drive and what are early signals you need to see?
- Example: Compare with the manual baseline: ≥25% less net prospecting time, no drop in prospect relevance, and saved time used for candidate care. Track offer acceptance longer.

• Economics: Which benefit and cost assumptions need testing?
- Example: Measure setup and running costs, including recruiter review time. Use observed time savings and prospect quality to update the business-case assumptions. Track actual agency fees avoided and additional delivery contribution over a longer period.

• Guardrails: What must not happen?
- Example: No unauthorized outreach or material opt-out breach.

• Decision: What must be true to expand, revise, or stop the pilot? 
- Example: At week 4: do the early results justify continuing a bounded test? Continue if early gates pass; revise if fixes are viable; stop for a material breach or no credible path to value. Full ROI is not yet proven.

6) Scale scope & autonomy 

Based on performance of pilot & state of readiness criteria (from step 4), progressive productionizing of the workflow, rollout to the org, and autonomy for AI occurs. 

Link to the workshop & worksheet: https://t.co/nSwyNkEWZI
