text:
I need China to approve the shipment for our announcement that we no longer need China.

I'm a trade official at the U.S. Treasury. My job this week is to secure the magnets and preserve the tone.

The magnets go in things we would prefer to keep making. The tone goes on television.

Our manufacturer called at 8:10. He asked whether the shipment was coming.

I told him America would never be held hostage.

He said he could do Tuesday or Wednesday, but after that he'd have to stop the line.

I wrote "Wednesday" on a piece of paper and covered it with the national strategy.

We were preparing for talks on trade, AI, and critical minerals. I'd been assigned the section on reducing our dependence on China.

I called my Chinese counterpart to ask what time suited him.

He said Thursday.

I said Tuesday would demonstrate greater mutual respect.

He asked whether this was about the magnets.

I said we should avoid reducing a complex bilateral relationship to a single commodity.

He said Thursday, then.

I asked how early on Tuesday he could start.

Before the call, Communications sent me the proposed announcement. It said we were breaking China's grip on American industry.

My counterpart sent a shipment form. It required an explanation of why we needed the shipment.

I opened both documents side by side.

In the speech, America could stand alone.

In the form, we required expedited assistance.

I asked Legal whether a phrase could work in both.

They suggested "temporary strategic necessity."

I asked how long temporary could last.

They asked how often I could renew it.

The manufacturer called again. He'd seen a clip of the speech rehearsal and wanted to know whether we had found another supplier.

I said we had several options.

He asked for a phone number.

I gave him our office number.

He already had it. That was becoming the problem.

By lunch, I'd obtained a letter from him explaining what would happen without the magnets. I attached it to the Chinese application as evidence of urgency.

Communications asked for evidence that our policy was working.

I sent them the same letter with the subject line "American manufacturer stands ready."

My counterpart called. The application looked fine. Could we confirm that we wanted the quantity shown?

I said yes.

He asked about next month.

I said we were committed to reducing reliance on foreign suppliers.

He asked whether that meant a smaller order.

I said to keep it the same while we assessed the situation.

He offered to set up a recurring shipment.

I said recurring would be difficult to explain.

He said he could send the same form every month and I could sign it again.

I thanked him for understanding our sovereignty.

The manufacturer thanked me for keeping his factory open. Communications thanked me for holding firm. My director asked whether I'd consider taking over the independence program permanently.

I said I'd need an assistant.

They asked what the assistant would do.

"Renewals."

text:
The most interesting part of @DeriveXYZ V3 has very little to do with people trading directly on Derive.

It’s about distribution.

Hyperliquid already showed what can happen when an exchange becomes infrastructure for other apps:

• Wallets like Phantom and Rabby own the frontend and the user relationship.
• Hyperliquid provides the trading infrastructure.
• The apps get paid for bringing the flow.

And I think this is one of the more interesting ways to think about Derive V3.

Derive doesn’t necessarily need every future options trader to become a direct Derive user either. It can become the options engine running underneath other products.

Derive already has Builder Codes, so apps can route trades through Derive and monetize the activity they generate.

V3 then makes that integration layer much more powerful by exposing the infrastructure builders need to create their own options products and UX.

Imagine a wallet showing: “Protect my ETH from falling below $3,000.” The user doesn’t need to know they’re buying a put.

Or a yield app showing: “Earn yield while being willing to sell ETH at $6,000.”

Underneath, it can package an options strategy.

This matters because options have a huge UX problem. Strikes, expiries, implied volatility, Greeks, strategy combinations.

Most users don’t want to learn all of that. But maybe the answer isn’t teaching everyone how to use an options chain, it’s hiding the options chain completely.

Let builders turn complex options positions into simple products users already understand:
• Protection
• Yield
• Directional bets
• Structured payoffs

And let Derive handle the liquidity, execution and risk engine underneath.

Hyperliquid proved the builder distribution model can work for perps. Derive now has a chance to test what that same model looks like for onchain options.

text:
the launchpad is not the thesis for Trade Zone. 

it is the entry point into Quai

start with what makes an L1/L2 ecosystem work:
- networks produce blockspace
- blockspace attracts applications
- applications create assets, markets, liquidity, and culture
- those things attract more users, which creates more demand for the network and its native asset

Solana is probably the clearest example

SOL performed well -> users had more capital to rotate into Solana tokens -> those tokens attracted more volume and attention -> more people needed SOL and entered the Solana ecosystem

SOL helped the memes, and the memes helped SOL

this is reflexive

now compare that with Base or Robinhood Chain

both use ETH for gas so there is no separate Base or Robinhood asset that gives users direct exposure to the growth of those specific ecosystems (outside of large cap stocks)

the apps and tokens can perform extremely well, but the relationship between ecosystem activity and a native asset is less direct

Quai is different

QUAI is the native asset on the fastest Proof of Work EVM chain

but Quai also has QI, the private energy-based flatcoin, with WQI bringing that asset into the smart-contract economy

Trade Zone supports both sides of this monetary system. bonded markets begin against native QUAI or WQI

that means activity does not only create more reasons to acquire and use QUAI. it also gives QI more places to trade, pair, and build liquidity through WQI, helping deepen the markets that support its usefulness and stability

so if Quai-native tokens attract attention, that attention can create demand for QUAI

and if QUAI gains liquidity, users, and value, more capital becomes available for Quai-native tokens

QUAI helps the ecosystem, and the ecosystem helps QUAI

the same loop can help QI from another direction: more WQI markets -> more liquidity and utility -> a stronger energy-based currency inside the Quai economy

the important part is that this loop is only beginning

there are not yet hundreds of dominant Quai applications or established categories. liquidity has not already settled around a handful of winners. the culture and default assets of the ecosystem are still being formed

that makes it riskier, obviously, but it is also what being early actually means

launchpads are useful here because they compress the process of market formation

token creation -> price discovery -> trading -> liquidity -> communities -> new applications

and all of this is happening on a fast Proof-of-Work smart-contract network, secured by miners rather than a company database or a single sequencer

so, sure, Trade Zone is another launchpad

but the interesting part is not the launchpad mechanic

it is the chance to participate early in the feedback loop between Quai applications, Quai-native assets, and the future energy based economy

so the launchpad is not the innovation

the emerging Proof-of-Work economy around it is

text:
seeing a lot of #subnet capitulation on my timeline. some things to consider: 

1) trading mechanics

like it or not, subnets are both 1) highly-correlated to bittensor:native and 2) higher-beta than TAO.

alt season has already started. capital rotation from ZEC=>TAO is just getting under way. 

it makes *no sense*, in my opinion, to sell #subnets when we are on the doorstep of a massive run-up in TAO price. subnet prices (as measured by Sum of Subnets, or SoS) may lag initially vs. TAO...but at the apex of the oncoming TAO bull run, subnets will *wildly* outperform the base currency as traders/investors move out on the risk curve for higher returns once TAO has already moved violently higher.  

don't overthink it. if you wait for exposure, it will be too late. 

2) diversification

if you are selling subnets, I have a suggestion for you: perhaps your problem is not subnet exposure, but trade timeline (you are too short-term focused). stop flipping in and out of subnets with short-term trades, trying to multiple your TAO overnight. it will backfire, and you will lose: you will rotate back into TAO at local lows with tail tucked between legs. 

instead, seek to gain broad exposure to subnets (SoS). you can do this either by 1) staking to root and letting your subnet basket compound while not risking your core TAO position (essentially risk-free!), or 2) through a white-glove service like @TrustedStake that will allow you to gain broad diversified exposure to high-quality subnets without having to worry about 1) daily moves in price or 2) the mechanics of constantly rebalancing. 

*diversification* is the key many are missing. you (probably) wouldn't take your entire 401k and put it into one stock. so don't take a large % of your TAO stack and dump it into low-liquidity, high-beta subnets. all subnets are still experimental, and will have VC-like returns (higher rate of failure, but *massive* outperformance for those that succeed). the key is surviving and (unemotionally) waiting for the successes.

3) compound interest

also; remember the power of compound interest. many subnets are earning 40%+ APY; so if you approach subnet investing with a long-term mindset, it will be *very* hard to lose money over time.

good luck and Godspeed.

Sometimes feels like people don’t give @arthur0x the credit he deserves.

He rose to fame as cocky VC wunderkid affiliated with 3AC but the untold story is how he managed to survive and thrive after being likely the single individual fucked over the most by 3AC. Working alongside with him through it gave me insane appreciation for his character and grit and I’m happy to call him my friend. 

For people that don’t know the lore, when 3AC blew up, the liquidators came after @DeFianceCapital’s assets even though DeFiance never benefited from or even knew about any of that leverage.

Due to shitty legal structuring, his position was actually pretty bad and most of the lawyers we consulted told us we had a <10% chance of winning. 

Almost all of Arthur’s net worth was in that fund and he wasn’t allowed to use those funds to pay legal fees. Most LPs didn’t want to contribute. Bro was just selling any asset he had that was somewhat liquid (his NFTs, his car etc) to keep fighting against the estate’s unlimited money (some of which was literally his).

I recall an incident where a lawyer told him about how bad his chances were. This mf, under the stress of potentially losing everything, smiles and dropped one of the coldest lines ever. 

“Look at the name of my fund.”

Another time, when I was driving him home from a meeting with our lawyers I had a serious chat with him. I said “Bro as a friend, do you want to start thinking about asset protection? Cover your downside.”

He told me no. I pressed that he might lose everything, that the liquidators might try to squeeze him personally for more.

“If I lose everything I’ll just start again from zero.”

We even had someone suggest given we custodied the disputed assets that Arthur just fuck off to Taiwan with the money to force the liquidators to settle with him rather than stay in Singapore bc it’s harder to enforce overseas. 

He refused bc he didn’t believe he should run when he’s in the right “even though I like Taiwan”.

Eventually we navigated it together towards a settlement that although was incredibly unfair on the facts (tbh anything less than 100% felt unfair), still provided far more recovery than our lawyers (and even his LPs) expected.

You really see people’s true character when the chips are down and Arthur has a force of will and self-conviction I’ve never seen in anyone else before.

What Homura is: our own 30B model, open weights, Apache-2.0. It is trained to call tools, not to chat 11 of them, in a strict JSON protocol, over a Solana-native surface: fresh launches, trader PnL, LP pools, cross-chain yield. 

Append a tool it has never seen at inference and it still calls it correctly. The whole fine-tune cost $12.10 on 560 hand-written examples.

Homura was 119,776 downloads on @huggingface the GGUF so far, and we publish the arithmetic with it: much of that is LM Studio and Ollama range-probing rather than people. Read it as reach, not as users.

What is new today: Homura is also for sale. We rent one A40 and serve it on @UsePodAI, so anyone can buy inference from the same model they can download for free.

Both sides of one market:

→ we buy frontier inference over x402, paid from the user's own wallet
→ we sell our own model back into the same marketplace
→ $0.15 in / $0.45 out per 1M tokens
→ 1 of 1 providers serving homura-30b

text:
hold coupons, earn pons.

$COUPONS went live on robinhood chain a few days ago. 3% tax on every buy and sell, 100% of it swapped to $PONS and paid out to holders. no creator cut, no skim. hold 10,000+ coupons and you get paid.

i think it's the first reflection token on hood chain that pays out rewards in pons. 

why pons?

robinhood chain had a huge initial surge and has cooled off over the last month, but vlad and team have shown they clearly care about this chain succeeding, and they're very smart operators. 

pons is the premier launchpad on the chain and the metrics speak for themselves. if you're going to collect rewards, why not collect them in the asset with a real shot at multi billions on a new chain backed by robinhood?

the stonk/knots comparison:

stonk is the sol launchpad and knots is the reflection token that pays holders in it. i have a lot of respect for stonk and what they've built. 

but there was a gap in the market. pons should have a "knots" too. by the stonk/knots ratio, that's roughly 10% of pons market cap. coupons is at $1M right now. interesting upside potential...

and the upside here is arguably better than knots. 20% of coupons supply is already burned and 5% is locked, and none of it earns rewards, so every payout is split across fewer coins. that means holders get a much bigger cut of every payout. 

the teams plan is to keep burning tokens as mcap hits milestones, up to 50%. at 50% burned, every coupon gets DOUBLE the slice it would in a token with nothing burned. knots and zcat don't have that (i hold a lot of both of those and love them too).

i think that's an important point to restate. this is a rewards token on steroids. 

payouts go out every few hours, whenever enough pons has pooled up in the dividend wallet. every one is a plain pons transfer you can watch on chain.

one more thing:

coupons isn't fully tradable on fomo yet. they're working on integrating evm tax tokens on their backend. 

i think that's bullish. the friction means the people buying right now actually want to be here, and they're buying while even though there is extra friction. when fomo integration lands and it's fully tradable there, i'd expect the floodgates to open.

can buy on any dex right now: uniswap, metamask, phantom, etc

Strategy CEO：目标是成为比特币领域的摩根大通

据 Bitcoin Magazine 披露，Strategy 首席执行官 Phong Le 表示，公司的目标并非成为一家单纯的比特币控股公司，而是成为“比特币领域的摩根大通”——通过创造产品、构建市场并为数字资产经济提供流动性，服务一个他认为最终可能覆盖 80 亿人的经济体。

Phong Le 介绍称，Strategy 的数字信贷生态系统规模目前约为 150 亿美元，建立在 STRC 之上的 DeFi 协议所构建的收益与代币化产品，比 Strategy 自身推出的产品更为重要。他还谈及公司选择回购而非提高 STRC 股息的原因，以及经历压力期后对数字信贷业务的思考。

在比特币策略上，Strategy 采取长期积累与灵活性并重的双向路线，将比特币视为资产负债表上接近现金的条目。Le 还回应了 MSCI 指数相关问题，称公司正基于原则反对被排除在外，并透露 AI 工具已嵌入 Strategy 软件与比特币业务的各个环节。

補充一下公募策略,以及為什麼看好

去掉技術不談 ,單純從博弈角度來看公售賠率

前幾輪融資狀況：

Series B (2025/06): 融資 $57M，估值1B。

Series A (2024/03): 融資 $73M，估值約在 300M -400M 之間。

Seed/Pre-seed: 約融資 $8M。

還沒算公售的12%拍賣 , 大概還能拿個50M以上!!

這樣項目方手上有多少錢？

估計約 1.5 -2 億美金。這足以支撐其數年的研發與強力的市場維護（拉盤與生態激勵）。
-----------------------------------------------

公售結構 (12% 供應量)：

社區銷售 (2%)： 針對 OG NFT 持有者，價格固定在 $0.005（底價）。

主拍賣 (8%)： 1/21–1/24 進行密封投標荷蘭式拍賣，無解鎖期（100% TGE）。但大家成本相同!

售後階段 (2%)： 1/27–2/2 以拍賣清算價出售給錯過拍賣的散戶。(這應該是為了製造Fomo)

-------------------------------------------------------
公售策略:

假設公售出價 400M - 700M FDV，從博弈角度來看有以下角度:

優勢:
 一級/二級倒掛空間： 由於 Series B 估值已經是 1B，若能在 400M - 700M 標到，相當於以 40-70% 的價格拿到了B輪籌碼。(但比A輪略高)

拉盤能力評估：  Zama 手握 1.5 億美金現金，且本次公售僅釋放 12% 左右的流動籌碼。他們「絕對有錢」拉盤。

在 TGE 初期，團隊有強大的財務動機與實力維持價格在高於公售價格。

劣勢:
劣勢在於2% NFT OG 籌碼的拋壓

由於2% 的總供應量（約 2.2 億顆 ZAMA）分配給了 5,500 個 OG NFT 持有者。這些人的認購價僅為 $0.005 (55M FDV)。若公售價格落在 500M FDV，這群人的帳面獲利就是 10 倍，鐵定砸的!!
2% 的總量看似不大，但在流動性初期（公售釋放僅 12%）佔比顯著。

資金部署：資金分兩筆,一筆打公售(但不要BID太高400-800m),考慮到 Zama 手頭有 1.5 億美金的現金儲備，他們有足夠的彈藥在二級市場接回這 2% 的籌碼來完成換手。

另一筆則是如果開盤因為這 2% 的拋售導致價格跌破公售價，才用以加倉。

總結
Zama 的流通盤除了2% OG NFT外, 非常「乾淨」。大家成本相同,主要的博弈對手盤是那群拿了 2% 獎勵的社群 OG。以及市場是否有買盤!!
只要能接住這波壓力，項目方是有動機拉盤的!

text:
Some days on the Hyperliquid calendar should never be treated like normal days.

Because behind all these numbers is a pretty unusual story.

Jeff Yan grew up in Redwood Shores, in a family that wasn’t particularly wealthy compared with the people around him.

His parents divorced when he was in third grade. His mother worked overtime as an accountant.

Nobody pushed him toward some grand career.

Then, in eighth grade, a friend took him to a math competition. I think he got obsessed.

The following summer, he woke up at 5am, downloaded old competition papers, and solved them alone in his room. No tutor. No summer program.
Nobody telling him to do it.

Just something he genuinely wanted to get better at.

A few years later, he was on the US Physics Olympiad team.

Then came a gold medal at the International Physics Olympiad, ranking 24th in the world.

Fast forward to today.

That same obsession produced Hyperliquid. With 11 people.

$900M+ in 2025 profit, according to the Colossus profile.

$4T+ in cumulative trading volume.

And a company that was valued at roughly $10B in value without taking VC funding. 

But this is the part I find more interesting.

Hyperliquid now has its own calendar of moments worth remembering.

Nov 29, 2024. 310M HYPE. 31% of the total supply. Distributed to more than 90,000 early users. No private investor allocation. 

Feb 18, 2025. HyperEVM went live.

Apr 21, 2025. The validator set became fully permissionless.

Oct 13, 2025. HIP-3 went live.

And now we’re watching HYPE become something much bigger than the token that launched that November morning.

These are the days I want to remember.
The days when something changed.

should i surface this?

did their intent change?
should this ui adapt?

this basically adds a new computational programming primitive for ~free.

text:
Drug discovery used to run on years of physical lab work.

Ben Pouladian @benitoz says that timeline is now weeks.

Host Ronan Chambers brought up Pouladian's own essay calling the lab the next AI inflection point. Pouladian pointed to Ture Therapeutics, a Los Angeles biotech he's tracked for five years, sequencing billions of molecules and feeding the results into AI models. Work that used to take years of physical lab time compresses into weeks, generating data that otherwise wouldn't exist. Host Luke Knight agreed live that this beats the current chatbot wave.

The AI story with the longest runway isn't the one generating text. It's the one generating lab data nobody could produce fast enough before.

Source: BEP Research - https://t.co/Sq9JADXC4f
author: benitoz
quoted_text:
Running your own AI infrastructure isn't really an infrastructure decision.

It's a data decision, Ben Pouladian @benitoz says.

Hosts Luke Knight and Ronan Chambers pressed him on where frontier labs' economics hold up now that NVIDIA owns Hugging Face. Pouladian's framing: rent a frontier model like Opus for the hard problems, and let it orchestrate cheaper open models like Nemotron or Qwen for the routine work you already own. The reason to own that layer isn't the hardware bill. It's that the data stays on your own system instead of training the model company selling it back to you.

The infrastructure spend isn't really about hardware. It's about which vendor doesn't get to train on your data and use it against you later.

Source: BEP Research - https://t.co/Sq9JADXC4f

I look at those two "filmmakers" and their film, NAZA. Absolute lies from beginning to end.

My country was the one torn apart on October 7. But it did not begin there. For decades, we Israelis have been targets of Islamist terrorists and extremists in Gaza and around the world.

Let me ask you something. Have you ever imagined seeing your friend beheaded? Your children bleeding to death? Your grandmother burning to death? What other extremist ideology has produced this much terror, this much evil?

For three years, I have lived with the atrocities of October 7. I put my life aside to create a record that could never be erased or forgotten. I went to sleep with these images every night, crying out to the world: Do not forget.

I have seen things I cannot even write about. I have watched atrocities that words cannot describe. Here in Israel, we have respect for the dead. We have never wanted to publish images of the bodies of those who were murdered. Their families do not deserve to live with those images forever.

If the full footage were released, many people would be psychologically harmed by images the human mind cannot process.

We never wanted war with Gaza. Lebanon did not interest us either. For years, we begged our government to end the constant attacks - decades of rockets and incendiary kites while we remained trapped in a disastrous policy of restraint that helped bring October 7 to our doorstep.

What would you do if a terrorist wearing a green headband broke into your home, abducted your wife and children, dragged them into a dark tunnel, starved them, and murdered them with his own hands? What if your neighbors were murdered in their beds? If your daughters were raped? What would you do?

Again and again, we watched a world driven by antisemitism blame us and turn the predator into the victim. We watched you threaten us, isolate us, condemn us.

We buried our dead and stood up again. Together. United. We fought back. We rose from the ashes and took back our skies. We lost soldiers. We lost our sons. In a war we never asked for.

We watched people celebrate the massacre against us and hit "like" on photos of our kidnapped children. And now we have watched people from within our own society sell their souls for money and sell us out for applause - the same kind of applause heard in Khan Younis when a crowd cheered as members of the Bibas family were returned in coffins.

We survived that cursed day. We stood up again. We fought on every front. Thousands of terrorists were eliminated. The IDF paid a devastating price while taking measures intended to avoid harming civilians. Had we not been stopped again and again, we would have continued to act against the Islamic regime - the head of the octopus behind so much of our suffering.

Many of us also fight on the information front, as platforms blur our evidence and silence us while Iranian agents and bots distort the truth.

Many of you know me through my documentation of October 7. The stories and testimonies will continue to be told. We will not surrender to pressure or vested interests. Deep down, you know the truth.

September 11, October 7, January 8, and the atrocities in Sweida - we have seen the bodies, the blood, and the horror. We know what murderous Islamist jihadists are capable of. And still, they receive applause from comfortable seats in Venice and elsewhere around the world. You have always looked away from our losses, just as the world now looks away while innocent Iranians are executed day after day.

Make no mistake. We are the ones condemning you. And in the name of every victim whose suffering you chose to ignore, we will never forgive you.

There is only one truth. You will never erase it. We never asked for war. But when war comes knocking at our door, we will be the ones who win.

This is me in 2023, looking at what they had done to us, realizing my life had changed forever.

Yeah look, agents trading real accounts through an MCP server is the part most brokers are still writing memos about. Fair play.

Your own help page is honest about the limit though. The agent can trade, it can't transfer, stake or lend. So it sits in cash between trades earning zero, and the human still has to go do the yield part by hand.

That gap gets louder when gas stops being free and people start asking what the balance is doing on the days it isn't trading.

We've had this chain scoped for a while. 

Licensed yield-bearing RWAs, ERC-4626, already live across EVM chains, so for us it's more like a deployment and not a build. Agent holds the share token, earns while it waits, trades out when it wants to.

You asked to hear from builders. We're past the memo stage too.

AI agents reviewed Letters of Credit and supporting trade documents, while the resulting receivables were issued as programmable, permissioned onchain assets with compliance controls embedded directly into the infrastructure.

But trade finance is only one part of the story.

Injective is now also an SEC-registered transfer agent, becoming the first layer 1 blockchain to combine native RWA infrastructure with the regulated recordkeeping capabilities required by U.S. capital markets.

This infrastructure has now helped bring over $1 billion in real estate mortgages to Injective, further expanding the network’s footprint across real-world assets.

To date, Injective has brought a growing range of assets onchain, including:

The goal is much larger than tokenizing individual assets.

text:
Jev might genuinely be an “Internet moment” for AI.

TypeSafe reports up to 193x faster and 444x cheaper performance in tests with Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.

@0xCodila just wrote a great 10-page article explaining what Jev is, how to use it, and where its 100x advantage comes from.

Here are the 10 steps:

1 → LLMs create. Agents act. Jev decides the next move.

2 → Turn agent forks into three primitives: Choice, Score and probability.

3 → Build with OpenAI, Anthropic or xAI first, then swap Jev in without rebuilding the graph.

4 → Start with shared state, parallel decisions, risk thresholds and an execution queue.

5 → Batch decisions instead of making them sequentially. In one test, 13 questions were 10x faster and 12.2x cheaper.

6 → Put Jev at bounded forks: agent, model, tool, browser action or human escalation.

7 → Benchmark the whole loop, not just individual model calls.

8 → Rank wide, read narrow: shortlist first, then spend compute on what matters.

9 → Reuse the same system: State → Questions → Action → Verify.

10 → Keep Jev out of math, writing and irreversible execution. Code computes, LLMs create, Jev decides.

The result:

A slow, expensive agent loop becomes a much faster decision system that can route, score and escalate in milliseconds.

text:
Brooke you've gotten a lot of snarky replies and this won't be one of them. This will be from the heart. 

My wife was 29 when we met. I was 25. She went to two Ivy's and was working in venture with a lot of savings and a high income. I went to a city university and was living with my mom while working as a consultant at EY. I was also in credit card debt because I used all my paychecks for the down payment for the small apartment we lived in. 

We had almost no mutual friends and didn't hang in the same circles. If we didn't meet randomly at a book signing, we would have never gotten together. I got her number, asked her on a date the next day, and we went out the day after that. We've been together since. Moved in after two months. Got engaged the next year, married the year after, bought a home the following year, and had our first of three boys the next year. 

If either of us put our "non-negotiable" list together, I don't think we would have ever ended up together. 

You are going about it wrong. Theres really no such thing as non negotiables except for extreme cases such as alcoholism, drug addiction, etc. 

You should just try to find someone that you love spending time with and that you think would be a great life partner. 

Since I met my wife Ive become healthier and more masculine, more of a protector and provider, not quite post economic but certainly very successful, and so on. She didn't get the finished product on day 1 and neither will you. 

Your mindset and approach will not get you what you want. I recommend being more open and realizing that it's really only a few things that matter - how well you get along, how easily you can resolve conflicts, and wanting to raise kids in a similar way. Everything else doesn't really matter.

quoted_text:
A mother and her three young children were trapped inside an upside-down SUV that was filling with water in a Florida canal.

One of the little boys was banging on the door, screaming that his mom’s head was underwater.

That’s when Casey Curtis heard the cries and ran toward the canal. He reached the submerged SUV and started pulling the children out one by one, getting all three to safety.

But their mother was still inside.

Casey went back to the vehicle and found her unconscious, still buckled into her seat with her head underwater. He lifted her face above the water, realized she wasn’t breathing and gave her a breath right there in the canal.

She started breathing again.

The mother spent several days in intensive care, but she survived. All three of her children survived too.

Those kids watched a stranger pull them from a sinking SUV, then turn around and go back into the water for their mom when she couldn’t save herself. Casey Curtis is the kind of person people should know about.

author: retserofer
quoted_text:
🚨 OBAMA ON AI: "If we are thinking about AI just in terms of how do we cure cancer or get better energy, you can do that without having agentic AI and having it just roaming free in the internet. The reason you are doing that is because you have to market a product that people will pay money for.

That’s a misalignment between what our society needs and the commercial imperatives that these companies are facing, not because necessarily they’re trying to do bad things, but because they’ve got to justify these valuations.

So, that’s one more reason why it is really important for us to have a competent government and a serious bipartisan conversation around this issue, and we have to do it fast. And I would encourage voters to pay attention to this. If somebody does not have a serious plan for how to deal with this, then they’re not meeting the moment, and you should probably look for somebody else."

text:
What AI founders are asking for isn’t “control” or “governance.”

It’s a liability waiver dressed up as safety.

AI doesn’t only raise the top. It hands leverage to people who never had power, capital, or institutional access — people the old gatekeepers never had to compete with. Founders see that. So the pitch becomes: slow us down, regulate us, “align” us — and shield us when someone uses the tool in ways we can’t police.

Real safety engineering is fine. A campaign that freezes U.S. capability while labs lobby for immunity from downstream users is something else.

Don’t kneecap the country so a few founders sleep better in court. Build the tech. Own the lead. Write clear rules for abuse without handing them a blank waiver.

Capability first. Liability theater second.

The dollar was on one side of 89.2% of global FX trades. 

Foreign investors still hold enormous amounts of U.S. assets. The principal stablecoins are dollar-denominated. Treasury buybacks are about adding liquidity and managing the maturity structure, not somehow controlling a $30T+ market.

Median household income in 2025: $87,460 — a record.
Official poverty rate: 10.2% — a historic low.
Atlanta Fed GDP forecast: 5.1% annualized real GDP growth in Q3.

And that’s before looking under the hood at the private-sector momentum behind capex and the AI buildout.

The latest numbers show continued employment growth, while business investment and capital expenditures have been expanding, as the CapEx comeback story has continued to broaden out, with nearly 20% more equipment investment in Q2 2026 than at the end of Biden’s term.

Databricks' @alighodsi says "Right now the existential risk is close to zero." Why he thinks the public doom talk is irresponsible:

"Leaders have responsibility to not freak people out unnecessarily unless there's really, really good reason."

"Talking about these kind of existential risks and scenarios where all of humanity's gonna be wiped out, I think is irresponsible. It can tip a lot of people over, and it can cause a lot of mental health issues."

"If there is an actual reason for it, that's a different story. But I think that right now the existential risk is close to zero. So why freak everybody out? It's not actually needed. There are risks. We'll get into it. That's probably where we disagree."

"First and foremost, I think leaders should not freak everyone out."

"If there's technical nuances in how we're doing AI research, researchers can discuss that. You don't need to every time go on TV and blast on Twitter to millions of people that 'I think there's like this 10% risk that all humanity is gonna be wiped out.'"

author: martin_casado
quoted_text:
Databricks' @alighodsi on AI risk and adoption:

Ali isn't losing sleep over the existential risk debate.

He says a number of conditions would all have to be true simultaneously to enable an actual runaway takeoff scenario, and currently several opposite conditions exist.

Each frontier training run requires significantly more resources. Power, GPUs, engineers - and some attempts fail, burning up huge piles of money with them. Until that reverses, he doesn't see the self-improving loop happening.

Cyber is what he's watching most closely and where he anticipates real impact. Most orgs are not equipped for the coming change in agentic capabilities. The time between a vulnerability being published and being weaponized has collapsed from years to hours.

On adoption, he believes most companies don't need a smarter model. The models are already smart enough. The gap is context they don't absorb - the things an employee who's worked at a company for five years learned by osmosis.

If the frontier stopped advancing today, he thinks it wouldn't meaningfully change the value most are extracting from AI anyway.

text:
The most interesting part of @DeriveXYZ V3 has very little to do with people trading directly on Derive.

It’s about distribution.

Hyperliquid already showed what can happen when an exchange becomes infrastructure for other apps:

• Wallets like Phantom and Rabby own the frontend and the user relationship.
• Hyperliquid provides the trading infrastructure.
• The apps get paid for bringing the flow.

And I think this is one of the more interesting ways to think about Derive V3.

Derive doesn’t necessarily need every future options trader to become a direct Derive user either. It can become the options engine running underneath other products.

Derive already has Builder Codes, so apps can route trades through Derive and monetize the activity they generate.

V3 then makes that integration layer much more powerful by exposing the infrastructure builders need to create their own options products and UX.

Imagine a wallet showing: “Protect my ETH from falling below $3,000.” The user doesn’t need to know they’re buying a put.

Or a yield app showing: “Earn yield while being willing to sell ETH at $6,000.”

Underneath, it can package an options strategy.

This matters because options have a huge UX problem. Strikes, expiries, implied volatility, Greeks, strategy combinations.

Most users don’t want to learn all of that. But maybe the answer isn’t teaching everyone how to use an options chain, it’s hiding the options chain completely.

Let builders turn complex options positions into simple products users already understand:
• Protection
• Yield
• Directional bets
• Structured payoffs

And let Derive handle the liquidity, execution and risk engine underneath.

Hyperliquid proved the builder distribution model can work for perps. Derive now has a chance to test what that same model looks like for onchain options.

text:
Glassnode：比特币两年上涨 28%，山寨币中位市值下跌 74%

据 Glassnode 与 Bybit 联合发布的报告显示，过去两年间比特币累计上涨 28%，而中位市值山寨币平均下跌 74%，以太坊则基本持平。报告将这一分化视为本轮市场周期的标志性特征，与以往资本随市场成熟从比特币轮动至小币种的“山寨季”模式形成鲜明反差。

杠杆分布同样呈现集中化趋势。报告指出，比特币期货未平仓合约规模约占其市值的 2%，而 PEPE 等投机性小币种的这一比例接近 24%，风险泡沫正聚集在市场最危险的角落。数据截至 8 月 23 日结算收盘，且 Glassnode 覆盖的交易平台有限，相关数字仅反映其追踪的场所。

机构资金流向也明显偏向比特币。现货比特币 ETF 累计净流入约 552 亿美元，远超以太坊 ETF 的约 131 亿美元，后者近期还出现连续多日净流出。本周早些时候，美联储发布鸽派预测后比特币重新站上 8 万美元，带动加密总市值单日上涨 4.6% 至约 2.85 万亿美元，Solana、NEAR、Uniswap 等币种当日涨幅更大。

Pare Stocks（$PARE）：Robinhood 链原生协议，已支持 AAPL、SPY、QQQ 等标的拆分（拆分费 10 bps，收益赎回费 5%），YT 收益源于发行人披露的股息参数。

2️⃣信贷与结构化收益（Lending & Structured Products）
赋予股票代币抵押借贷与票据化属性，提高资金利用率。
Morpho（$MORPHO）：隔离市场借贷协议，可针对单只股票代币精细化配置风险参数（抵押率、清算线），极为适合建立独立股票借贷池。
Gage（$GAGE）：Robinhood 链点对点固定成本借贷，支持以代币化股票或 Meme 作抵押借出 USDG。主打“到期不还清算资产而非强制平仓”模式。
Note Systems（$NOTE）：Robinhood 链结构化票据协议，将股票代币包装成“带障碍价格、自动赎回”的票息产品（如年化票息与下跌保护结构）。

3️⃣多链流量出口 DEX（EVM & Non-EVM）
股票代币交易热潮将向 Ethereum/Robinhood 链之外的生态辐射：
PancakeSwap（$CAKE）：BSC 生态的绝对 DEX 龙头，承接 BSC 链上的股票代币交易流量。
Raydium（$RAY）：Solana 生态核心 AMM，高弹性标的，若 Solana 出现股票代币与配对 Meme 发行潮，将最直接受益。

4️⃣币股 Meme 的爆发行情与两条新路径
传统币股 Meme（如结合股票概念的代币）在政策后呈现两条新分化路径：
获得底层公司/创始人积极回应（正向背书）：
SEC 政策赋予了上市公司“交易阻断权”。因此，公司态度至关重要。
正例（BONER）：其正股 Hims & Hers（HIMS）创始人关注了 BONER 官方账号，社区解读为积极信号，支撑其高市值。
反例（MEME）：因 AMC CEO 对 Robinhood 股票代币公开排斥，缺乏长期监管与正统性预期。
链上股权控制权与无主基金会（治理演进）：
https://t.co/tIaRLYPy43（$GSTOCK 等）：BSC 上的新尝试，主张将股票代币放入无主基金会，通过链上多签在链下行使真实股权权利（结合 CZ 提及的 BNC 生态与财库公司概念）。

📒总结与风险提示

短期看点：围绕 收益拆分（Pendle）、抵押借贷（Morpho/Gage）、结构化票据（Note） 和 流量 DEX（Pancake/Raydium） 这四层叙事进行炒作。
长期关键：项目能否真正落地，取决于上市公司是否接受、链下股权/股息权利是否真实对应、资产能否顺畅赎回，以及交易场所是否满足监管的具体条件（TSV）。
风险提示：许多新协议（如 Pare、Gage、Note、https://t.co/tIaRLYPy43）仍处于初创早期，存在未经审计、合规风险高（如对美国用户限制）及市场波动剧烈等不确定性。

quoted_text:
🟡The Mother of all Symbols!
 
A few weeks back, after many iterations of the fractal torus model, I created an algorithmic artwork called Tortoise, made in tandem with AI. As part of the Nameless ( https://t.co/8v0mwbg4L6 ) framework, I had landed on the Hopf fibration as an important structure for defining physical reality. I took an artistic leap after this... overlaying two oppositely rotated Hopf fibre bundles, then repeating the whole structure again and again at the interstices formed by their intersections, to form a fractal torus. This differs from other torus visualisations I've seen, not only in its use of Hopf fibres, but in the fractal arrangement, which produces that "many, many eyes" quality or the "wheels within wheels" quality.

Studying it from different angles, I realised, to my shock, that this structure had many many connections to scientific concepts, myths and symbols across the world and across history:
Science: the black hole and white hole paradigm, wormholes
 Sacred geometry: Flower of Life, Lotus of Life, Triskelion, Yin Yang
 Religious symbols: Sri Yantra on Kurma, Shatkona, Swastika, Tree of Life, Thousand Petalled Lotus, Reclining Vishnu, Samudra Manthan, Shivlingam, Avalokiteshvara, Ezekiel's Wheel, the Celtic Cross,
 Sacred architecture: Muqarnas and Islamic geometric patterns, Rose windows
 Visionary art made in altered states, such as @alexgreycosm 's
 Contemporary design: even the @OpenAI logo

To show how all these might derive from one source, I built a system that varies the parameters of the same root Tortoise artwork until it matches each symbol. Then I made a visualiser where you can click any symbol, read about the connection, and study the match visually.

I'm not claiming these are all derived from this single structure. Each connection is pattern-matched at this stage, and the scientific ones especially are speculative. I claim only the visual match, not an actual connection. But there are too many to ignore. Perhaps what the ancients meditated upon is the same structure science is reaching towards, and the same structure seen in altered states of consciousness. If the universe is sound based, perhaps the wave-structure formed by the primordial sound corresponds to a similar fractal torus structure?

Many of these connections already exist in literature and in esoteric theory. Some were abstract, some pointed directly to a torus, though not, as far as I know, to this particular variation. The visualiser is therefore a synthesis of many people's work over millennia, seen through the lens of my own. I'm assembling it with humility and respect, hoping we notice that we are all telling the same story through different lenses...

I have made 26 connections so far, and I hope to add more. I'm giving equal weight to each tradition, so if you spot flaws or biases in the text or visual, they aren't intentional, and I hope to improve these over time.

Find the artwork “Tortoise” and the visualiser at: https://t.co/isCWdb2K6x

Music credits: Music by DELOSound from Pixabay

quoted_text:
Jev is going to change the prosumer/consumer AI landscape by unlocking a specific thing:

Ad-supported + free AI native apps

this is going to usher in a generation of new AI-native marketplaces, social networks, photo apps, messaging, calendars, email, collab tools, and much more.

Why? Previously, if you wanted to have an AI-native app with multiple/fast LLM calls on every screen, the math just didn’t work - inference costs just couldn’t be paid back from throwing a few video ads or affiliate links. So there were really just two solutions:

1) be a massive company and subsidize AI costs
2) charge a subscription fee to cover inference
(or both)

So what happens when you take a different approach that’s looks to be, initially, >400x cheaper than a more general LLM? I think it means that app developers are going to make their apps smarter and different in interesting ways. It won’t be as generically powerful as LLMs, but instead folks will create highly differentiated point solutions. You may not have a generically powerful virtual admin to schedule all your meetings, but you may have a free/ad-powered assistant that can comb through your inbox, filter for only important emails, figure out important dates, prioritize contacts, and do other interesting 80/20 work. Same for generically powerful virtual companions, or app builders, etc - it may be that we can hybridize the LLM and future Jev-like models that adds “wow” features at 1/1000ths of the cost, to make the economics work.

If folks hear of interesting new apps/interactions/etc built on Jev, I’d love to hear it!

text:
Hey Beni,

Seems like a bunch of wires got crossed here so I just wanted to set the record straight. Your original claim was that Kalshi’s crypto prediction market volume was fake. The chart from Artemis shows prediction market volume share, not perps. We don’t do rebates for crypto prediction markets. Also, the way that contracts <> notional $ is calculated is universal amongst prediction markets and same with poly so it’s apple-to-apples.

Separately on perps you claimed that “Here SCM means market makers that are selected by Kalshi lmfao”. This isn’t true. Anyone can become a Self-Clearing Member of a CFTC regulated exchange as long as they meet the regulatory requirements. “Fair access” is a reg requirement for us.

All exchanges run rebate and incentive programs to help provide better liquidity on the exchange for traders. CME does it. So does Hyperliquid and Binance (in fact they run NEGATIVE market maker rebates).

I’m the first to admit that it’s early days for perps for us given we're building a new product in untrodden territory (US perps). But the core difference between Kalshi and offshore perp exchanges is that while other exchanges run deals in the dark, we need to file our incentive programs publicly and so what you see is truly what you get.

text:
how to setup and use Jev in 10 minutes

from nothing to a call that returns a decision

1. get access

join the waitlist at typesafe, people report getting in within a day

don't want to wait, it's already hosted in two places:
→ vercel ai gateway as typesafe-ai/jev, no waitlist
→ cloudflare workers ai as typesafe/jev

2. install the skill so your agent writes the call correctly

npx skills add typesafe-ai/skills --skill typesafe-ai

on claude code it's two commands:

- claude plugin marketplace add typesafe-ai/skills
- claude plugin install typesafe@typesafe-ai

then in your prompt just say "use the typesafe skill"

3. learn the shape before you write a line

the body is a state and a map of questions. the state is your context, whatever you would have pasted into a prompt. the questions are typed

three types, that's the entire api:

→ Noul returns a raw 0 to 1
→ Choice picks one from up to 255 options you define
→ Score places it on a 2 to 10 level scale

every Choice and Score comes back with a confidence from 0 to 1

4. make the first call a real one

pick a decision already living in your code as an llm call that never writes text. the "which of these" one

how to do it:

- build the option list in your own code, not in the prompt
- send your existing context as the state, unchanged. don't rewrite it yet
- ask your question plus three more you're curious about, they run in parallel against the same state and output tokens are free
- log the answer, the confidence, and what your old call said
- leave the old call running. delete nothing on day one

5. put a limit on it before it touches anything

read confidence on every response, never just the answer

low limit for reading and sorting. 0.85+ for anything you cannot undo. everything under the limit falls through to the old call

that fallback is four lines, and it's the reason you can ship this on a tuesday instead of planning it for q4

the 10 minutes is real. the hour after is the actual work: you, a log of answers and confidences, deciding where your lines go

start in the playground in the console, and paste a real state from your own product, not the sample one

特斯拉这波更新，被总结成「人没开，也帮你躲」。这个说法本身没错，但热闹之外，真正动的是方向盘的归属。

具体说：14.3.9 和 14.3.10 给 HW4 车型加了个功能，叫 Automatic Collision
Evasion。你手动开着车，系统判定正面碰撞迫近，可以自行切入
FSD，转向、制动、加速，替你把这一下躲过去。官方把口子开得很窄，主要在受控高速路上，时速约 85
英里以下。HW3 老车主没有同款，拿到的是 14.2 Lite。

85 英里什么概念？约等于每小时 137 公里。美国高速的法定限速大多在 65 到 80 英里，也就是说，最常见的巡航
场景已经被这个功能盖住了。说形象一点：紧急那几秒里打方向、踩刹车的，可以不再是人。

当然，先泼半盆冷水。触发条件这么窄，日常真用上的概率不高，短期内它更像一个法律样本，而不是卖点。但责任
这件事，过去很清楚：辅助驾驶，手在方向盘上，出事算司机的。现在系统在人没碰方向盘的时刻自己动了手，那这
几秒算谁的？答案会写进产品说明书的措辞里，说明书每改一个字，责任边界就跟着挪一寸。

监管会把「人没开也帮你躲」记成新能力，还是新风险，接下来几个月见分晓。这份判词怎么写，也就决定了这套系
统敢在多少个场景里继续松开人的手。如果你开着 HW4 上过高速，欢迎在留言区说说，你愿不愿意把那几秒交给它

text:
Robinhood has aggressively been pushing for RWAs in the form of onchain tokenized stocks, but why have they been pushing towards that direction?

Firstly, let’s understand what RWAs mean.

RWAs is short for Real World Assets and they are financial assets that exist outside crypto markets but can be represented digitally onchain. E.g stocks, government bonds, real estate, etc

Instead of relying entirely on TradFi systems to record ownership and process transactions, RWAs allow parts of that process to happen on a blockchain. The basic idea is simple, make financial assets easier to access, transfer and use while reducing the friction found in traditional markets.

What’s the market for it and why are they (and many others) betting largely towards this direction?

Zooming out, Robinhood’s vision is about becoming part of the infrastructure through which financial assets are issued, owned, traded, and accessed. This can be understood through three major opportunities ⇨ The size of existing financial assets, The demand for easier access to investments and The potential for onchain-based markets to operate beyond traditional trading hours.

The existing market is already enormous as it is. The US Equity market is in the range of tens of trillions of dollars and just capturing a fraction of this is already hundreds of billions to trillions in value. 

The current state of tokenized stocks is about $3 billion in value and an average $30 billion in monthly volume so there’s clearly a lot of room for growth

Also with the SEC coming up with the Innovation Exemption act, this helps put this vision on the same side as regulators, as they and other similar products get some breathing space to figure out the underlying tech. The SEC exemption specifically permits Venues to use AMMs and LPs for permissioned trading.

This means, Exchanges can use onchain trading systems to match transactions and provide liquidity, rather than relying exclusively on traditional exchange infrastructure.

And speaking further on the tech, Robinhood Chain uses an Ethereum-compatible setup built on Arbitrum Orbit. In simple terms, it combines Ethereum's development environment with infrastructure designed to process transactions on its own network. This gives teams building RWA products a familiar foundation for creating and managing digital assets.

quoted_text:
Ben Horowitz and Erik Torenberg with Nas, Steve Stoute, and Grandmaster Caz on the Paid in Full Foundation

Caz penned rhymes that became Rapper's Delight. Even with his name in them, he got nothing.

The Paid in Full foundation honors the people who created hip-hop by making sure they're "paid in full," financially, spiritually, and culturally.

As Nas points out, money alone reads as a handout. So the grant comes attached to the honor. Each year at the foundation's Hip Hop Grandmaster Awards, pioneers are celebrated by the artists they inspired.

text:
how to setup and use Jev in 10 minutes

from nothing to a call that returns a decision

1. get access

join the waitlist at typesafe, people report getting in within a day

don't want to wait, it's already hosted in two places:
→ vercel ai gateway as typesafe-ai/jev, no waitlist
→ cloudflare workers ai as typesafe/jev

2. install the skill so your agent writes the call correctly

npx skills add typesafe-ai/skills --skill typesafe-ai

on claude code it's two commands:

- claude plugin marketplace add typesafe-ai/skills
- claude plugin install typesafe@typesafe-ai

then in your prompt just say "use the typesafe skill"

3. learn the shape before you write a line

the body is a state and a map of questions. the state is your context, whatever you would have pasted into a prompt. the questions are typed

three types, that's the entire api:

→ Noul returns a raw 0 to 1
→ Choice picks one from up to 255 options you define
→ Score places it on a 2 to 10 level scale

every Choice and Score comes back with a confidence from 0 to 1

4. make the first call a real one

pick a decision already living in your code as an llm call that never writes text. the "which of these" one

how to do it:

- build the option list in your own code, not in the prompt
- send your existing context as the state, unchanged. don't rewrite it yet
- ask your question plus three more you're curious about, they run in parallel against the same state and output tokens are free
- log the answer, the confidence, and what your old call said
- leave the old call running. delete nothing on day one

5. put a limit on it before it touches anything

read confidence on every response, never just the answer

low limit for reading and sorting. 0.85+ for anything you cannot undo. everything under the limit falls through to the old call

that fallback is four lines, and it's the reason you can ship this on a tuesday instead of planning it for q4

the 10 minutes is real. the hour after is the actual work: you, a log of answers and confidences, deciding where your lines go

start in the playground in the console, and paste a real state from your own product, not the sample one

text:
A village once hired a watchman to keep them safe from wolves.

He took the role seriously. Each night, while the rest of the villagers slept, he walked the fence line with a lantern. With time he taught himself to spot what others would overlook: the impressions wolves left in soft soil, the hush of movement in brush, and the shallow stretches of river they often used to cross.

As his skill grew, so did his intensity. What began as careful attention turned into constant searching.

One night he noticed a snapped branch near the fence. “A wolf was here,” he said.

The next night he found no tracks at all. “They’ve learned to hide their tracks,” he said.

Another evening the chickens rustled and complained. “They can smell the wolves.”

When the chickens stayed quiet the following night, his fear didn’t ease - it deepened. “The wolves have learned how to approach without frightening them.”

The villagers pointed out that he hadn’t actually seen a wolf in months and suggested the pack might have moved on. He only shook his head.

“That is exactly what they want us to think.”

From then on, everything became proof to him. Evidence meant wolves.

And so did the absence of evidence.

If a chicken disappeared, it meant wolves.

If a chicken returned, it meant the wolves had released it.

A gap beneath the fence meant wolves had come through.

An unbroken fence meant they’d found another way in.

He stopped sleeping. He started drawing maps, connecting broken branches, footprints, missing tools, odd sounds, and the shifting patterns of birds. Strings began to cover his walls, tying one small incident to the next.

To everyone else, the village felt quiet.

To him, it had never been more dangerous.

Then, one night, he saw two glowing eyes beyond the fence.

“At last,” he whispered.

He raised his bow and let an arrow fly.

By morning the villagers learned what he had hit: and old lantern hanging at the far gate. Two pieces of glass had caught his own light and reflected it back to him.

The old blacksmith bent down, lifted one of the shards, and faced the watchman.

“You were once the best watchman we’ve ever had,” he said.

“I still am,” replied the watchman. “That’s why I see what the rest of you cannot.”

The blacksmith placed the shard in his hand.

“No. Once you searched for wolves.

Now you search for reasons to believe there are wolves.”

The watchman looked into the glass. For the first time in years, the only thing staring back was himself.

Then he finally understood:

A man who doubts everything may believe himself impossible to deceive.

But when every shadow becomes evidence, he no longer needs anyone else to deceive him.

He can do it all by himself.

“People are working 12 to 13 hours a day just to press enter.”

We are turning an entire generation of technical experts around the world into the equivalent of retirees pushing a button in front of casino slot machines. 

This will have lots of long run implications on companies. Most important of which, is that it will make existing moats even more brittle. 

The value of automated software is not making the software faster. 

It is understanding your intention and making the software BETTER. 

Better edge. 
Better design. 
Better alpha. 

But if you don’t slow down and map out your intention, you will just make your shitty code faster. 

We built 8090’s Software Factory to do this: when execution is a costless commodity, what really matters?

Over time, companies will realize that it’s:

1. Intention
2. Governance
3. Verification
4. Evidence

This is what will separate orgs consuming tokens and companies encoding their edge. This generally requires top down leadership from the CEO to the CFO/CIO. 

Bottoms up tool adoption only increases costs and accelerates slot machine behaviors. Essentially the brain rot of doom scrolling social media is coming for your development team…

Good luck to all the players.

author: JosephJacks_
quoted_text:
I said "auto-regressive LLMs, in and of themselves, will not lead human-level AI" 
That statement is still totally true.

First, the reasoning abilities of current AI systems are based non-auto-regressive search (which is what I have always advocated for). But AFAICT, they do it in token space, which is limited and inefficient. I have claimed that human-like reasoning must be a search in continuous representation space. It looks like the industry is moving towards that.

Second, the self-improvement methods, as currently practiced, only work for domains where the quality of outputs can be scored without human intervention, such as mathematics, code, and scenarios that can be simulated accurately. Not anything else. Humans and animals learn new skills way more efficiently than current RL methods.

Third, the multimodal capabilities of current AI assistants generally use separately-trained encoders (that are not LLMs). This is also what I've been advocating. Except that I think the best way to do this is with JEPA trained with self-supervised learning. The research community is clearly moving towards that (3000 papers on JEPA in just 4 years).

Fourth, if LLMs were a path to human-level AI, we would have domestic robots and Level-4 or Level-5 self-driving cars for consumers by now. And we don't. We certainly don't have cars that can learn to drive in 20 hours or practice like any teenager. We're still missing something pretty huge to claim human-level intelligence (let alone superhuman).

Sure, we now have computer systems that are impressive, very useful, and whose performance is superhuman in an increasing number of domains (coding being one of them). 
But that's true of the entire history of progress in computer technology. 

Lastly, there is a basic confusion about what intelligence actually is.
It is not the mere accumulation and regurgitation of existing declarative knowledge (which is essentially what LLMs do).
As Jean Piaget famously said, "intelligence is not what you know, it is what you do when you don't know." 
It is your ability to solve new problem without any prior training, to act in previously-unknown scenarios, and to adapt very quickly to new situations with minimal training.

We're still far from that.

quoted_text:
Sometimes feels like people don’t give @arthur0x the credit he deserves.

He rose to fame as cocky VC wunderkid affiliated with 3AC but the untold story is how he managed to survive and thrive after being likely the single individual fucked over the most by 3AC. Working alongside with him through it gave me insane appreciation for his character and grit and I’m happy to call him my friend. 

For people that don’t know the lore, when 3AC blew up, the liquidators came after @DeFianceCapital’s assets even though DeFiance never benefited from or even knew about any of that leverage.

Due to shitty legal structuring, his position was actually pretty bad and most of the lawyers we consulted told us we had a <10% chance of winning. 

Almost all of Arthur’s net worth was in that fund and he wasn’t allowed to use those funds to pay legal fees. Most LPs didn’t want to contribute. Bro was just selling any asset he had that was somewhat liquid (his NFTs, his car etc) to keep fighting against the estate’s unlimited money (some of which was literally his).

I recall an incident where a lawyer told him about how bad his chances were. This mf, under the stress of potentially losing everything, smiles and dropped one of the coldest lines ever. 

“Look at the name of my fund.”

Another time, when I was driving him home from a meeting with our lawyers I had a serious chat with him. I said “Bro as a friend, do you want to start thinking about asset protection? Cover your downside.”

He told me no. I pressed that he might lose everything, that the liquidators might try to squeeze him personally for more.

“If I lose everything I’ll just start again from zero.”

We even had someone suggest given we custodied the disputed assets that Arthur just fuck off to Taiwan with the money to force the liquidators to settle with him rather than stay in Singapore bc it’s harder to enforce overseas. 

He refused bc he didn’t believe he should run when he’s in the right “even though I like Taiwan”.

Eventually we navigated it together towards a settlement that although was incredibly unfair on the facts (tbh anything less than 100% felt unfair), still provided far more recovery than our lawyers (and even his LPs) expected.

You really see people’s true character when the chips are down and Arthur has a force of will and self-conviction I’ve never seen in anyone else before. 

Tiger is right - Eye of the Tiger could literally be his theme music lmao.

quoted_text:
My month-long California vacation is over. I spent most of it on my yacht—but I also stayed in a number of motels.

Yes. Motels. Cheap motels.

I normally stay at Hiltons. The first week of my vacation, I did. Then I woke up sweating in the middle of the night because of lousy AC controlled by a gaslighting thermostat (post below), took a weak shower, and discovered I’d paid $35 a night to park at a highway hotel surrounded by acres of empty asphalt.

So I tried an experiment: forget the brand. Prioritize cold AC, hot showers, and good reviews.

My criteria were simple:

Giant AC unit visible in the photos.
Recently remodeled.
No horrifying guest photos.
Rating above 8/10.

In one month, I saved $1,359.

And it’s been glorious.

I did walk into one terrible room. But it cost less than half the Hilton rate, so I ate the charge, walked out, and booked another cheap motel.

Will I do this again next trip? I don’t know.

There are three major drawbacks:

Every motel smells like lemon Lysol.
Most of the lighting has all the warmth of a police interrogation room.
The walls are sometimes approximately three molecules thick.

But I’ll take all three over waking up drenched in sweat, then standing under a low-pressure Hilton shower wondering why I paid 3x for the privilege.

So what did I choose for my last night in California?

The Vagabond Inn in San Luis Obispo.

It’s clean and the AC could preserve a cadaver. The shower has the water pressure of a fire hose.

Five stars. No notes.

Now I just have to explain to my wife why our credit-card statement looks like I spent a month in California having a string of affairs with truck stop barmaids. 💀

author: chamath
quoted_text:
I said "auto-regressive LLMs, in and of themselves, will not lead human-level AI" 
That statement is still totally true.

First, the reasoning abilities of current AI systems are based non-auto-regressive search (which is what I have always advocated for). But AFAICT, they do it in token space, which is limited and inefficient. I have claimed that human-like reasoning must be a search in continuous representation space. It looks like the industry is moving towards that.

Second, the self-improvement methods, as currently practiced, only work for domains where the quality of outputs can be scored without human intervention, such as mathematics, code, and scenarios that can be simulated accurately. Not anything else. Humans and animals learn new skills way more efficiently than current RL methods.

Third, the multimodal capabilities of current AI assistants generally use separately-trained encoders (that are not LLMs). This is also what I've been advocating. Except that I think the best way to do this is with JEPA trained with self-supervised learning. The research community is clearly moving towards that (3000 papers on JEPA in just 4 years).

Fourth, if LLMs were a path to human-level AI, we would have domestic robots and Level-4 or Level-5 self-driving cars for consumers by now. And we don't. We certainly don't have cars that can learn to drive in 20 hours or practice like any teenager. We're still missing something pretty huge to claim human-level intelligence (let alone superhuman).

Sure, we now have computer systems that are impressive, very useful, and whose performance is superhuman in an increasing number of domains (coding being one of them). 
But that's true of the entire history of progress in computer technology. 

Lastly, there is a basic confusion about what intelligence actually is.
It is not the mere accumulation and regurgitation of existing declarative knowledge (which is essentially what LLMs do).
As Jean Piaget famously said, "intelligence is not what you know, it is what you do when you don't know." 
It is your ability to solve new problem without any prior training, to act in previously-unknown scenarios, and to adapt very quickly to new situations with minimal training.

We're still far from that.

Introducing Sherpa: the most advanced fiction writing AI

We accelerated from $250M in ARR to $500M because Sherpa helped increase content production by 1200% in 1 year

Sherpa was trained on 5.5B hours of playtime with minute by minute dynamic retention data.

550K+ creators have produced 2.6M hours of content annualised using it

Pocket FM is like Netflix for audio-only dramas, with our own pool of one-person studios.

10% of eligible writers on Pocket FM make >$200K
One blockbuster produced >$100M in revenue
3 writers have become millionaires in <2 yrs

We built Sherpa to enable anyone to make >$1M by writing world-class fiction stories:

1. The Idea: Drop a 1-2 sentence concept. Sherpa interrogates it like a veteran editor on tension, stakes, and psychology
2. World & Characters: It builds out the complete lore, tone, and character psychologies
3. Sub-Plot planning: Breaks the premise into arcs, arcs into episodes, and episodes into scenes
4. Scene-by-Scene Generation: Outlines and drafts entire episodes, with you able to steer, rewrite, or override anytime
5. Editorial Review: Stress-tests every draft for pacing, engagement drop-offs, prose, and coherence before it locks
6. One-Tap Production: Pick a voice, convert to audio drama, and publish directly to Pocket FM’s millions of listeners
7. Global Scale & Monetization: Revenue-share on performance, with automatic localization so you earn across international markets

Test Sherpa for free here: https://t.co/R39M5o0Miz
_____________________________________________

Generic LLMs fail at serialized fiction because they lack a long-horizon narrative reward function.

Sherpa solves this through three core technical leaps:

1. Narrative World Model (State Tracking & Retrieval): Context windows degrade over long runs. Sherpa constructs an evolving semantic knowledge graph tracking character states, secrets, and plot dependencies. High-speed retrieval surfaces exact context on demand, maintaining zero continuity decay across hundreds of episodes

2. Hierarchical Story Planner: When writing a 500-episode story like Naruto, you need to plan 100s of sub plots. Rather than generating linearly, Sherpa decomposes narrative across discrete levels: season -> arc -> sequence -> episode -> scene.

Rather than generating everything upfront, like a generic LLM, Sherpa uses progressive planning and dynamic replanning. As the story evolves, it identifies what changed, traces the downstream impact, and replans only the affected parts.

3. Prose Engine (Trained on series' retention data): LLMs write robotically, but serial fiction needs emotion, tension, pacing, and dialogue that sounds like real people.

Sherpa's Prose Engine was designed specifically for storytelling. It was built on 1B+ tokens of Pocket's own stories, trained by learning from what listeners engage with, where they drop off, and what keeps them hooked.

Feedback is taken from specialized evaluator models that measure every scene against a 40-item checklist. (Evaluator models were benchmarked against human reviewers and matched them 80–90% of the time.)
_______________________________________________

Owning distribution and creation puts us in a very unique spot.
More shows -> More data -> Sherpa becomes better -> more creator success -> more creators -> more shows

Pocket FM has already seen one $100M IP. I believe Sherpa will soon lead to dozens of single-person studios creating billion-dollar shows.

Most people are scared of AI but I think it'll unlock more human creativity, help creators earn more, and bring the next great IPs to life. This will create millions of jobs and new income streams.

quoted_text:
Ben Horowitz and Erik Torenberg with Nas, Steve Stoute, and Grandmaster Caz on the Paid in Full Foundation

Caz penned rhymes that became Rapper's Delight. Even with his name in them, he got nothing.

The Paid in Full foundation honors the people who created hip-hop by making sure they're "paid in full," financially, spiritually, and culturally.

As Nas points out, money alone reads as a handout. So the grant comes attached to the honor. Each year at the foundation's Hip Hop Grandmaster Awards, pioneers are celebrated by the artists they inspired.

Caz ultimately received a five-year grant, bought a house, and left the projects. In his words: "The thing is the honor. The thing is putting you in the light that you deserve to be in."

Ben says he bought Paid in Full (the album) for $10 and got at least $5 million worth of value out of the record, with no way to pay it back.

The vision is paying the debt. Felicia Horowitz runs the foundation. She and Ben are matching donations 2.5 to 1, and every dollar goes to the artists.

9月19日夜到20日凌晨，乌军对莫斯科州发动大规模无人机与导弹打击。莫斯科市长称这是开战以来最大规模对首都方向的袭击，并承认炼油厂设施受损；州政府通报至少2人死亡、约20人受伤。

泽连斯基随后确认命中莫斯科炼油厂和物流目标。俄方称24小时拦截1600多架无人机，其中约450架飞向莫斯科——拦截数字无法独立核实，但炼油厂起火、仓库被打，有现场画面和官方承认。

节奏不是昨晚才变的。真正拐点在2025年末到2026年春：前线推进大幅放缓，战争重心转到互相打能源和后勤。战争研究所（ISW）9月19日评估：俄方宣称2026年占领5300多平方公里，但可核实控制大约148平方公里；同期乌军收复约973平方公里。

3月以来俄军净推进接近停滞。能源侧更清楚——国际能源署数据显示，俄炼油加工量6月掉到每天380万桶，创20多年来新低，比上年同期低约三成。莫斯科卡波特尼亚炼油厂6月就遭重创，当时已传出要修到2027年，这次是再打一记。

外交没跟上。美方特使来回穿梭，一度传出互不打能源、互不打首都，但打击很快恢复。双方都说愿意谈，核心条件没变：俄要领土和政治让步，乌不接受。泽连斯基已公开判断，战事大概率拖进冬天。

现在看局势，别盯“谁赢了一晚”，盯两件事就够：前线推进是不是继续接近零，俄乌炼油和电力还能撑几个冬天。消耗战一旦成型，比谁先喊停，更看家底。

text:
I introduced appliance reservations in our house to save money. By Saturday, my son owned breakfast.

I'm the father of 2 children and, until recently, the person who decided when the toaster was available.

We were trying to move some electricity use out of the busiest hours. I made a shared calendar so the washing machine, oven, and dryer wouldn't all run at once.

My wife asked if we could just remember.

I said remembering was how we'd got here.

I gave everyone equal booking rights. I wanted the children to learn responsibility.

At 7:15 the next morning, I put bread in the toaster.

My son showed me his reservation.

7:00 to 8:00. Recurring. Weekdays.

He wasn't eating toast. He was still in bed. He'd sent his sister to enforce it.

I asked what she was getting out of this.

Hair dryer. Saturday. Exclusive use.

I told him unused reservations would be canceled.

He came downstairs, toasted half a bagel, and went back to bed. His sister photographed the bagel beside that day's newspaper.

We don't get a newspaper. They'd printed the front page.

On my printer slot.

I added a rule against booking equipment you didn't intend to use.

My daughter booked the oven for a cake.

I asked what kind.

She said she was still accepting proposals.

By dinner, my wife had offered her £5 to include a tray of potatoes. I said this was rewarding the wrong behavior.

My wife said the potatoes were in at 6:30 and I was welcome to join them.

I called a family meeting.

My son asked whether attendance was compulsory. I said yes.

He booked the washing machine for the same time, then explained he couldn't attend because I'd taught him not to leave wet clothes sitting.

I moved the meeting.

At 2:10 a.m., I found him making pizza.

I asked why he was awake.

He pointed to my calendar. I'd marked the overnight period green and written "PREFERRED."

He had also done a wash. It contained 1 sock. The sock was on top of the pizza box, drying.

I deleted the calendar.

Nobody argued.

At 7:30, my wife asked why the washing machine was full of wet towels. My daughter needed the oven. My son had promised a toaster slot to a friend who was now standing in our kitchen holding a crumpet.

The friend asked whether his booking would be honored.

I restored the calendar from backup.

Then I created an administrator slot from 7:20 to 7:40 every morning. Nobody else can edit it.

My son called that unfair.

I told him ownership carries responsibilities he would understand when he was older.

I've also reserved the dishwasher for Father's Day.

I don't know what I want yet. I'm accepting proposals.

text:
Stocks are becoming more sensitive to sharp moves in the Treasury market:

The 30-day correlation between the ICE BofA MOVE Index and the S&P 500 is up to -0.58, its highest since mid-June.

The MOVE index, also called the "VIX of bonds," measures the yield volatility of 2Y, 5Y 10Y, and 30Y Treasuries.

This means rapid increases in bond volatility are now translating into larger declines in stock prices.

A similar phenomenon took place in March this year and in April 2025, when violent moves in the MOVE Index exacerbated market selloffs.

The index has now surged +8.0% over the last week, to 80.7 points, near its highest level since mid-May.

Bond volatility is again becoming a key driver of stocks.

text:
“People are working 12 to 13 hours a day just to press enter.”

We are turning an entire generation of technical experts around the world into the equivalent of retirees pushing a button in front of casino slot machines. 

Essentially the brain rot of doom scrolling social media is coming for your development team…

This will have lots of long run implications on companies. Most important of which, is that it will make existing moats even more brittle. 

The value of automated software is not making the software faster. 

It is understanding your intention and making the software BETTER. 

Better edge. 
Better design. 
Better alpha. 

But if you don’t slow down and map out your intention, you will just make your shitty code faster. 

We built 8090’s Software Factory to do this: when execution is a costless commodity, what really matters?

Over time, companies will realize that it’s:

1. Intention
2. Governance
3. Verification
4. Evidence

This is what will separate orgs consuming tokens and companies encoding their edge. This generally requires top down leadership from the CEO to the CFO/CIO. 

Bottoms up tool adoption only increases costs and accelerates slot machine behaviors.

Good luck to all the players.

quoted_text: I am done with this shit. It is over. The state of engineering right now is horrible. It has been half a month since I started a new role at a big company. Nobody knows anything here. The specs, code, tests, PRDs, tickets, resolution of those tickets, reports, etc., everything is made by Claude Code. Nobody on my team likes this. They are being forced to ship as much as they can. I have heard multiple times from higher management that pushing code is not a bottleneck, so why are we slow? People are working 12 to 13 hours a day just to press enter. Nobody is reading anything. Humans in corporate are doing nothing on their own. Everyone, literally everyone, from an L1 to an L7 engineer here is doing the same thing. Talk to Claude. There is no sense of victory. Nobody is resolving bugs. In reality, nobody is thinking anymore. Everything is done by LLMs. It is so soul-sucking. I would not mind it, to be honest, if we were at least given the time to check out the code and see what is going where. But no, the goal is to just ship. No matter what happens.

Tokenized equities today are exactly where stablecoins were in 2019.

the first pmf is here. bringing equities onchain is just as obvious, simple, yet genius as bringing dollars onchain was back then. we've already seen the first growth spurt push us to the first few billion in onchain supply.

but zoom out and it's painfully obvious we're still incredibly early. an easy 100x in growth still ahead over the next few years.

here's where it gets interesting though:

stablecoin growth was slower, because we spent years operating in a completely different environment. one that mocked crypto, treated it with deep skepticism, and forced us to fight regulatory headwinds the whole way. one of the biggest catalysts, the GENIUS Act, only came last year, many years after the first pmf, and accelerated stablecoin significantly.

tokenized equities are positioned completely differently.

there's already massive institutional interest and adoption, and tokenized equities are an obvious, compelling fit for exactly that crowd. and just days ago the SEC issued its Innovation Exemption, explicitly allowing tokenized stocks to trade onchain, actively pushing this development forward instead of fighting it.

so I think tokenized equities are equally obvious with equally asymmetric upside as stablecoins in 2019. except this time it's going to move much, much faster.

one of the biggest opportunities forming in this space right now.

Jev now does the same as general typed Choice/Score over any state/options (interacting probs + confidence), plus evals/routing: 70-500 ms, $0.042/M tokens (~$0.0001/call), 40-200× faster/cheaper than LLMs.

Tradeoff: Matrix zero-cost specialized open precursor; Jev broader calibrated production leader.

text:
I know humility is important, but what I didn't know is what it means. I thought it is submissiveness

This is unf so true for many Indian girls. 

Thankfully, over time, by learning from a lot of amazing people around, especially my husband, I've learned what humility really is. 

To me, it's self assurance with an innate power to not slip into comparisons and futile judgements

By futile judgements, I mean, judging to feel better about oneself or to feel victim when the other person is "better"

Judgements are not inherently bad. Contrast futile judgement with constructive judgement: 
- Empathy for someone who has served bad cards, and
- the lens of analysis to see what one can learn from somebody who is in a "better" position 

What I now feel humility is, in summary, is unrelenting self-assurance, especially when life kicks you, being brave to show the fierce side of you when someone mistakes your humility for weakness or gullibility, and being constructively judgementle

No life advice, but hey - using X for what it is - sharing one's own thoughts as we all evolve together. thanks for reading 😇
